title: Evaluating a multi-vaccine respiratory immunization strategy involving SARS-CoV-2, pneumococcal, and influenza vaccines in adults: A randomized, open-label, multicenter, controlled, non-inferiority Phase IV trial in China.
abstract: Co-administration of vaccines targeting multiple respiratory pathogens may enhance coverage and streamline adult immunization programs. We conducted a randomized, multicentre, open-label Phase IV trial registered at Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR2100046227) in China to evaluate the immunogenicity and safety of co-administering an inactivated SARS-CoV-2 vaccine (WIBP-CorV) with the 23-valent pneumococcal polysaccharide vaccine (PPV23) and a quadrivalent inactivated influenza vaccine (IIV4). A total of 1,404 adults aged ≥ 18 year, including equal numbers of adults aged 18-59 year and ≥60 year, were randomized 1:1:1 to receive WIBP-CorV + PPV23 on Day 0 followed by WIBP-CorV + IIV4 on Day 28, WIBP-CorV alone on Days 0 and 28, or PPV23 on Day 0 followed by IIV4 on Day 28. Co-administration preserved humoral immune responses across vaccine platforms. Non-inferiority in geometric mean titers or concentrations was demonstrated for SARS-CoV-2 neutralizing antibodies and pneumococcal serotype-specific IgG responses. Seroconversion rates were non-inferior to those following separate administration for all pneumococcal serotypes, though results were less consistent for SARS-CoV-2 (after the second dose) and influenza A(H1N1). Age-stratified analyses showed age- and strain-specific non-inferiority findings that should be interpreted cautiously. Co-administration demonstrated an acceptable safety profile, with only slightly higher rates of mild, transient local reactions and no vaccine-related serious adverse events (SAEs). These findings support the feasibility of co-administering WIBP-CorV with PPV23 and IIV4 while maintaining immunogenicity and safety in adults represented in this study. Trial registration The study was registered in the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR) under registration number ChiCTR2100046227.

analysis.summary_en: This Phase IV randomized, open-label, multicenter trial evaluated the immunogenicity and safety of co-administering an inactivated SARS-CoV-2 vaccine (WIBP-CorV) with pneumococcal (PPV23) and influenza (IIV4) vaccines in adults. The study included 1,404 participants aged ≥18 years, divided equally into age groups 18-59 and ≥60. The main results showed non-inferiority in SARS-CoV-2 neutralizing antibodies and pneumococcal serotype-specific IgG responses, though results for SARS-CoV-2 after the second dose and influenza A(H1N1) were less consistent. The safety profile was acceptable, with only slightly higher rates of mild local reactions and no serious adverse events. The findings suggest that co-administration of these vaccines is feasible in adults, maintaining immunogenicity and safety. However, age- and strain-specific non-inferiority findings require cautious interpretation. The study provides important insights for respiratory immunization strategies in adults, supporting the integration of multiple vaccines.

title: Effectiveness of remdesivir in individuals with confirmed Omicron variant: a systematic review and meta-analysis of cohort studies.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: The emergence of the Omicron variant (B.1.1.529) of SARS-CoV-2 represents a new challenge due to its high transmissibility and potential resistance to existing treatments. While Remdesivir, an FDA-approved antiviral, has been widely used in managing COVID-19 cases, its efficacy against the Omicron variant remains uncertain and warrants further investigation. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluates the effectiveness of remdesivir in individuals infected with the Omicron variant. METHOD: A systematic search of MEDLINE (PubMed), Embase, Cochrane Library, Google Scholar, and ClinicalTrials.gov identified relevant cohort studies. Data extraction and risk of bias assessment followed PRISMA guidelines, with statistical analysis conducted by random-effects model using the RevMan. In addition, subgroup analysis and sensitivity analysis were applied as necessary. RESULTS: Fourteen cohort studies with 964,156 participants were included. Remdesivir significantly reduced all-cause death among hospitalized individuals (OR: 0.70, 95% CI [0.60-0.81]), all-cause hospitalization (OR: 0.27, 95% CI [0.14-0.54]), and COVID-19-related death (OR: 0.13, 95% CI [0.03-0.58]). However, its effect on oxygen supplementation was not significant (OR: 0.52, 95% CI [0.08-3.52]). CONCLUSION: These findings reinforce the role of remdesivir in preventing severe COVID-19 outcomes among patients infected with the Omicron variant. However, this finding should be confirmed by large randomized clinical trials.

title_zh: 瑞德西韦对已确诊的 Omicron 变异个体的有效性:队列研究 研究的系统回顾和荟萃分析。
source_body_en: INTRODUCTION: The emergence of the Omicron variant (B.1.1.529) of SARS-CoV-2 represents a new challenge due to its high transmissibility and potential resistance to existing treatments. While Remdesivir, an FDA-approved antiviral, has been widely used in managing COVID-19 cases, its efficacy against the Omicron variant remains uncertain and warrants further investigation. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluates the effectiveness of remdesivir in individuals infected with the Omicron variant. METHOD: A systematic search of MEDLINE (PubMed), Embase, Cochrane Library, Google Scholar, and ClinicalTrials.gov identified relevant cohort studies. Data extraction and risk of bias assessment followed PRISMA guidelines, with statistical analysis conducted by random-effects model using the RevMan. In addition, subgroup analysis and sensitivity analysis were applied as necessary. RESULTS: Fourteen cohort studies with 964,156 participants were included. Remdesivir significantly reduced all-cause death among hospitalized individuals (OR: 0.70, 95% CI [0.60-0.81]), all-cause hospitalization (OR: 0.27, 95% CI [0.14-0.54]), and COVID-19-related death (OR: 0.13, 95% CI [0.03-0.58]). However, its effect on oxygen supplementation was not significant (OR: 0.52, 95% CI [0.08-3.52]). CONCLUSION: These findings reinforce the role of remdesivir in preventing severe COVID-19 outcomes among patients infected with the Omicron variant. However, this finding should be confirmed by large randomized clinical trials.

title: Clinical effects of third doses of mRNA COVID-19 vaccines among hemodialysis patients: a nationwide retrospective cohort study.
abstract: Background: Evidence on the effectiveness of third-dose messenger RNA (mRNA) coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) vaccination during the Omicron-dominant period in Asian hemodialysis (HD) patients remains limited. We evaluated the clinical effectiveness of a third mRNA vaccine dose against severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infection, hospitalization, and mortality in Korean HD patients. Methods: Using the Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency-National Health Insurance Service database, we conducted a nationwide cohort study of HD patients aged ≥18 years who received two or three doses of BNT162b2 or mRNA-1273 before January 16, 2022. Study outcomes were SARS-CoV-2 infection, hospitalization, and death. Cox proportional hazards models were used to assess the associations between third-dose vaccination and clinical outcomes. Results: Among 66,389 HD patients (mean age, 65.7 ± 12.9 years; 60.5% male), 55,125 (83.0%) received three vaccine doses and 11,264 (17.0%) received two doses. Receipt of three doses was associated with a significantly lower risk of SARS-CoV-2 infection (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR], 0.58; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.56-0.60). Among 17,886 patients with SARS-CoV-2 infection, third-dose vaccine recipients had a lower risk of hospitalization (aHR, 0.65; 95% CI, 0.62-0.70) and 30-day mortality (aHR, 0.35; 95% CI, 0.30-0.41) compared with those who received two doses. Receipt of mRNA-1273 as the third dose was associated with lower observed risks of infection and hospitalization than receipt of BNT162b2. Conclusion: A third dose of an mRNA COVID-19 vaccine was associated with lower risks of SARS-CoV-2 infection, hospitalization, and mortality among HD patients during the Omicron-dominant period. These findings support the clinical importance of booster vaccination in this high-risk population.
authors: Korean Society of Nephrology Disaster Preparedness and Response Committee

title_zh: Clinical effects of third doses of mRNA COVID-19 vaccines among hemodialysis patients: a nationwide retrospective cohort study.
source_body_en: Background: Evidence on the effectiveness of third-dose messenger RNA (mRNA) coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) vaccination during the Omicron-dominant period in Asian hemodialysis (HD) patients remains limited. Methods: Using the Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency-National Health Insurance Service database, we conducted a nationwide cohort study of HD patients aged ≥18 years who received two or three doses of BNT162b2 or mRNA-1273 before January 16, 2022. Receipt of mRNA-1273 as the third dose was associated with lower observed risks of infection and hospitalization than receipt of BNT162b2. Conclusion: A third dose of an mRNA COVID-19 vaccine was associated with lower risks of SARS-CoV-2 infection, hospitalization, and mortality among HD patients during the Omicron-dominant period. These findings support the clinical importance of booster vaccination in this high-risk population.

title: Exploring booster vaccine hesitancy: evidence from the COVID-19 in Hong Kong.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The COVID-19 pandemic showed that effective pandemic prevention may require repeated vaccination. However, booster uptake can be influenced by psychosocial factors, particularly during a prolonged public health crisis. OBJECTIVE: This study examined factors associated with adults' willingness to receive an additional COVID-19 vaccine dose in Hong Kong. METHODS: Data were drawn from the fourth-wave follow-up survey of a longitudinal study and analyzed cross-sectionally using multinomial logistic regression. RESULTS: A total of 689 participants were analyzed: 401 (58.2%) were willing to receive an additional dose, 130 (18.9%) refused, and 158 (22.9%) were undecided. Relative to being undecided, higher pandemic fatigue (OR = 1.630, 95% CI: 1.256-2.115) and lower trust in authorities (OR = 0.602, 95% CI: 0.471-0.769) were statistically significantly associated with greater odds of refusal, whereas greater perceived convenience of preventive measures was statistically significantly associated with greater odds of acceptance (OR = 1.288, 95% CI: 1.011-1.640). Higher daily hassles were statistically significantly associated with increased odds of both refusal (OR = 1.578, 95% CI: 1.150-2.163) and acceptance (OR = 1.257, 95% CI: 1.005-1.572), indicating a bidirectional relationship, and the association with acceptance held only among those who perceived measures as less convenient. Among demographic factors, only age was significant, with younger participants more likely to remain undecided than older participants. CONCLUSIONS: The findings highlight the role of everyday pandemic experiences in shaping vaccination decisions. Improving the convenience and manageability of preventive measures may help promote booster vaccine uptake in future pandemic contexts.

title: An interpretable machine learning model integrating mucosal and cellular immunity to predict SARS-CoV-2 reinfection: a multicenter cohort study.
abstract: SARS-CoV-2 reinfection remains a significant public health challenge that requires accurate risk assessment across populations. Using prospectively collected data from two independent cohorts, we developed and externally validated an interpretable machine learning model for predicting symptomatic SARS-CoV-2 reinfection. The cohort comprised 1,156 adults from Wuxi and Nantong, China, with a median follow-up duration of 10 months. Reinfection occurred in 128 participants (11.1%). The model integrated eighteen clinical and immune features, and ultimately identified spike-specific nasal secretory immunoglobulin A (sIgA) and spike-specific CD4 + central memory T cells (T CM ) as key predictors. Developed using the extreme gradient boosting (XGB) algorithm, the prediction model achieved an AUC of 0.835 in the internal validation cohort and demonstrated strong discrimination in the external validation cohort. SHAP analysis revealed that higher nasal spike-specific sIgA was associated with lower risk, while spike-specific CD4 + T CM cells exhibited a non-linear association with reinfection. This interpretable immune-based model provides a framework for immune-informed risk stratification, enabling better prediction and management of SARS-CoV-2 reinfection risk in settings with heterogeneous population immunity.

title_zh: 整合粘膜和细胞免疫来预测 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 再感染的可解释机器学习模型:一项多中心 队列研究 研究。
source_body_en: SARS-CoV-2 reinfection remains a significant public health challenge that requires accurate risk assessment across populations. Using prospectively collected data from two independent cohorts, we developed and externally validated an interpretable machine learning model for predicting symptomatic SARS-CoV-2 reinfection. The cohort comprised 1,156 adults from Wuxi and Nantong, China, with a median follow-up duration of 10 months. Reinfection occurred in 128 participants (11.1%). The model integrated eighteen clinical and immune features, and ultimately identified spike-specific nasal secretory immunoglobulin A (sIgA) and spike-specific CD4 + central memory T cells (T CM ) as key predictors. Developed using the extreme gradient boosting (XGB) algorithm, the prediction model achieved an AUC of 0.835 in the internal validation cohort and demonstrated strong discrimination in the external validation cohort. SHAP analysis revealed that higher nasal spike-specific sIgA was associated with lower risk, while spike-specific CD4 + T CM cells exhibited a non-linear association with reinfection. This interpretable immune-based model provides a framework for immune-informed risk stratification, enabling better prediction and management of SARS-CoV-2 reinfection risk in settings with heterogeneous population immunity.
abstract_zh: 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 再感染仍然是一项重大的公共卫生挑战,需要对人群进行准确的风险评估。使用从两个独立的 队列研究 前瞻性收集的数据,我们开发并外部验证了一个可解释的机器学习模型,用于预测有症状的 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 再感染。队列研究 包括来自中国无锡和南通的 1,156 名成年人,中位随访时间为 10 个月。128 名参与者(11.1%)发生再感染。该模型整合了 18 个临床和免疫特征,最终确定了尖峰特异性鼻分泌性免疫球蛋白 A (sIgA) 和尖峰特异性 CD4+ 中央记忆 T 细胞 (T CM ) 作为关键预测因子。该预测模型使用极限梯度提升(XGB)算法开发,在内部验证队列研究中实现了0.835的AUC,并在外部验证队列研究中表现出很强的辨别力。SHAP 分析显示,较高的鼻尖峰特异性 sIgA 与较低的风险相关,而尖峰特异性 CD4 + T CM 细胞与再感染呈非线性相关。这种可解释的基于免疫的模型为免疫知情风险分层提供了一个框架,能够在具有异质群体免疫的环境中更好地预测和管理 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 再感染风险。

title: [Dynamics of behavioral factors and attitudes toward vaccination in moscow during the COVID-19 pandemic: from the acute phase to adaptation].
abstract: BACKGROUND: The transition of the COVID-19 pandemic from the acute phase to adaptation was accompanied by changes in preventive behavior, institutional trust, emotional state and attitudes toward vaccination. OBJECTIVE: To analyze the dynamics of awareness, preventive behavior, trust, emotional state and attitudes toward vaccination among Moscow residents in 2021 compared with 2020. MATERIALS AND METHODS: The survey tool was developed by the WHO Regional Office for Europe with support from the University of Erfurt and adapted to the Moscow context. CATI was conducted using a stratified dual-frame sample. The article analyzes the 4th and 5th survey waves: February 2021 (n = 1038) and July-August 2021 (n = 998). RESULTS: By the 5th wave, adherence to most preventive measures decreased, especially social distancing, limiting contacts and using hand sanitizers. The proportion not wearing gloves increased sharply after the requirement was lifted. The mean self-assessment of emotional state decreased to 3.47 points; institutional assessments declined and vaccination attitudes became more polarized. CONCLUSIONS: Public health strategies should combine consistent scientific communication, targeted work with vaccine-hesitant groups and horizontal trust.

source_body_en: BACKGROUND: The transition of the COVID-19 pandemic from the acute phase to adaptation was accompanied by changes in preventive behavior, institutional trust, emotional state and attitudes toward vaccination. OBJECTIVE: To analyze the dynamics of awareness, preventive behavior, trust, emotional state and attitudes toward vaccination among Moscow residents in 2021 compared with 2020. MATERIALS AND METHODS: The survey tool was developed by the WHO Regional Office for Europe with support from the University of Erfurt and adapted to the Moscow context. CATI was conducted using a stratified dual-frame sample. The article analyzes the 4th and 5th survey waves: February 2021 (n = 1038) and July-August 2021 (n = 998). RESULTS: By the 5th wave, adherence to most preventive measures decreased, especially social distancing, limiting contacts and using hand sanitizers. The proportion not wearing gloves increased sharply after the requirement was lifted. The mean self-assessment of emotional state decreased to 3.47 points; institutional assessments declined and vaccination attitudes became more polarized. CONCLUSIONS: Public health strategies should combine consistent scientific communication, targeted work with vaccine-hesitant groups and horizontal trust.

title: Immunogenicity and Safety of PHH-1V COVID-19 Vaccine as a Heterologous Booster in Adolescents.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: PHH-1V, a protein-based, non-mRNA, bivalent, adjuvanted COVID-19 vaccine, has demonstrated strong immunogenicity and favorable safety as a booster in adults. This study evaluated PHH-1V as a heterologous booster in adolescents. METHODS: HIPRA-HH-3 was a phase IIb, open-label, multicenter, noninferiority trial assessing the immunogenicity and safety of PHH-1V in 240 healthy adolescents (≥ 12 to < 18 years) primed with BNT162b2. Immunogenicity (N = 90) was assessed by measuring neutralizing antibodies against SARS-CoV-2 variants and total binding antibodies in adolescent participants vs young adults (≥ 18 to ≤ 25 years) (N = 81) from a previous trial, who had also been boosted with PHH-1V. T-cell responses at day 14 post booster were also evaluated. Antibody durability and adverse events (AEs) were assessed through day 336. RESULTS: Neutralizing titers-against Omicron BA.1 (primary endpoint), WH1, Beta, and Delta variants-and total binding antibodies were significantly higher in adolescents than in young adults (P < .001), demonstrating noninferiority (margin < 1.5). T-cell responses against BA.1 and Beta also increased significantly (P < .001). Cross-variant antibody titers remained above baseline (day 0) through day 336. AEs were mostly mild/moderate, primarily injection-site pain and headache within 28 days. No related serious AEs were reported. CONCLUSIONS: As a heterologous booster in adolescents, PHH-1V is safe and elicits cellular and sustained humoral responses with cross-variant immune recognition, which support the use of PHH-1V in adolescent vaccination strategies. Data in younger and specific risk groups are still needed.

title_zh: Immunogenicity and Safety of PHH-1V COVID-19 Vaccine as a Heterologous Booster in Adolescents.
source_body_en: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: PHH-1V, a protein-based, non-mRNA, bivalent, adjuvanted COVID-19 vaccine, has demonstrated strong immunogenicity and favorable safety as a booster in adults. This study evaluated PHH-1V as a heterologous booster in adolescents. METHODS: HIPRA-HH-3 was a phase IIb, open-label, multicenter, noninferiority trial assessing the immunogenicity and safety of PHH-1V in 240 healthy adolescents (≥ 12 to < 18 years) primed with BNT162b2. Immunogenicity (N = 90) was assessed by measuring neutralizing antibodies against SARS-CoV-2 variants and total binding antibodies in adolescent participants vs young adults (≥ 18 to ≤ 25 years) (N = 81) from a previous trial, who had also been boosted with PHH-1V. T-cell responses at day 14 post booster were also evaluated. Antibody durability and adverse events (AEs) were assessed through day 336. RESULTS: Neutralizing titers-against Omicron BA.1 (primary endpoint), WH1, Beta, and Delta variants-and total binding antibodies were significantly higher in adolescents than in young adults (P < .001), demonstrating noninferiority (margin < 1.5). T-cell responses against BA.1 and Beta also increased significantly (P < .001). Cross-variant antibody titers remained above baseline (day 0) through day 336. AEs were mostly mild/moderate, primarily injection-site pain and headache within 28 days. No related serious AEs were reported. CONCLUSIONS: As a heterologous booster in adolescents, PHH-1V is safe and elicits cellular and sustained humoral responses with cross-variant immune recognition, which support the use of PHH-1V in adolescent vaccination strategies. Data in younger and specific risk groups are still needed.

title: Pooled intravenous immunoglobulins exhibit broad binding and Fc-mediated activity against diverse SARS-CoV-2 variants.
abstract: ABSTRACT During the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic, caused by the severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), antibody-based therapies such as COVID-19 convalescent plasma (CCP) and monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) emerged rapidly. However, many CCP clinical trials failed to show consistent benefits, and mAbs lost effectiveness as new SARS-CoV-2 variants emerged. These studies consistently indicated that antibody therapies are effective when given very early in disease and in patients with delayed or suppressed immune responses. Intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG), which is pooled IgGs from thousands of donors, has been explored as an additional source of anti-SARS-CoV-2 antibodies to treat acutely ill patients because IVIG was shown to prevent disease and death in animal models against variants even without neutralizing activity. As antibodies can also protect via Fc-mediated activation of innate immune effector functions, in this study, we compared the qualitative and quantitative properties of CCP and IVIG to determine if IVIG might serve as a clinical therapeutic alternative to CCP. We measured SARS-CoV-2 spike (S)- and nucleocapsid (N)- specific antibody-binding titers across variants and evaluated their ability to induce antibody-dependent effector functions. We found that IVIG and CCP had comparable binding and Fc-effector activity against ancestral SARS-CoV-2. Remarkably, IVIG manufactured before the emergence of XBB.1.5, JN.1, KP.2, XEC, and XFG demonstrated strong binding and Fc-effector activity against these newer variants. IMPORTANCE Despite the availabilities of vaccines for SARS-CoV-2 for most individuals, there remain vulnerable populations for which vaccination is ineffective. As the emergence of SARS-CoV-2 variants has rendered many monoclonal antibody therapies ineffective, there remains a need to understand the role of polyclonal antibody therapies for SARS-CoV-2, such as COVID-19 convalescent plasma (CCP) and intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG). While CCP is variable and donor-dependent, IVIG is pooled from thousands of donors with a range of vaccine- and natural infection-derived antibody responses and may represent a consistent source of polyclonal antibodies. We compared high neutralizing antibody titer CCP, previously shown to be associated with reduced time to hospital discharge, with IVIG produced post-2021. We find that IVIG offers expanded antibody binding to SARS-CoV-2 variants, including those that emerged after the IVIG was collected, and enhanced induction of Fc-mediated innate immune effector functions, highlighting the potential utility of IVIG as an adjunct treatment of SARS-CoV-2. CLINICAL TRIALS This study is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov as NCT04524507. This study is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov as NCT04524507.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the effectiveness of intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) as a potential therapeutic alternative to convalescent plasma (CCP) for treating SARS-CoV-2 infections. The research highlights that IVIG, which is pooled from thousands of donors, exhibits broad binding and Fc-mediated activity against diverse SARS-CoV-2 variants, including those that emerged after the IVIG was collected. The study compares IVIG with CCP, emphasizing that IVIG may offer expanded antibody binding and enhanced induction of innate immune effector functions, making it a promising adjunct treatment for SARS-CoV-2. The findings suggest that IVIG could be valuable in populations where vaccination is ineffective or when monoclonal antibodies lose their potency against new variants. The study is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov as NCT04524507. The evidence is based on binding and effector function assessments, and the results indicate that IVIG maintains effectiveness against newer variants, potentially offering a more consistent therapeutic option.

title: Psychological distress among nurses before and after COVID-19 vaccines: A repeated cross-sectional study.
abstract: BackgroundExtensive research conducted during the COVID-19 pandemic has consistently found significant levels of anxiety, perceived stress and depression among healthcare workers, particularly among nurses. Nevertheless, the effect of COVID-19 vaccine availability on the psychological distress of healthcare workforce remains unexplored.ObjectiveTo compare levels of anxiety, perceived stress and depression among Spanish nurses immediately before and after the full COVID-19 vaccination protocol which was conducted in Spain throughout 2021.MethodsWe employed a repeated cross-sectional design recruiting 439 and 410 Spanish registered nurses at the first (pre-vaccination) and second (post-vaccination) timepoints respectively. Data on psychological distress were collected via online surveys using the Perceived Stress Scale (PSS) and the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS).ResultsAfter vaccination nurses showed lower perceived stress and depression with a small effect size, but anxiety was not reduced. The magnitude of these effects was very small. Although in both timepoints psychological distress was higher in women, the initial differences between frontline and non-frontline professionals tended to disappear. Over the period studied, the proportion of nurses receiving psychiatric or psychological care increased from 7.7% to 20.4%, and half of those using psychotropic drugs had started treatment in the preceding year.ConclusionsThe psychological distress of nurses continued being a relevant problem even after COVID-19 vaccines became available. Policymakers and health systems must ensure adequate psychological support for nurses and a supportive work environment to improve their long-term resilience and well-being, regardless of the existence of effective vaccines.

title: Susceptibility of human neural stem cells to SARS-CoV-2: Entry mechanisms and glycocalyx influence
abstract: Previous work demonstrated that ectodermal cells exhibit greater susceptibility to SARS-CoV-2 than endodermal and mesodermal cells, raising concerns about potential vulnerability of the developing nervous system. We hypothesized that neural stem cells (NSCs) derived from human ectoderm are susceptible to SARS-CoV-2. Using pseudotyped viral particles representing both wild-type and Omicron spike variants, we confirmed efficient transduction in NSCs, with Omicron variants preferentially utilizing endocytosis-mediated entry. Inhibition of endocytosis with filipin and OcTMAB significantly reduced viral entry across all spike variants. Low glycosylation levels on NSCs facilitated viral entry, and enzymatic removal of glycosylation increased their susceptibility. Ectodermal infection by SARS-CoV-2 raises serious concern for potential teratogenic effects on the nervous system, possibly causing latent or subclinical anomalies not immediately evident at birth. Therefore, future clinical studies and long-term surveillance of infants and children exposed in utero are necessary to investigate and identify potential neurodevelopmental deficits.

title: Developing a Culturally Tailored COVID-19 Educational Website for Latina and Black/African American Breast Cancer Survivors: Findings from a Community-Engaged Study.
abstract: Introduction The COVID-19 pandemic disproportionately affected Latino and Black/African American communities, exacerbating health disparities and disrupting cancer care. COVID-19 vaccine uptake was limited due to systemic mistrust, safety concerns, and misinformation. Breast cancer survivors undergoing treatment faced additional uncertainty regarding vaccination. This study describes the community-engaged process used to develop a culturally tailored, bilingual COVID-19 educational website for Black/African American and Latina breast cancer survivors. Methods Between January and March 2021, we conducted formative research with two community-based organizations. Eligible participants were Black/African American or Latina breast cancer survivors. Participants completed surveys assessing sociodemographic, clinical characteristics, followed by optional interviews exploring vaccine perceptions and information sources. title: Leveraging Military-Civilian Partnerships in Crisis: A Case Study of the Las Vegas Response to COVID-19.
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic exposed critical vulnerabilities in civilian healthcare surge capacity, highlighting the potential for military-civilian partnerships (MCPs) to augment public health emergency responses. The Las Vegas Military-Civilian Partnership (LV MCP), a unique collaboration, offers a case study of such integration. The objective of this study was to evaluate the impact of the LV MCP, specifically the workload of US Air Force (USAF) pulmonary and critical care medicine (PCCM) physicians, on the Las Vegas civilian healthcare system during the COVID-19 pandemic. This retrospective review analyzed USAF PCCM physician workload data at University Medical Center (UMC) of Southern Nevada from 2019 to 2023. Data included critical care encounters (CPT codes 99291 and 99292) and COVID-19 encounters (ICD-10 coding). Staffing of 5 USAF PCCM physicians was maintained, with 7 individuals rotating. We assessed changes in the volume of critical care and COVID-19-specific encounters managed by USAF PCCM physicians at UMC. Analysis indicated USAF PCCM physicians reported 19,155 encounters between 2019 and 2023. Encounters peaked at 4,648 in 2020, then declined to 3,155 by 2023. From 2019 to 2020, critical care encounters increased by 1,180, from 1,010 to 2,190. In 2020, 846 (38.6%) of the 2,190 critical care encounters were COVID-19-related. The highest workload occurred during 2020 and 2021, aligning with COVID-19 surges. Of the 2,914 COVID-19-related encounters, 1,892 (64.9%) were classified as critical care-reflecting strong response capability and return to baseline operations. The LV MCP is an effective model for military medical support during a protracted public health crisis. Its preexisting, integrated structure enabled a rapid and sustained surge response, significantly increasing critical care capacity in a medically underserved region without requiring ad hoc federal deployments or DSCA. This underscores the value of embedded military-civilian partnerships as a resilient, efficient strategy for future emergency preparedness, advocating comprehensive data collection to inform integrated responses.

title_zh: Leveraging Military-Civilian Partnerships in Crisis: A Case Study of the Las Vegas Response to COVID-19.
source_body_en: The COVID-19 pandemic exposed critical vulnerabilities in civilian healthcare surge capacity, highlighting the potential for military-civilian partnerships (MCPs) to augment public health emergency responses. The Las Vegas Military-Civilian Partnership (LV MCP), a unique collaboration, offers a case study of such integration. The objective of this study was to evaluate the impact of the LV MCP, specifically the workload of US Air Force (USAF) pulmonary and critical care medicine (PCCM) physicians, on the Las Vegas civilian healthcare system during the COVID-19 pandemic. This retrospective review analyzed USAF PCCM physician workload data at University Medical Center (UMC) of Southern Nevada from 2019 to 2023. Data included critical care encounters (CPT codes 99291 and 99292) and COVID-19 encounters (ICD-10 coding). Staffing of 5 USAF PCCM physicians was maintained, with 7 individuals rotating. We assessed changes in the volume of critical care and COVID-19-specific encounters managed by USAF PCCM physicians at UMC. Analysis indicated USAF PCCM physicians reported 19,155 encounters between 2019 and 2023. Encounters peaked at 4,648 in 2020, then declined to 3,155 by 2023. From 2019 to 2020, critical care encounters increased by 1,180, from 1,010 to 2,190. In 2020, 846 (38.6%) of the 2,190 critical care encounters were COVID-19-related. The highest workload occurred during 2020 and 2021, aligning with COVID-19 surges. Of the 2,914 COVID-19-related encounters, 1,892 (64.9%) were classified as critical care-reflecting strong response capability and return to baseline operations. The LV MCP is an effective model for military medical support during a protracted public health crisis. Its preexisting, integrated structure enabled a rapid and sustained surge response, significantly increasing critical care capacity in a medically underserved region without requiring ad hoc federal deployments or DSCA. This underscores the value of embedded military-civilian partnerships as a resilient, efficient strategy for future emergency preparedness, advocating comprehensive data collection to inform integrated responses.

title: Associations with SARS-CoV-2 Positivity Among People in Refugee Settlements
abstract: Introduction: Limited SARS-CoV-2 testing capacity during the early COVID-19 pandemic required approaches to identify individuals at highest risk of infection for prioritized testing. We assessed the association between symptoms and exposures reported at the time of SARS-CoV-2 testing and test positivity among individuals referred for testing through an interactive voice response (IVR) platform in refugee settlements in Uganda. We used Dial-COVID, a multilingual, toll-free interactive voice response (IVR) platform to survey residents of refugee settlements in Uganda regarding COVID-19 symptoms, exposures, and comorbidities. Respondents reporting symptoms or exposures were invited for SARS-CoV-2 testing using nasal or oropharyngeal swab specimens. At the time of testing, an interviewer-administered questionnaire assessed symptoms and exposures occurring within the preceding two weeks. Log-binomial regression was used to identify factors associated with SARS-CoV-2 positivity. Between February 2021 and March 2022, 6,913 of 15,467 Dial-COVID callers (44.7%) completed the IVR survey. Among survey respondents, 5,184 (75.0%) reported at least one symptom or exposure. Of these, 1,361 (26.3%) were invited for testing, and samples were collected from 751 (55.2%) within seven days of survey completion. SARS-CoV-2 test results were available for 741 individuals, of whom 48 tested positive (6.5%). Among symptoms reported at the testing visit, severe muscle pain (risk ratio [RR] 2.08; 95% CI 1.20–3.57) and unusual fatigue (RR 2.34; 95% CI 1.36–4.03) were associated with SARS-CoV-2 positivity in unadjusted analyses. After adjustment for sex, refugee status, hypertension, and diabetes, only unusual fatigue remained independently associated with a positive test result (aRR 2.10, 95% CI 1.20–3.67). Few self-reported symptoms were associated with SARS-CoV-2 positivity, highlighting the challenges of prioritizing testing based on symptoms alone. IVR-based platforms may provide a feasible approach for screening, surveillance, and linkage to testing in resource-constrained humanitarian settings.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on SARS-CoV-2 and its association with symptoms and exposures in refugee settlements in Uganda. The central question is whether symptoms or exposures reported at the time of testing can be used to prioritize testing for SARS-CoV-2 positivity.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review utilized an interactive voice response (IVR) platform called Dial-COVID to collect data from residents of refugee settlements in Uganda. The study design involved surveying individuals about symptoms, exposures, and comorbidities, followed by SARS-CoV-2 testing for those reporting symptoms or exposures. Log-binomial regression was used to analyze the association between reported symptoms/exposures and test positivity.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review found that among symptoms reported at the time of testing, severe muscle pain and unusual fatigue were associated with SARS-CoV-2 positivity in unadjusted analyses. However, after adjusting for sex, refugee status, hypertension, and diabetes, only unusual fatigue remained independently associated with a positive test result. The study highlights the challenges of using symptoms alone to prioritize testing for SARS-CoV-2.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review notes that few self-reported symptoms were associated with SARS-CoV-2 positivity, which raises questions about the effectiveness of symptom-based prioritization for testing. Additionally, the study does not provide information on the performance of the IVR platform in different demographic or geographic contexts.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review suggests that IVR-based platforms may offer a feasible approach for screening, surveillance, and linkage to testing in resource-constrained humanitarian settings. It also implies the need for further research to improve symptom-based prioritization strategies and to evaluate the effectiveness of IVR platforms in diverse populations.

analysis.summary_en: This review examines the association between symptoms and exposures reported at the time of SARS-CoV-2 testing and test positivity among individuals in refugee settlements in Uganda. Using an IVR platform, the study collected data on symptoms, exposures, and comorbidities, then conducted testing for those reporting symptoms or exposures. The findings indicate that while severe muscle pain and unusual fatigue were linked to SARS-CoV-2 positivity in unadjusted analyses, only unusual fatigue remained independently associated after adjusting for key demographic and health factors. The study highlights the limitations of symptom-based testing prioritization and suggests that IVR platforms could be valuable tools for screening and surveillance in resource-limited settings.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该审查重点关注 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 及其与乌干达难民安置点症状和暴露的关联。核心问题是测试时报告的症状或暴露情况是否可用于优先测试 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 阳性。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该审查利用了名为 Dial-COVID 的交互式语音应答 (IVR) 平台来收集乌干达难民安置点居民的数据。研究设计包括调查个人的症状、暴露情况和合并症,然后对报告症状或暴露情况的人进行 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 测试。对数二项式回归用于分析报告的症状/暴露与测试阳性之间的关联。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 审查发现,在测试时报告的症状中,严重的肌肉疼痛和异常疲劳与未经调整的分析中的 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 阳性相关。然而,在调整性别、难民身份、高血压和糖尿病后,只有异常疲劳仍然与阳性检测结果独立相关。该研究强调了仅使用症状来优先检测 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 的挑战。

elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 审查表明,基于 IVR 的平台可以提供一种可行的筛查方法、监测 以及与资源有限的人道主义环境中的测试的联系。它还意味着需要进一步研究以改进基于症状的优先策略并评估 IVR 平台在不同人群中的有效性。

title: Distinct Energetic and Allosteric Mechanisms of SARS-CoV-2 Spike Binding and Virus Neutralization by Site V and CR3022-Site Silent-Face Antibodies: An Integrated Computational Analysis
abstract: Broadly neutralizing antibodies targeting the silent face of the SARS-CoV-2 receptor-binding do-main (RBD) provide essential templates for pan-sarbecovirus therapeutics, yet the precise bio-physical mechanisms dictating their neutralization breadth, energetic propensities, and escape re-silience remain unresolved. By combining all-atom and coarse-grained molecular dynamics, systematic mutational scanning, rigorous MM-GBSA binding free energy analysis, and residue interaction network modeling we delineate the comparative structural, energetic, and allosteric signatures of Site V (CC25.4, CC25.43, CC25.56, 7D6, 6D6 ) and CR3022-site (Group 1: CC25.54, CC84.2, CC84.24) antibodies. We discover that these two classes by engaging spatially opposite faces of the RBD fold produce mutually exclusive energetic hotspot modules. Site V antibodies are anchored along a surface-exposed lateral ridge by residues R355, R357, R466, I468, F464, and K462, whereas CR3022-site antibodies engage a buried β-sheet-core module comprising R408, K378, C379, Y380, F377, and Q414. Remarkably, despite these distinct epitopes, both classes converge on an ultra-conserved paratope tyrosine triad (Y99, Y100, Y49), establishing a universal structural motif for silent-face recognition. Network centrality modeling demonstrates that Site V and CR3022-site antibodies modulate ACE2 receptor interface dynamics via distinct upstream allo-steric pathways that converge on shared RBM-loop relays at Y423, Y396, and F464. Crucially, in CR3022-site antibodies, binding free energy hotspots and allosteric communication hubs coincide directly within the structurally constrained β-sheet core. This enforces a dual-constraint mecha-nism where escape mutations inherently compromise viral fold integrity. Conversely, Site V binding hotspots and allosteric networks are structurally segregated, exposing cryptic allosteric liabilities where mutations at non-contact positions (F456, R509) dynamically rewire network communication to impair neutralization without altering static interface affinity. Furthermore, within-class resilience is governed by epitope architecture: focused antibodies (CC25.56, 6D6, CC25.54) concentrate binding energy into single dominant anchors vulnerable to point mutations, whereas broad antibodies (CC84.2, CC84.24, CC25.4, CC25.43) distribute binding energetics across multi-residue contact networks. These quantitative findings align directly with experimental neutralization data. The structural immutability of the β-sheet-core module provides a mechanistic explanation for why CR3022-site antibodies CC84.2 and CC84.24 retain activity against highly evasive Omicron sublineages BA.2.86 and JN.1. A complete absence of energetic or allosteric hotspots at major Class 1/2 escape loci explains the cross-variant breadth exhibited by both si-lent-face classes. By establishing how silent-face antibodies balance potency, breadth, and resili-ence, this work offers a predictive biophysical framework for tracking viral antigenic drift and designing durable, multi-epitope antibody cocktails.

analysis.methods: The researchers employed all-atom and coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations, systematic mutational scanning, MM-GBSA binding free energy analysis, and residue interaction network modeling to examine the structural, energetic, and allosteric properties of the antibodies.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the mechanisms by which broadly neutralizing antibodies targeting the silent face of the SARS-CoV-2 receptor-binding domain (RBD) achieve their neutralization breadth, energetic propensities, and escape resilience. The study highlights how these antibodies modulate ACE2 receptor dynamics through different allosteric pathways, with implications for tracking antigenic drift and developing durable antibody therapies. title_zh: 位点 V 和 CR3022 位点 Silent-Face 抗体的 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 尖峰结合和病毒中和的独特能量和变构机制:综合计算分析
source_body_en: Broadly neutralizing antibodies targeting the silent face of the SARS-CoV-2 receptor-binding do-main (RBD) provide essential templates for pan-sarbecovirus therapeutics, yet the precise bio-physical mechanisms dictating their neutralization breadth, energetic propensities, and escape re-silience remain unresolved. By combining all-atom and coarse-grained molecular dynamics, systematic mutational scanning, rigorous MM-GBSA binding free energy analysis, and residue interaction network modeling we delineate the comparative structural, energetic, and allosteric signatures of Site V (CC25.4, CC25.43, CC25.56, 7D6, 6D6 ) and CR3022-site (Group 1: CC25.54, CC84.2, CC84.24) antibodies. We discover that these two classes by engaging spatially opposite faces of the RBD fold produce mutually exclusive energetic hotspot modules. Site V antibodies are anchored along a surface-exposed lateral ridge by residues R355, R357, R466, I468, F464, and K462, whereas CR3022-site antibodies engage a buried β-sheet-core module comprising R408, K378, C379, Y380, F377, and Q414. Remarkably, despite these distinct epitopes, both classes converge on an ultra-conserved paratope tyrosine triad (Y99, Y100, Y49), establishing a universal structural motif for silent-face recognition. Network centrality modeling demonstrates that Site V and CR3022-site antibodies modulate ACE2 receptor interface dynamics via distinct upstream allo-steric pathways that converge on shared RBM-loop relays at Y423, Y396, and F464. Crucially, in CR3022-site antibodies, binding free energy hotspots and allosteric communication hubs coincide directly within the structurally constrained β-sheet core. This enforces a dual-constraint mecha-nism where escape mutations inherently compromise viral fold integrity. Conversely, Site V binding hotspots and allosteric networks are structurally segregated, exposing cryptic allosteric liabilities where mutations at non-contact positions (F456, R509) dynamically rewire network communication to impair neutralization without altering static interface affinity. Furthermore, within-class resilience is governed by epitope architecture: focused antibodies (CC25.56, 6D6, CC25.54) concentrate binding energy into single dominant anchors vulnerable to point mutations, whereas broad antibodies (CC84.2, CC84.24, CC25.4, CC25.43) distribute binding energetics across multi-residue contact networks. These quantitative findings align directly with experimental neutralization data. The structural immutability of the β-sheet-core module provides a mechanistic explanation for why CR3022-site antibodies CC84.2 and CC84.24 retain activity against highly evasive Omicron sublineages BA.2.86 and JN.1. A complete absence of energetic or allosteric hotspots at major Class 1/2 escape loci explains the cross-variant breadth exhibited by both si-lent-face classes. By establishing how silent-face antibodies balance potency, breadth, and resili-ence, this work offers a predictive biophysical framework for tracking viral antigenic drift and designing durable, multi-epitope antibody cocktails.
abstract_zh: 针对 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 受体结合域 (RBD) 沉默面的广泛中和抗体为泛沙病毒治疗提供了必要的模板,但决定其中和广度、能量倾向和逃避再沉默的精确生物物理机制仍未解决。通过结合全原子和粗粒度分子动力学、系统突变扫描、严格的 MM-GBSA 结合自由能分析和残基相互作用网络建模,我们描绘了位点 V(CC25.4、CC25.43、CC25.56、7D6、6D6)和 CR3022 位点(第 1 组:CC25.54、CC84.2、 CC84.24) 抗体。我们发现这两类通过接合 RBD 折叠的空间相对面产生相互排斥的能量热点模块。位点 V 抗体通过残基 R355、R357、R466、I468、F464 和 K462 沿表面暴露的侧脊锚定,而 CR3022 位点抗体接合包含 R408、K378、C379、Y380、F377 和 Q414 的埋藏 β 片层核心模块。值得注意的是,尽管有这些不同的表位,但这两个类别都集中在一个超保守的互补位酪氨酸三联体(Y99、Y100、Y49)上,为沉默面部识别建立了通用的结构基序。网络中心性模型表明,位点 V 和 CR3022 位点抗体通过不同的上游变位路径调节 ACE2 受体界面动力学,这些路径汇聚在 Y423、Y396 和 F464 处的共享 RBM 环中继上。至关重要的是,在 CR3022 位点抗体中,结合自由能热点和变构通讯中心直接在结构受限的 β-折叠核心内重合。这强制执行了双重约束机制,其中逃逸 突变 本质上损害了病毒折叠完整性。相反,Site V 结合热点和变构网络在结构上是隔离的,暴露了神秘的变构责任,其中非接触位置(F456、R509)的 突变 动态重新连接网络通信,以在不改变静态界面亲和力的情况下削弱中和作用。此外,类内弹性受表位结构控制:聚焦抗体(CC25.56、6D6、CC25.54)将结合能集中到易受点 突变 影响的单个显性锚定中,而广泛抗体(CC84.2、CC84.24、CC25.4、CC25.43)将结合能量分布在多残基接触网络中。这些定量发现与实验中和数据直接一致。β-片层核心模块的结构不变性为为什么 CR3022 位点抗体 CC84.2 和 CC84.24 保留针对高度规避的 Omicron 亚系 BA.2.86 和 JN.1 的活性提供了机制解释。主要 1/2 类逃逸位点完全不存在能量或变构热点,这解释了两个沉默面孔类所表现出的跨变体广度。通过确定沉默面孔抗体如何平衡效力、广度和弹性,这项工作提供了一个预测性生物物理框架,用于跟踪病毒抗原漂移和设计持久的多表位抗体混合物。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在阐明针对 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 受体结合结构域沉默面的广泛中和抗体的中和广度、能量倾向和逃逸弹性背后的生物物理机制。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究结合了全原子和粗粒度分子动力学、系统突变扫描、MM-GBSA 结合自由能分析和残基相互作用网络模型来分析针对 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 及其变体(包括 Omicron 亚系 BA.2.86 和 JN.1)的位点 V 和 CR3022 位点抗体。
analysis_zh.methods: 研究人员采用全原子和粗粒度分子动力学模拟、系统突变扫描、MM-GBSA 结合自由能分析和残基相互作用网络模型来检查抗体的结构、能量和变构特性。
analysis_zh.main_results: 位点 V 抗体通过残基 R355、R357、R466、I468、F464 和 K462 沿表面暴露的侧脊锚定,而 CR3022 位点抗体接合包含 R408、K378、C379、Y380、F377 和 Q414 的埋藏 β 片层核心模块。这两类都集中在一个超保守的互补位酪氨酸三联体(Y99、Y100、Y49)上。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,V位点和CR3022位点抗体的不同表位导致不同的能量和变构机制,这解释了它们不同的中和广度和逃避弹性。这项研究为理解沉默面孔抗体识别提供了一个新的框架。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现提供了一个预测性生物物理框架,用于跟踪病毒抗原漂移并设计持久的多表位抗体混合物,以保持针对新出现的变异的功效。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究基于计算分析,不包括实验验证,这可能会限制其结论的可信度。然而,结果与实验中和数据一致,支持适度的置信度评估。

title: Exploring Psidium guajava L. Leaf Fractions as a Sustainable Source of Antiviral Compounds for the Inhibition of SARS-CoV-2 Spike–ACE2 Interaction (Wuhan and Omicron) and 3CLpro Activity
abstract: The leaves of Psidium guajava L. (guava) are an underutilized resource containing diverse bioactive metabolites. The present study evaluated the inhibitory potential of P. guajava leaf fractions against two SARS-CoV-2 molecular targets: the Spike RBD–ACE2 interaction of the Wuhan and Omicron BA.1 variants, and 3CLpro enzymatic activity. A methanolic extract was fractionated by vacuum liquid chromatography, and fraction F14 was then separated into subfractions F14A–F14D through the use of Sephadex LH-20. The activity was evaluated using colorimetric Spike RBD–ACE2 binding assays and a fluorometric 3CLpro assay. F14 and its subfractions inhibited the Spike RBD–ACE2 interaction of the Wuhan variant, whereas against Omicron BA.1, all fractions showed IC50 values <1.25 mg mL−1. F14, F14C, and F14D also inhibited 3CLpro, with IC50 values <1.25 mg mL−1. F14D demonstrated the most consistent inhibitory profile across all the three targets and was selected for further characterization by LC–HRMS. The three major constituents were tentatively assigned as a myricetin hexoside, a quercetin hexoside, and a quercetin pentoside. Overall, the results of this study suggest that F14D contains bioactive constituents with potential inhibitory activity against SARS-CoV-2 molecular targets, although further studies are required to determine their antiviral activity.

title_zh: 探索 Psidium guajava L. 叶组分作为 抗病毒药物 化合物的可持续来源,以抑制 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 Spike-ACE2 相互作用(Wuhan 和 Omicron)和 3CLpro 活性
source_body_en: The leaves of Psidium guajava L. (guava) are an underutilized resource containing diverse bioactive metabolites. The present study evaluated the inhibitory potential of P. guajava leaf fractions against two SARS-CoV-2 molecular targets: the Spike RBD–ACE2 interaction of the Wuhan and Omicron BA.1 variants, and 3CLpro enzymatic activity. A methanolic extract was fractionated by vacuum liquid chromatography, and fraction F14 was then separated into subfractions F14A–F14D through the use of Sephadex LH-20. F14 and its subfractions inhibited the Spike RBD–ACE2 interaction of the Wuhan variant, whereas against Omicron BA.1, all fractions showed IC50 values <1.25 mg mL−1. F14, F14C, and F14D also inhibited 3CLpro, with IC50 values <1.25 mg mL−1. F14D demonstrated the most consistent inhibitory profile across all the three targets and was selected for further characterization by LC–HRMS. The three major constituents were tentatively assigned as a myricetin hexoside, a quercetin hexoside, and a quercetin pentoside. Overall, the results of this study suggest that F14D contains bioactive constituents with potential inhibitory activity against SARS-CoV-2 molecular targets, although further studies are required to determine their antiviral activity.
abstract_zh: Psidium guajava L.(番石榴)的叶子是一种未充分利用的资源,含有多种生物活性代谢物。本研究评估了番石榴叶组分对两个 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 分子靶点的抑制潜力:Wuhan 和 Omicron BA.1 变体的 Spike RBD-ACE2 相互作用,以及 3CLpro 酶活性。通过真空液相色谱法对甲醇提取物进行分级,然后通过使用Sephadex LH-20将级分F14分离成亚级分F14A-F14D。使用比色 Spike RBD-ACE2 结合测定和荧光 3CLpro 测定评估活性。F14 及其亚组分抑制武汉变体的 Spike RBD-ACE2 相互作用,而针对 Omicron BA.1,所有组分均显示 IC50 值 <1.25 mg mL−1。F14、F14C 和 F14D 也抑制 3CLpro,IC50 值 <1.25 mg mL−1。F14D 在所有三个靶标中表现出最一致的抑制特性,并被选择通过 LC-HRMS 进行进一步表征。三种主要成分暂定为杨梅素己糖苷、槲皮素己糖苷和槲皮素戊糖苷。总体而言,本研究的结果表明,F14D 含有对 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 分子靶点具有潜在抑制活性的生物活性成分,尽管需要进一步研究来确定其 抗病毒药物 活性。

title: SARS-CoV-2 Seroprevalence and Antibody Dynamics in The Gambia During the Transition from Pandemic to Endemic Circulation - 2022 and 2023.
abstract: OBJECTIVES To understand population-level seroprevalence once SARS-CoV-2 becomes endemic. METHODS We conducted two cross-sectional-sero-surveys (CSS) in three Health and Demographic Surveillance Systems (HDSS) in The Gambia: Farafenni, Basse and Kiang West. Dried blood spots were collected from 3909 participants in CSS1_2022 and 3991 in CSS2_2023, aged ≥1-year. SARS-CoV-2-spike (S-IgG) and nucleocapsid (NCP-IgG) proteins were measured by ELISA in both CSSs, while antibodies to SARS-CoV-2 variants and other respiratory viruses were quantified by multiplex-Luminex in CSS2_2023. Another CSS was conducted in Kiang West (KW survey) 3-months after CSS1_2022 to assess antibody dynamics. Statistical analysis was done using Stata/SE19.5. RESULTS S-IgG seroprevalence increased between CSS1_2022 and CSS2_2023 [88.1% 95%CI (86.3, 89.6) vs. 93.1% (92.0, 94.0), p<0.0001], whereas NCP-IgG seroprevalence declined [72.7% (70.7, 74.7) vs 61.7% (59.3, 63.9), p<0.0001]. S-IgG seroprevalence was higher in vaccinated vs. unvaccinated individuals [CSS1_2022 [aOR = 3.11(1.85, 5.23)] and CSS2_2023 [2.01(1.18, 3.42)]. SARS-CoV-2 variants seroprevalence ranged between 50%-80%, while seroprevalence to other respiratory viruses was more heterogeneous. In the KW survey, S-IgG seroprevalence remained stable compared with CSS1_2022: 89.2% (85.3, 92.3), while NCP-IgG seroprevalence dropped from 73.1% (68.5, 77.3) to 61.2% (53.6, 68.4). CONCLUSION By 2022-2023, SARS-CoV-2 exposure in The Gambia was nearly universal. Still, COVID-19 vaccinated individuals showed highest seroprevalence.

title: The pan-African natural products library compounds oleanolic acid, poinsettifolin B, and rhuschalcone III disrupt SARS-CoV-2 spike-host ACE2 interactions and SARS-CoV-2 replication
abstract: Abstract Natural product (NP)-based chemical libraries are a rich source of antiviral compounds that can serve as the basis for new therapeutic leads to treat viral diseases, particularly for individuals lacking sustained access to existing vaccines and therapeutics. To identify new NP-based candidate inhibitors of SARS-CoV-2 cellular entry and viral replication, we screened the pan-African Natural Products Library (p-ANAPL), a collection of physical pure compounds obtained from African medicinal plants, for NPs that can disrupt the in vitro interaction of the SARS-CoV-2 Spike receptor-binding domain (RBD) with its host ACE2 entry receptor. This screen identified three compounds – oleanolic acid, poinsettifolin B, and rhuschalcone III – which disrupt RBD/ACE2 interactions with half-maximal inhibitory concentrations (IC 50 s) of 0.5–2.4 μM but do not disrupt an unrelated PD-1/PD-L1 host ligand/receptor binding pair. Oleanolic acid and rhuschalcone III, but not poinsettifolin B, additionally inhibited SARS-CoV-2 replication in Vero cells without cytotoxicity at low micromolar concentrations. Computational modelling indicated that all three compounds interact with numerous RBD and ACE2 residues, including a subset conserved across SARS-CoV-2 variants of concern. Taken together, we identify three NPs that selectively interfere with factors involved in SARS-CoV-2 entry and/or viral replication, representing new antiviral leads for COVID-19 management in resource-limited areas.

title: Mental Health Burden and Vulnerability Among Long-Term Care Facility Residents During the COVID-19 Pandemic: A Systematic Review With Exploratory Prevalence Meta-Analysis.
abstract: BackgroundOlder adults in long-term care facilities (LTCFs) faced social and care disruptions during COVID-19, but evidence on mental health burden and vulnerability remains fragmented.ObjectiveTo synthesise evidence on mental health outcomes among LTCF residents during the pandemic and identify resident- and facility-level vulnerability and protective conditions.MethodsMEDLINE, Embase and PsycINFO were searched for English-language peer-reviewed studies published from January 2020 to January 2025. Findings were narratively synthesised, and exploratory random-effects meta-analyses were conducted where at least three studies reported extractable resident-level prevalence.ResultsThirty-two studies were included as follows: 24 quantitative, six qualitative and two mixed-methods. Most reported high prevalence, deterioration, or qualitative evidence of depression, anxiety, loneliness, isolation, or related distress. Pooled prevalence was 55.6% for depression, 51.4% for anxiety and 54.5% for loneliness, with substantial heterogeneity. Vulnerability reflected clinical, social and facility-level factors; consistent staffing, social connection and family communication were potential protective conditions.

Findings were narratively synthesised, and exploratory random-effects meta-analyses were conducted where at least three studies reported extractable resident-level prevalence.ResultsThirty-two studies were included as follows: 24 quantitative, six qualitative and two mixed-methods. Most reported high prevalence, deterioration, or qualitative evidence of depression, anxiety, loneliness, isolation, or related distress. Pooled prevalence was 55.6% for depression, 51.4% for anxiety and 54.5% for loneliness, with substantial heterogeneity. Vulnerability reflected clinical, social and facility-level factors; consistent staffing, social connection and family communication were potential protective conditions.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review with exploratory meta-analysis examines the mental health burden and vulnerability among long-term care facility (LTCF) residents during the COVID-19 pandemic. The review synthesises evidence from 32 studies, including 24 quantitative, six qualitative, and two mixed-methods, published between January 2020 and January 2025. The findings indicate high prevalence and deterioration of mental health outcomes such as depression, anxiety, loneliness, and isolation. Pooled prevalence estimates for these conditions were 55.6%, 51.4%, and 54.5%, respectively, with substantial heterogeneity. The review highlights that vulnerability is influenced by clinical, social, and facility-level factors, and suggests that consistent staffing, social connection, and family communication may serve as protective conditions. The study underscores the need for targeted interventions to address mental health challenges in LTCF residents during pandemics.

title: The Infection and Coinfection of Clinical Aspergillus fumigatus and SARS-CoV-2
abstract: The global emergence of coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) was caused by severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2). The clinical manifestations of COVID-19 in patients range from asymptomatic disease to severe multiorgan dysfunction and even death. Moreover, the growing population of clinically immunodeficient patients and the use of single clinical antifungal agents have gradually increased the incidence of Aspergillus fumigatus infections, the complex clinical manifestations of which are yet to be fully clarified. The mortality rate among COVID-19 patients coinfected with A. fumigatus has risen significantly. Therefore, a comprehensive understanding of the diagnosis and treatment of A. fumigatus infections, SARS-CoV-2 infections, and their coinfections is crucial. In this review, we first provide a comprehensive description of the life cycle of A. fumigatus, together with an in-depth analysis of its characteristics, diagnosis, and treatment strategies for associated diseases. Then, the basic structure of SARS-CoV-2, the evolution of variant strains, and key aspects of its prevention and control are discussed. Finally, the symptoms, diagnosis, and treatment of COVID-19 coinfection with A. fumigatus are summarized. In this paper, we provide methodological references and data to support the clinical prevention and treatment of A. fumigatus and SARS-CoV-2 infections.

Moreover, the growing population of clinically immunodeficient patients and the use of single clinical antifungal agents have gradually increased the incidence of Aspergillus fumigatus infections, the complex clinical manifestations of which are yet to be fully clarified. The mortality rate among COVID-19 patients coinfected with A. fumigatus has risen significantly. Therefore, a comprehensive understanding of the diagnosis and treatment of A. fumigatus infections, SARS-CoV-2 infections, and their coinfections is crucial. In this review, we first provide a comprehensive description of the life cycle of A. fumigatus, together with an in-depth analysis of its characteristics, diagnosis, and treatment strategies for associated diseases. Then, the basic structure of SARS-CoV-2, the evolution of variant strains, and key aspects of its prevention and control are discussed. Finally, the symptoms, diagnosis, and treatment of COVID-19 coinfection with A. fumigatus are summarized. In this paper, we provide methodological references and data to support the clinical prevention and treatment of A. fumigatus and SARS-CoV-2 infections.

title: SARS-CoV-2 infection detection efficiency in Denmark before major vaccine impacts
abstract: Abstract To deal with the COVID-19 pandemic, Denmark implemented an aggressive program aimed at controlling the pandemic which included both testing and contact tracing programs. The large amount of data collected in Denmark on the pandemic and its integrated nature made it possible to investigate the effectiveness of the testing and contact tracing effort. The results of that investigation and a discussion of the effectiveness and limitations of the different control efforts are reported herein, as are lessons learned concerning possible improvements for the future. The analysis is limited to the period from the start of the COVID-19 pandemic in Denmark (late Feb. 2020) into May 2021, at which time the impact of vaccination intervention was already playing a role with ∼25% of the Danish population at least partially vaccinated. From the available data sets we estimate the national Infection Detection Efficiency ( IDE ) starting around July 1, 2020, the time at which the national infection detection program started to be implemented in a more robust form. The results rely on daily COVID-19 hospital admissions, PCR test results, and antibody prevalence values for the Danish population. We find that for the long-term average, the combined Danish national testing and contact tracing program identified on average about 55 to 60% of the infected individuals during the period from Sept. 1, 2020, into early May 2021. However, higher infection detection efficiencies were achieved in localized areas for short time intervals. Our investigations further indicate that the Danish testing and contact tracing program, which was among the most ambitious in the world, could have had a better balance between voluntary probing on the one hand and focused contact tracing and targeted testing on the other hand. As typically implemented, it proved to be largely ineffective in controlling the pandemic. However, in at least one case when it was implemented in an enhanced and focused mode, it was able to bring a large local outbreak that dominated the country’s cases under control. We have compiled a list of lessons learned regarding the use of contact tracing procedures to control potential future pandemics before vaccinations become available.

title: Nationwide survey of testing practices for respiratory viruses in Australia in the post COVID-19 pandemic era.
abstract: Background In the wake of the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic, there have been dramatic changes in the testing protocols for respiratory illness. Laboratory identification of respiratory pathogens causing clinical symptoms has become more important in the post-COVID-19 era, both for epidemiological and clinical reasons. This is particularly the case for respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) where a number of preventatives are at the point of clinical translation. The laboratory diagnosis is one of the critical elements in understanding the disease burden of respiratory pathogens and the effectiveness of preventatives. The aims of this study were to understand current laboratory testing and reporting practices across Australia. Methods We undertook a cross-sectional survey of Australian NATA (National Association of Testing Authorities) accredited laboratories to collect data on patterns of laboratory testing, the methods used and their reporting processes. The survey asked participants to report on testing of respiratory samples for 2022 as well as current respiratory multiplex testing in 2023. Outcomes In total, 45 out of 193 eligible laboratories (23%) completed the online survey. The majority of laboratories were from Victoria and New South Wales (31% and 27%, respectively) and most were hospital-based clinical diagnostic laboratories. Overall, 40% of responding laboratories (18/44) reported that > 80% of all tests in the molecular laboratory in 2023 were respiratory multiplex. Influenza viruses, RSV and SARS-CoV-2 were tested most frequently on respiratory multiplex PCR panels. RSV typing (RSV A or RSV B) was included in under a quarter of panels (9/43; 21%), compared to almost two-thirds for influenza typing (influenza A or influenza B: 29/44; 66%). There was considerable variability in testing platforms used, with thirty-seven laboratories using 87 different platforms (18 unique platforms). GeneXpert® (Cepheid) was the most commonly used platform; with a higher concentration of this instrument in laboratories from the eastern states (New South Wales, Queensland, Victoria). Forty percent of laboratories reported changes to respiratory testing procedures/panels in 2023 compared to the previous year. Laboratories were most likely to report results directly to the referring doctor (96-100%) followed by notifying their jurisdictional Department of Health.

title: Trends before and after legalization and COVID-19 on cannabis use among gay, bisexual, and other men who have sex with men in Montreal, Toronto, and Vancouver, Canada: A prospective cohort study.
abstract: Objectives We examined how cannabis use was affected by the legalization of cannabis in Canada in October 2018 and the COVID-19 pandemic among urban gay, bisexual, and other men who have sex with men (GBM). Methods Sexually active GBM aged ≥ 16 years in Vancouver, Montreal, and Toronto, Canada, were recruited from February 2017 to August 2019. Participants completed surveys every 6-12 months until August 2022. We examined past 6-month (P6M) trends of any cannabis use, frequency of use, and high-risk use measured by the Alcohol, Smoking, and Substance Involvement Screening Test (ASSIST) with observation periods stratified into February 2017-October 2018; November 2018-March 2020; and June 2020-August 2022. We modelled associations between high-risk use (ASSIST scores ≥ 27) using multivariable generalized linear mixed models. Results We analysed data from 950 GBM in Montreal, 258 in Toronto, and 387 in Vancouver. No significant changes in P6M any cannabis use were noted from November 2018 to March 2020 but declines were noted after June 2020 (OR = 0.81; 95% CI 0.66-1.00). There were no significant trends in frequency of consumption in any time period. High-risk cannabis use was not associated with visits from November 2018-March 2020 (AOR = 1.23; 95% CI 0.7-2.13) or after COVID-19 (AOR = 0.66; 95% CI 0.36-1.20) but was associated with AUDIT-C scores ≥ 4 (AOR = 1.69; 95% CI 1.00-2.87); moderate/severe anxiety scores (AOR = 2.94; 95% CI 1.60-5.39), moderate/severe depression scores (AOR = 2.55; 95% CI 1.26-5.17), and diagnoses of depression (AOR = 2.42; 95% CI 1.29-4.57). Conclusion Our study found no changes in the proportion of GBM reporting any cannabis use after legalization and declines after COVID-19. High-risk cannabis use was not associated with study visits after legalization or after COVID-19.

title: SARS-CoV-2 variant-dependent alterations in nasopharyngeal microbiota and host inflammatory response
abstract: ABSTRACT The SARS-CoV-2 pandemic saw multiple outbreaks occur over short periods. This was linked to the virus’s high infectivity and rapid mutation rate, which hindered the development of effective treatments and a comprehensive understanding of COVID-19 pathophysiology. The nasopharyngeal tract, the main entry site of SARS-CoV-2, interacts with angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 receptors via the viral spike glycoprotein, triggering pro-inflammatory responses that affect both tissue integrity and the resident microbiota. Viral infection induces dysbiosis by modulating microbiome diversity. Although distinct variants produce independent symptoms and viral loads, their impact on the nasopharyngeal microbiota and host inflammatory profile remains poorly understood. To address this, we analyzed nasopharyngeal samples from Chilean individuals collected during different phases of the pandemic. The microbiota was characterized by 16S rRNA gene sequencing (V3–V4 region), and cytokine expression was quantified by RT-qPCR. Finally, applied rigorous data processing and machine-learning models, Random Forest and K-Nearest Neighbors, to identify associations between SARS-CoV-2 variants, inflammatory markers, and opportunistic bacterial genera. Our results reveal that SARS-CoV-2 infection is associated with distinct immunomicrobial signatures marked by increased TNF-α expression and the expansion of opportunistic taxa. These variant-dependent alterations indicate that host inflammatory responses and microbial dysbiosis are closely intertwined in the nasopharyngeal environment. This study provides a comprehensive framework integrating microbial and host factors to better understand the mechanisms underlying COVID-19 pathogenesis and highlights the potential of combining microbiome and cytokine profiling with machine-learning approaches to differentiate infection outcomes across viral variants. IMPORTANCE Understanding how SARS-CoV-2 infection alters the upper respiratory microbiota and host immune responses is essential to uncover the mechanisms underlying COVID-19 severity. In this study, we integrate bacterial 16S rRNA sequencing, inflammatory markers, and machine learning to identify key descriptors of infection such as TNF-α, Acinetobacter , Prevotella , and Staphylococcus . These markers define a conserved immunomicrobial signature across viral variants, linking inflammatory activation with microbial dysbiosis in the nasopharyngeal environment. Our findings highlight the value of the correct and robust application of machine learning models and nested cross-validation strategies in high-dimensional (wide) data sets to improve variant discrimination, reveal host–microbe interactions, and support the development of therapeutic strategies for respiratory viral infections.

title: Antibiotic overuse and mortality in patients hospitalised for COVID-19: a global cohort study.
abstract: Background Global antibiotic use during the COVID-19 pandemic and its impact remain unclear. This study analysed antibiotic use, bacterial co-infections, and the association between antibiotic use and in-hospital mortality among patients hospitalised for COVID-19, using a WHO database. Methods We conducted a multicountry cohort study using anonymised patient-level data from The WHO Global Clinical Platform for COVID-19. Data were collected across 64 countries in all six WHO regions between January, 2020, and October, 2023. The study included hospitalised patients of all ages with suspected or confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection. We obtained patient-level data from standardised WHO case report forms completed prospectively or retrospectively and from harmonised national registries, research studies, and hospital databases. Patients without a suspected or confirmed COVID-19 diagnosis or missing information on hospital admission date, antibiotic use, or outcome were excluded from the analysis. Patients were followed up from hospital admission until death, discharge, transfer, or 28 days, whichever occurred first. Follow-up data were collected at hospital discharge or death by the treating facility and entered into the platform. The primary outcome was 28-day in-hospital mortality, and we analysed this outcome using Cox proportional hazards models with a shared frailty term to account for country-level clustering. Findings The median age of the study population was 61·9 years (±21·7), with 198 223 women and 251 990 men with data available on antibiotic use. Of the 592 898 patients enrolled, 451 291 (76·1%) had data on antibiotic use and were included in the descriptive analysis; 122 854 had complete data on empirical treatment type, of whom 47 359 (38·5%) were included in the regression analysis. Among the 451 291 patients with data on antibiotic use, 341 125 (75·6%) received antibiotics, more frequently in severe to critical cases than in mild to moderate cases (80·5% vs 71·6%). Prescribing was highest in the Eastern Mediterranean (83·0%) and African (82·7%) regions and lowest in the Western Pacific region (32·8%), declining in the European region and region of the Americas but increasing in the African region between 2020 and 2022. Treatment was predominantly empirical and involved Watch antibiotics of the WHO Access, Watch, and Reserve classification. Clinically suspected co-infections were reported in 47 050 (7·9%) of the 592 898 patients; among those with positive cultures, 1815 (42·8%) of 4237 had multidrug-resistant bacteria. In the unadjusted analyses, empirical antibiotic use was associated with higher mortality across severity strata. After adjustment for age, sex, comorbidities, and disease severity, empirical antibiotic use remained associated with increased mortality in mild to moderate cases (adjusted hazard ratio 1·80, 95% CI 1·36-2·38) and severe to critical cases (1·16, 1·08-1·24). Interpretation Despite clinically suspected co-infections being reported in only 47 050 (7·9%) of the 592 898 enrolled patients, 341 125 (75·6%) of the 451 291 patients with data on antibiotic use received antibiotic therapy, predominantly broad-spectrum agents. As antibiotic use was not associated with improved clinical outcomes and is known to increase antimicrobial resistance, it should be rationalised through strengthened antimicrobial stewardship and behavioural interventions, particularly during respiratory viral epidemics.

After adjustment for age, sex, comorbidities, and disease severity, empirical antibiotic use remained associated with increased mortality in mild to moderate cases (adjusted hazard ratio 1·80, 95% CI 1·36-2·38) and severe to critical cases (1·16, 1·08-1·24). INTERPRETATION Despite clinically suspected co-infections being reported in only 47 050 (7·9%) of the 592 898 enrolled patients, 341 125 (75·6%) of the 451 291 patients with data on antibiotic use received antibiotic therapy, predominantly broad-spectrum agents. As antibiotic use was not associated with improved clinical outcomes and is known to increase antimicrobial resistance, it should be rationalised through strengthened antimicrobial stewardship and behavioural interventions, particularly during respiratory viral epidemics.

title: Assessing the predictors of COVID-19 vaccination acceptance among pregnant women in the Sekondi Takoradi metropolis of Western Ghana using protection motivation theory
abstract: WHO recommends COVID-19 vaccination as one of the most effective measures for preventing severe COVID-19 outcomes. However, the success of vaccine use depends on its acceptability. This study explores the motivating factors for COVID-19 vaccination acceptance among pregnant women in the Secondi Takoradi metropolis of the Western Region of Ghana during the outbreak of the COVID-19 pandemic. A cross-sectional survey of 334 respondents was conducted using systematic sampling from the sub-district antenatal care registers. Data were collected through a structured questionnaire and analyzed using STATA. Pearson’s Chi-Square test was used to assess the relationship between respondents’ socio-demographic characteristics and Protection Motivation Theory (PMT) constructs, and regression analyses were employed to predict the predictors of COVID-19 vaccination acceptance. Pearson’s Chi-Square test showed that the number of children a respondent has was significantly related to the PMT constructs of vulnerability (p = 0.015), severity (p = 0.001), respondents’ self-efficacy (p = 0.001), and response efficacy (p = 0.045). The bivariate regression analyses also showed that vulnerability, severity, self-efficacy, and response efficacy were predictors of COVID-19 vaccine acceptance. Risk communication efforts should focus on women with fewer or no children. Also, the design of epidemic risk communication tools should be based on protection motivation. To enhance vaccine acceptance, the ministry in charge of communication and the National Commission for Civic Education should implement measures to ensure that only accurate information is provided during epidemics. Number of children influences epidemic risk perception and vaccine acceptance. Perceptions of the severity of an epidemic influence vaccine acceptance. Perceptions of vulnerability to an epidemic influence vaccine acceptance. Perceptions of the ability to undertake epidemic preventive measures influence vaccine acceptance. Perceptions of the efficacy of preventive measures influence vaccine acceptance.
