title: Comorbidities and Procedures Associated with Mortality in COVID-19 Hospitalizations
abstract: Abstract Background and Aims COVID-19 is associated with multisystem illness, but national evidence on mortality correlates and selected inpatient procedures remains limited. We examined associations of documented COVID-19, comorbidities, bronchoscopy, and left heart catheterization with in-hospital outcomes. Methods This retrospective cross-sectional analysis used adult discharges from the Healthcare Cost and Utilization Project National Inpatient Sample from 1 April 2020 through 31 December 2021. Survey weights, strata, and hospital clusters generated national estimates. Survey logistic regression estimated associations with in-hospital mortality, and survey-weighted general linear models examined ln(LOS+1). Analyses were discharge-level and associative. Results The analysis included 9,763,989 discharges, representing approximately 48.82 million weighted discharges. COVID-19 was documented in 8.2% of weighted discharges, and in-hospital mortality was 12.9% among COVID-19 discharges compared with 2.6% among non-COVID-19 discharges. In the fully adjusted model, COVID-19 was associated with higher mortality (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 5.456; 95% confidence interval [CI], 5.379–5.535). The association remained in sensitivity analyses restricted to principal-diagnosis COVID-19 (aOR, 3.805; 95% CI, 3.737–3.873) and in a reduced model with ordinal APR-DRG severity (aOR, 1.484; 95% CI, 1.462–1.506). Among COVID-19 admissions, bronchoscopy was associated with mortality (aOR, 6.625; 95% CI, 6.135–7.155) and longer transformed length of stay; the mortality association remained after severity adjustment (aOR, 4.362; 95% CI, 4.022–4.731). Among COVID-19 admissions with principal-diagnosis acute coronary syndrome, left heart catheterization was not significantly associated with mortality in the primary model (aOR, 0.890; 95% CI, 0.721–1.099), although a severity-adjusted sensitivity model yielded an inverse association (aOR, 0.743; 95% CI, 0.592–0.934). Conclusions Documented COVID-19 was associated with substantially higher in-hospital mortality. Bronchoscopy identified a particularly high-risk, resource-intensive group. The left heart catheterization results were sensitive to model specification. These discharge-level findings do not establish procedural treatment effects and remain susceptible to residual confounding and uncertain temporal ordering.

title: Did the emergence of the Omicron variant impact the COVID-19 vaccine sentiments in the Arab world? A Twitter-based comparative analysis
abstract: Background: Vaccine hesitancy constitutes a major obstacle for achieving herd immunity against coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19). Research has shown high vaccine hesitancy rates and low compliance among Arabic-speaking populations in the 2021–2022 period. The aim of this study was to analyze sentiments related to COVID-19 vaccines before and after the emergence of the COVID-19 Omicron variant in the Arab-speaking world. Methods Tweets were collected before and after the Omicron emergence period in the Arab-speaking world using Python-enabled CAMeL Tools (Arabic Natural Language Processing toolkit) libraries. A sentiment analysis on COVID-19 vaccines using Arabic keywords, a sentiment analysis by city, and a time series were conducted. Results The data sets exhibited a shift towards less negativity, more neutrality, and a possible adoption of a pragmatic discourse towards vaccine uptake. Sentiments by city showed the Gulf region registered the most presence in the Twitter data, and the time series demonstrated change in sentiments followed public health events. Conclusions Despite its limitations, the study pointed to change in sentiments in response to vaccine-related events. Increased neutral sentiments and vaccine discourse shifting towards vaccine uptake pragmatism after the onset of Omicron, indicate change is possible. Future research may focus on how change towards more vaccine acceptance can be triggered; on how Twitter vaccine discourse translates within local communities; on including other social media (for instance Facebook); on vaccine discourse analysis to get nuanced insights; and on ethical implications of vaccine policies.

title: COVID-19 severity among individuals with chronic diseases.
abstract: Background Previous studies reported that individuals with underlying chronic diseases who are infected with COVID-19 are at greater risk for more severe outcomes. In this study, we measured these risks among a wide range of comorbidities in a large cohort. Methods In this retrospective study, we analyzed the risk for hospitalization and the severity and mortality risk of COVID-19 among adults with obstructive lung diseases, hypertension, cardiovascular diseases, diabetes, kidney diseases, malignancies and immunosuppression states before the emergence of the Omicron variant. We used univariant analyses and adjusted for age, sex, Body Mass Index (BMI), smoking habits, Socioeconomic Status (SES) and the Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI). Results Of the 44,866 individuals who were positive for COVID-19, 2358 were hospitalized. The adjusted Odds Ratio (aOR) for hospitalization was significantly greater for most chronic diseases, with the highest risk for individuals who underwent a kidney transplant (15.06; 95% Confidence Interval [95% CI 7.86-28.73]). A significantly greater risk for severe COVID-19 than for mild to moderate disease (602 and 1657 patients, respectively) was found for patients with cerebrovascular diseases (aOR = 1.46; 95% CI 1.07-1.99). A greater mortality risk was demonstrated for individuals who had undergone kidney transplantation (aOR = 4.23; 95% CI 1.36-11.82) and those with Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD) (aOR = 1.43; 95% CI 1.02-1.99). Conclusions Individuals with cerebrovascular disease were at increased risk for severe COVID-19, whereas individuals with CKD and past kidney transplantation were at increased mortality risk. These individuals should receive early medical intervention when they are diagnosed.

title: Long COVID undercoding and prediction from releasable electronic health record summaries in All of Us
abstract: Objective: To estimate Long COVID undercoding in electronic health records (EHRs) against federal survey prevalence, and to evaluate a predictor of later coding that anyone can rebuild from counts a research enclave releases. Materials and Methods: Among 23,790 All of Us adults with COVID-19, we compared coded shares with Household Pulse Survey prevalence. Among 23,300 adults uncoded at day 90, we predicted a first U09.9 code by day 455. We fitted naive Bayes and linear discriminant models outside the enclave from released counts and compared them with an elastic net fitted inside to the same patients and features. Tests were a random 20% of patients (4,680, 50 coded) and 18 held-out EHR sites (5,760, 60 coded). Results: Under survey-comparability assumptions, about 1 in 9 adults who ever had Long COVID carried its code, and the women-to-men coding ratio was 0.79 (95% sensitivity interval, 0.65-0.95). The released models' areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROCs) were 0.68 (95% CI, 0.60-0.75) on the patient test and 0.64 (0.55-0.72) at held-out sites, 0.049 (0.001-0.104) above the elastic net. On the patient test, the elastic net had a higher area under the precision-recall curve (difference 0.062, 0.003-0.122). Released probabilities overestimated coding risk at held-out sites. Discussion: Fitting from released counts did not consistently lower discrimination. Coded outcomes inform disease discrimination only under stated coding assumptions. Conclusion: Long COVID is substantially and unevenly undercoded, and a model rebuilt from public counts predicts its later coding with moderate discrimination.

title: Emergence of Novel Macrolide-Resistant Mycoplasma pneumoniae Sequence Type 3 Subclades in Children after COVID-19 Pandemic, Taiwan.
abstract: Post-COVID-19 pandemic Mycoplasma pneumoniae resurgences have occurred globally and have been particularly severe in Taiwan. We conducted a multicenter study to assess M. pneumoniae trends in children. Compared with the 2019 peak, 2024 data revealed a doubling of incidence (546/100,000 population), a 2.2-fold increase in intensive care unit admissions (10.9/100,000 population), and a 13.7-fold surge in central nervous system complications (6.1/100,000 population). In a 2023-2024 prospective cohort (n = 226), intensive care unit admission risk factors were neutrophils >7,000/μL (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 6.2 [95% CI 1.3-29.9]), platelets >400 × 10 3 /μL (aOR 12.5 [95% CI 2.7-57.9]), pleural effusion (aOR 9.7 [95% CI 1.6-58.1]), and central nervous system involvement (aOR 27.9 [95% CI 4.1-188.3]). Phylogenetic analysis of 698 genomes demonstrated that 4 emerging subclades replaced pre-COVID-19 lineages by mid-2024; 1 subclade was associated with severe outcomes, highlighting evolving resistant, neurotropic lineages and calling for enhanced surveillance.

Compared with the 2019 peak, 2024 data revealed a doubling of incidence (546/100,000 population), a 2.2-fold increase in intensive care unit admissions (10.9/100,000 population), and a 13.7-fold surge in central nervous system complications (6.1/100,000 population). In a 2023-2024 prospective cohort (n = 226), intensive care unit admission risk factors were neutrophils >7,000/μL (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 6.2 [95% CI 1.3-29.9]), platelets >400 × 10 3 /μL (aOR 12.5 [95% CI 2.7-57.9]), pleural effusion (aOR 9.7 [95% CI 1.6-58.1]), and central nervous system involvement (aOR 27.9 [95% CI 4.1-188.3]). Phylogenetic analysis of 698 genomes demonstrated that 4 emerging subclades replaced pre-COVID-19 lineages by mid-2024; 1 subclade was associated with severe outcomes, highlighting evolving resistant, neurotropic lineages and calling for enhanced surveillance.

title: Preliminary stability studies of a β-SARS-CoV-2 virus-like particle vaccine
abstract: ABSTRACT We aimed to study the stability of a Beta (β)-SARS-CoV-2 virus-like particle (VLP) vaccine in a series of preliminary experiments using selective stabilizing excipients. β-SARS-CoV-2 VLPs were produced and purified using established methodologies. The thermostability of VLPs was tested at 4°C and −30°C in the presence or absence of stabilizers polysorbate 80, sorbitol, or L-histidine in the presence of a physiological NaCl concentration of 137 mM. The integrity of VLPs was assessed using ELISA, Western immunoblot, and dynamic light scatter (DLS). β-SARS-CoV-2 VLPs were stable at 4°C for 14 days, and the addition of stabilizing excipients improved stability compared to VLPs in PBS alone. Storage of VLPs at −80°C maintained particle integrity by DLS analysis for up to 2 years. Excipients helped to maintain the antigenicity of the VLPs by ELISA and Western immunoblot, and DLS analysis revealed that VLPs retained their particulate structure. IMPORTANCE SARS-CoV-2 continues to circulate globally and cause significant illness. The problem of waning immunity to mRNA/LNPs has necessitated frequent boosters to keep pace with emerging variants. The development of alternative vaccines, therefore, remains a priority. Protein- based vaccines, like VLPs, offer a safe alternative able to produce longer-lasting immune responses. In this preliminary stability analysis, the β-SARS-CoV-2 VLPs were found to be stable at 4°C, and the addition of excipients improved VLP stability. Storage of VLPs at −30°C and −80°C also showed that the VLPs are stable for extended periods. Our findings will be of importance for the ongoing development of a SARS-CoV-2 VLP-based vaccine.

title: Variant-Specific Temporal Transcriptomic Responses of Ex Vivo Dog Lung Explants to SARS-CoV-2 Delta and Omicron Infection
abstract: The rapid evolution and emergence of SARS-CoV-2 variants have posed significant public health challenges due to enhanced transmissibility and diverse clinical outcomes. While the effects of these variants in humans have been extensively investigated, their impact on domestic animals remains insufficiently understood. Given the close interaction between humans and dogs, along with documented cases of human-to-animal transmission and the potential role of companion animals as reservoirs for viral evolution, understanding the molecular dynamics of SARS-CoV-2 infection in dogs is of considerable importance. However, in vivo infection studies in non-laboratory animal species are highly resource intensive, time-consuming, require ABSL3 facilities, and involve ethical constraints, limiting their widespread application. In this context, ex vivo culture systems provide a practical and physiologically relevant alternative. Therefore, in the present study, we employed an ex vivo lung explant culture model derived from domestic dogs to investigate host responses to the SARS-CoV-2 Delta and Omicron variants. Comprehensive transcriptomic profiling across multiple time points post-infection revealed significant alterations in genes associated with cell adhesion, structural components, extracellular matrix (ECM) organization and regulation, immune responses, mitochondrial activity, oxidative phosphorylation, and ribosomal function. Both variants induced marked downregulation of ECM-associated and T-cell-related genes, suggesting disruption of tissue integrity and suppression of adaptive immune responses. The Delta variant was characterized by early and sustained suppression of immune-associated signaling pathways, particularly T-cell receptor signaling, whereas the Omicron variant induced stronger activation of genes associated with mitochondrial activity, oxidative phosphorylation, and translational responses. At later stages of infection, especially at 24 h post-infection (hpi), canine lung explants exhibited increased expression of genes related to tissue repair, epithelial maintenance, mitochondrial function, and ribosomal activity, suggesting activation of compensatory responses aimed at maintaining cellular stability under viral stress. Notably, several hub genes were identified, including CD2, CD3D, CD3E, CD27, PTPRC, ZAP70, SYK, and LCP2 in Delta infection, and FLT3LG, MRPL2, MRPL4, MRPS11, MRPS12, RPS13, and RPS5 in Omicron infection, which are involved in critical pathways associated with immune signaling, mitochondrial function, metabolic regulation, and protein synthesis. Furthermore, the observed mitochondrial and ribosomal responses may indicate that therapeutic strategies aimed at supporting mitochondrial function and modulating excessive inflammation could potentially help reduce lung damage during severe infection. Overall, this study provides important insights into the transcriptomic response of dog lung explants following exposure to SARS-CoV-2 Delta and Omicron variants and also highlights the utility of ex vivo canine lung explant cultures as a valuable platform for studying host–pathogen interactions.

title: Mapping the Fragment-Binding Landscape of SARS-CoV-2 nsp14 for Antiviral Drug Discovery
abstract: Non-structural protein 14 (nsp14) is a bifunctional coronavirus drug target, combining a 3'-to-5' exoribonuclease domain with an N7-methyltransferase domain. Proof-of-concept data have demonstrated beneficial effects in animal models upon inhibition. Using microscale thermophoresis and X-ray crystallography, we screened full-length nsp14 for fragment hits and developed SAR-by-catalogue analogues with five- to eight-fold improved affinity. Several scaffolds showed pronounced overlap between distinct pockets, complicating structure-based optimisation. Analysis of mutational frequencies across over 14 million SARS-CoV-2 genome sequences identified nsp14 residues with markedly high and very low mutation rates, highlighting sites best suited to pan-coronavirus inhibitor design. Combining these data with all 19 publicly known fragment- and ligand-binding regions on nsp14, most of which have never been directly compared, we introduce a systematic site-naming system and rank every site by its potential for future structure-based development. Weighing criteria include proof-of-principle inhibitor data, cross-coronavirus conservation, mutation frequency, the number of fragments bound per site, and susceptibility to crystallographic artefacts from symmetry mates. This ranked, unified binding-site atlas resolves which of the many previously reported nsp14 sites merit prioritisation, providing a practical resource for future coronavirus antiviral drug development.

title: Incidence of adverse events following COVID-19 vaccination in observational studies
abstract: Abstract Introduction This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to estimate and synthesize real-world incidence measures of adverse events following immunization (AEFI) associated with COVID-19 vaccines and to examine how methodological and epidemiological factors influence reported estimates. Methods Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines and a prospectively registered protocol (PROSPERO), eight data sources including grey literature were searched for observational studies reporting AEFI incidence in the general population. A total of 160 studies met inclusion criteria. Incidence metrics were grouped by unit of analysis: events per notification, per exposed individual, per 100 doses, and cumulative incidence of individuals experiencing at least one AEFI. Subgroup analyses evaluated variation by age group, vaccine platform, number of doses, data source, study design, and denominator type. Risk of bias was assessed using the JBI tools and ROBINS-I. Results Pooled estimates differed according to metric definition. Event-to-exposure ratios yielded a combined estimate of 0.118 (95% CI: 0.066–0.211; 154 studies), whereas cumulative incidence proportions yielded 0.561 (95% CI: 0.336–0.763; 6 studies). Heterogeneity was extreme (I2 ≥ 99%), partly reflecting denominator type: ratios ranged from 0.002 (notification-based) to 0.378 (dose-based) ( p < 0.001). Most studies had moderate-to-high risk of bias; excluding high-risk studies reduced the Set 1 estimate by approximately 41% to 0.069 (95% CI: 0.033–0.146). Conclusions Real-world AEFI incidence varies according to the epidemiological metric, denominator structure, and methodological quality of primary studies; event-to-exposure ratios and cumulative incidence proportions capture distinct dimensions of AEFI occurrence and should not be directly compared.

title: Herpesvirus reactivation in COVID-19: clinical evidence, mechanistic insights, and research gaps
abstract: Herpesviruses establish lifelong latency and can reactivate when antiviral immune surveillance is compromised. Since the onset of COVID-19 pandemic, reactivation of multiple human herpesviruses has increasingly been documented, particularly in patients with severe or critical illness. Herpesvirus reactivation has been associated with prolonged intensive care unit stays, secondary infections, greater ventilatory support requirements, and increased mortality. This review summarizes the latency and reactivation characteristics of the major human herpesviruses and evaluates the clinical evidence linking their reactivation to SARS-CoV-2 infection. We further propose a multifactorial mechanistic framework involving impaired T-cell and natural killer cell surveillance, defective interferon-mediated immunity, sustained inflammation and cytokine signaling, direct and indirect effects of SARS-CoV-2 proteins, and host transcriptional and epigenetic reprogramming. However, despite accumulating clinical and experimental evidence supporting a biologically plausible association between SARS-CoV-2 infection and herpesvirus reactivation, the precise mechanisms underlying this interplay remain incompletely understood. Longitudinal viral monitoring, physiologically relevant latency models, and mechanistic intervention studies are therefore needed to establish causality and identify patients who may benefit from targeted surveillance or antiviral treatment.

title: Rehabilitation professionals at the COVID-19 frontline: a testimony-informed narrative review of health-worker mortality, vaccine hesitancy, physiotherapy and telerehabilitation
abstract: Background COVID-19 placed an unprecedented burden on health workers and disrupted rehabilitation services. Existing reviews have examined health-worker infection and mortality, vaccine hesitancy and telerehabilitation separately; few have considered these dimensions together from the perspective of rehabilitation professionals. Methods Narrative review following SANRA recommendations. PubMed, Scopus and Google Scholar were searched (initial search January 2019–December 2022; updated during revision to December 2025 to capture later publications reporting 2020–2021 data). Sources were selected purposively, prioritising systematic reviews, large multicentre studies and official agency reports. First-person clinical observations from the author's postgraduate training in two French university hospitals are presented separately, in labelled boxes, and are not used as evidence for quantitative claims. Results WHO estimated 80,000–180,000 health and care worker deaths from COVID-19 between January 2020 and May 2021 (central estimate 115,500), versus 6,643 reported through surveillance. Front-line workers had a 3.4-fold higher adjusted risk of a positive test than the general community. Vaccine hesitancy among health workers was 37% in a 91-country survey and 22.5% in a review of 76,471 workers; a scoping review of nurses reported 20.7% refusal. In a French tertiary centre, 73.1% were in favour, 23.1% hesitant and 3.9% opposed. Physiotherapy guidance addressed acute respiratory care, early mobilisation and post-COVID-19 rehabilitation. Telerehabilitation achieved outcomes similar to centre-based pulmonary rehabilitation, but accounted for only 6% of outpatient episodes in a large US database. Four heuristic constructs are proposed: Frontline Abandonment Syndrome (FAS), Vaccination Refusal Cascade (VRC), Telerehabilitation Emergency Pivot (TEP) and Post-COVID Functional Decoupling (PCFD). Each is positioned against existing terminology and presented as a testable hypothesis rather than a validated construct. Conclusions COVID-19 exposed gaps in health-worker protection, communication around vaccination and the integration of rehabilitation into pandemic preparedness. Telerehabilitation deserves a defined place in hybrid care models, and the proposed constructs require formal concept analysis and empirical testing.

title: Post-COVID-19 Expansion of Streptococcus pyogenes Lineages Causing Toxic Shock Syndrome, Japan, 2023-2024.
abstract: We analyzed 919 Streptococcus pyogenes isolates from laboratory-confirmed streptococcal toxic shock syndrome cases in Japan during 2023-2024. Post-COVID-19 resurgence was driven by expansion of M1 UK (49.8%) and emerging M1 13SNPs (37.4%) lineages, replacing ancestral M1 global . M1 13SNPs were associated with younger patient age and higher death rates in unadjusted analyses.

title: Crystal structures of SARS-CoV-2 main protease and its complex with PBI-0451.
abstract: The SARS-CoV-2 main protease (M pro ) has a pivotal role in mediating viral genome replication and transcription of the coronavirus, making it a prime target for antiviral drug development. This study presents four high-resolution crystal structures of SARS-CoV-2 M pro in the apo state. Among these structures, we identify a previously unobserved, stable inactive conformation, characterized by a major displacement of the oxyanion loop (especially Phe140, Leu141 and Asn142), the rotation of some important residues (including His163 and His172) and the loss of many key interactions around the active site, which provides new insights into the conformational dynamics of the enzyme. We also report structures of M pro in complex with the covalent inhibitor pomotrelvir (PBI-0451) for the wild-type enzyme and three clinical variant-associated mutants (G15S, K90R and P132H). PBI-0451 adopts a virtually identical mode when bound to wild-type M pro and the K90R and G15S M pro mutants. However, the crystal structure of PBI-0451 bound to SARS-CoV-2 M pro P132H reveals a discernible shift of the Gln189-bearing loop and incomplete electron density for the Gln189 side chain, which may be responsible for the subtle modest reduction in PBI-0451 susceptibility. These findings expand the conformational landscape of M pro and offer structural guidance for the design of M pro -targeted antiviral drugs.
journal: Acta Crystallographica Section D Structural Biology

Among these structures, we identify a previously unobserved, stable inactive conformation, characterized by a major displacement of the oxyanion loop (especially Phe140, Leu141 and Asn142), the rotation of some important residues (including His163 and His172) and the loss of many key interactions around the active site, which provides new insights into the conformational dynamics of the enzyme. We also report structures of M pro in complex with the covalent inhibitor pomotrelvir (PBI-0451) for the wild-type enzyme and three clinical variant-associated mutants (G15S, K90R and P132H). PBI-0451 adopts a virtually identical mode when bound to wild-type M pro and the K90R and G15S M pro mutants. However, the crystal structure of PBI-0451 bound to SARS-CoV-2 M pro P132H reveals a discernible shift of the Gln189-bearing loop and incomplete electron density for the Gln189 side chain, which may be responsible for the subtle modest reduction in PBI-0451 susceptibility. These findings expand the conformational landscape of M pro and offer structural guidance for the design of M pro -targeted antiviral drugs.

title: SARS-CoV-2 spike protein enhances HBV replication via autophagy and aggravates inflammation in CHB patients with liver dysfunction
abstract: ABSTRACT This study investigated the effects of the severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) spike protein (S protein) on hepatitis B virus (HBV) replication and immune function in patients with chronic hepatitis B (CHB), aiming to elucidate the underlying mechanisms of S protein–HBV interaction. Through in vitro cell experiments and clinical sample analyses, S protein expression was induced in HepG2.2.15 cells, leading to enhanced HBV replication; this effect was reduced by autophagy inhibitors, confirming the critical mediating role of autophagy. Furthermore, peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from CHB patients were co-cultured with the S protein, resulting in increased inflammatory responses in T cells and monocytes, particularly in patients with concurrent abnormal liver function and lipid metabolism disorders. In summary, the S protein promotes HBV replication by activating autophagy and exacerbates immune inflammation in CHB patients. Autophagy inhibitors block its effect on HBV replication, suggesting autophagy as a key regulatory target. The immune-activating effects of the S protein are more pronounced in patients with liver dysfunction and metabolic abnormalities. These findings provide a basis for further investigation into the interplay between the S protein and autophagy in HBV infection. IMPORTANCE This study reveals that the severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) spike protein promotes hepatitis B virus (HBV) replication by activating the autophagy pathway and elucidates its role in exacerbating immune inflammation in patients with chronic hepatitis B, particularly showing more pronounced responses in patients with liver dysfunction and lipid metabolism disorders. These findings provide critical molecular insights into the viral interaction and immunopathological mechanisms during SARS-CoV-2 and HBV co-infection. They also improve our understanding of the interplay between SARS-CoV-2 and HBV in the context of co-infection and provide a basis for future studies.

title: Multiple Protein Isoforms with Isoelectric Point in the Blood pH Physiological Range May Underpin High Virulence and Pathogenicity of SARS-CoV-2 B1617 Strain
abstract: Genome sequencing has ushered a new era in modern biology by allowing scientists to investigate the assembled genome for clues on pathogenic potential as well as new and emerging virulent genes in the genome. This work started out with the validation of an in-house MATLAB gene finder software that examined the SARS-CoV-2 B1617 strain assembled genome. Data reveals 70 open reading frames, whose calculated molecular weight and isoelectric point yields a theoretical protein 2D gel electrophoresis pattern with clustering of high molecular weight proteins (i.e., 50 to 300 kDa) within the physiological pH range of 6 to 8. Such results suggest one possible reason for the high virulence of SARS-CoV-2 B1617 strain due probably to the pathogenic effects of the high molecular weight proteins that have isoelectric point in the pH 6 to 8 window. Further observations of clusters of proteins with closely similar number of amino acids in the range of 200 to 300, 1300 to 1400, 1800 to 1900, 1900 to 2000, and 2000 to 2100 prompted the development of another in-house MATLAB multiple sequence alignment software. Results from the alignment reveals that, in each protein cluster, there are one or two more ancient proteins with long N-terminal end that is not present in the modern version of the protein, which share long segment of high sequence conservation with the ancient proteins after the N-terminal end segment. This shows that SARS-CoV-2 B1617 strain may be evolutionary ancient, and relics of ancient proteins are still remnants in the assembled genome of the virus strain. Overall, this work unexpectedly highlights salient features of SARS-CoV-2 B1617 strain as having high molecular weight proteins with isoelectric points in the pH 6 to 8 physiological window, as well as the virus harbouring ancient proteins with unknown pathogenic and virulence potential.

title: Applying normalized p-control charts for early detection of local COVID-19 outbreaks.
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic underscored the urgent need for early detection of local outbreaks to enable better resource allocation and effective mitigation. Outbreak identification largely depended on local infection rates, which were highly variable and influenced by daily testing volumes. Effective pandemic management requires accurate, adaptive methods that reflect the dynamic and localized nature of these rates, ensuring timely and appropriate interventions. This study seeks to improve the early detection and localization of COVID-19 outbreaks through Statistical Process Control (SPC) and health data analytics. We propose an adaptive outbreak-detection framework that combines a normalized p-control chart with an Amplitude-based labeler (ABL). For each area and day, the monitored statistic is a standardized positivity-rate score, computed from the observed daily positivity rate, the number of tests performed that day, and an area-specific baseline positivity estimate derived from recent historical observations. This calibration is followed by Phase II sequential monitoring using fixed three-sigma limits on the normalized scale and Western Electric decision rules. The framework accommodates varying daily sample sizes, captures regional interconnectedness, and supports parameter tuning using a temporally ordered train/test design. Accounting for daily testing fluctuations and spatial variability, it enhances the accuracy of local outbreak detection. Compared with the benchmark outbreak-detection methods considered in this study, the proposed framework was evaluated on its ability to predict outbreak onset within the following three days, achieving overall accuracy of 0.81 and averaged precision and recall of 0.83 and 0.79, respectively. Performance was further evaluated using the Fβ-measure, enabling a flexible trade-off between precision and recall depending on the relative cost of errors. SPC-based methods like ours can significantly improve early outbreak detection and localization. In the post-vaccination era, when targeted responses are key to controlling localized spread while avoiding widespread restrictions, health data analytics offer a valuable tool for informed decision-making.

title: Impact of SARS-CoV-2 vaccination on cancer trends: a nationwide interrupted time series study
abstract: BACKGROUND: A recent population-based cohort study of Seoul residents in South Korea reported increased incidence of several cancers within one year of SARS-CoV-2 vaccination. We examined whether a short-term, population-level change in cancer incidence trends was detectable at the national vaccination rollout, using a design that does not compare vaccinated with unvaccinated individuals. METHODS: We conducted an interrupted time series analysis of Korea National Health Insurance Service data for 36,024,394 individuals born between 1955 and 2004, covering February 2011 to September 2025 (176 months). The intervention point was August 2021, when cumulative first-dose coverage exceeded 50%. Monthly incidence of 13 cancer categories defined by ICD-10 code ranges and of four site-specific cancers (stomach, colorectum, lung and prostate) was compared with counterfactual forecasts from ARIMA/SARIMA models, and segmented regression estimated immediate level and trend changes (significance threshold P < 0.01). The placement of the intervention point was varied from 0 to 18 months, and the resulting estimates were compared with those obtained at 30 placebo points in the pre-pandemic period. RESULTS: Overall, 89.3% of the population received at least one dose. No immediate level change (relative risk 0.923-1.072) or trend change (0.995-1.005) reached significance for any of the 13 categories, and none reached significance for the four site-specific cancers. Across the lag grid, 2.0% of estimates met the threshold, compared with 4.1% at placebo points. The 99% confidence limits excluded immediate increases larger than 8.9% to 23.0% across the 13 categories and 8.1% to 23.4% across the four site-specific cancers. CONCLUSIONS: The national SARS-CoV-2 vaccination rollout in South Korea was not accompanied by a detectable short-term, population-level change in cancer incidence trends over the 50 months that followed. TRIAL REGISTRATION: Not applicable.

title: Cyclosporine treatment of ARDS due to severe COVID-19: The I-SPY COVID Adaptive Platform Trial.
abstract: Abstract Rationale Aberrant host response to SARS-CoV-2 infection causes severe lung injury and acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) with resultant multiorgan failure and death. Cyclosporine, a calcineurin inhibitor with potent immunosuppressant and direct antiviral properties, was hypothesized to reduce cytokine-driven injury in hospitalized patients with severe COVID-19 ARDS. Objectives To evaluate whether cyclosporine improves time to recovery and reduces mortality in critically ill patients with COVID-19, using the I-SPY COVID adaptive platform trial design. Methods In this phase 2, multicenter, open-label, randomized controlled trial, non-intubated and intubated adults with confirmed COVID-19 requiring ≥6L/min oxygen received oral cyclosporine 5mg/kg/day in two divided doses for 5 days, added to standard backbone therapy (dexamethasone and remdesivir), or standard therapy alone. Co-primary endpoints were time to recovery and time to death, assessed using Bayesian proportional-hazard models with pre-specified graduation thresholds. Results Of 238 randomized patients (110 cyclosporine, 128 control), 28-day recovery rates were 65.9% vs. 71.1% and 28-day mortality rates were 10.7% vs. 11.3%, respectively. The posterior probability that cyclosporine improved recovery was 6% (graduation threshold >97.5%) and that it reduced mortality was 59.6% (graduation threshold >90%), meeting neither pre-specified efficacy criterion. Serious adverse events were more frequent with cyclosporine (17.3% vs. No significant differences in inflammatory plasma biomarkers were observed between groups. Conclusions Cyclosporine did not meet pre-specified efficacy thresholds for recovery or mortality in severe COVID-19 ARDS and was associated with a higher rate of serious adverse events. These results do not support its addition to standard care in this population.
journal: Annals of the American Thoracic Society

title: Circulating calprotectin levels are associated with lung damage and disease outcome in patients with COVID-19.
abstract: Objective The present study aimed to investigate whether circulating calprotectin levels were associated with the extent of lung parenchyma involvement, laboratory parameters of inflammation/organ damage, and clinical outcome in patients with SARS-CoV-2 infection. Methods A retrospective observational cohort study was conducted enrolling 172 adult patients with laboratory-confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection. The extent of lung parenchyma involvement was assessed using a validated high-resolution computerized tomography (HRCT)-based stratification system. Serum calprotectin concentrations were quantified using the QUANTA Flash Circulating Calprotectin Reagents. Routine laboratory parameters were collected from clinical records. In a subset of patients who received tocilizumab ( n = 56), serum samples were longitudinally collected. Results Circulating serum calprotectin levels were significantly associated with the extent of CT-assessed pulmonary involvement, markers of systemic inflammation, and adverse clinical outcomes (mechanical ventilation requirement and in-hospital death). A calprotectin threshold of 3.86 μg/mL showed high sensitivity for identifying patients with ≥40% lung parenchyma involvement, while a threshold of 13.73 μg/mL showed high specificity for adverse clinical outcomes. Longitudinal monitoring of calprotectin in tocilizumab-treated patients revealed that rising levels during follow-up were associated with death or tracheotomy, independent of baseline values. Conclusion Our findings support the clinical utility of circulating calprotectin as a complementary biomarker in COVID-19 management.

source_records.abstract: OBJECTIVE The present study aimed to investigate whether circulating calprotectin levels were associated with the extent of lung parenchyma involvement, laboratory parameters of inflammation/organ damage, and clinical outcome in patients with SARS-CoV-2 infection. METHODS A retrospective observational cohort study was conducted enrolling 172 adult patients with laboratory-confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection. The extent of lung parenchyma involvement was assessed using a validated high-resolution computerized tomography (HRCT)-based stratification system. Serum calprotectin concentrations were quantified using the QUANTA Flash Circulating Calprotectin Reagents. Routine laboratory parameters were collected from clinical records. In a subset of patients who received tocilizumab (n = 56), serum samples were longitudinally collected. RESULTS Circulating serum calprotectin levels were significantly associated with the extent of CT-assessed pulmonary involvement, markers of systemic inflammation, and adverse clinical outcomes (mechanical ventilation requirement and in-hospital death). A calprotectin threshold of 3.86 μg/mL showed high sensitivity for identifying patients with ≥40% lung parenchyma involvement, while a threshold of 13.73 μg/mL showed high specificity for adverse clinical outcomes. Longitudinal monitoring of calprotectin in tocilizumab-treated patients revealed that rising levels during follow-up were associated with death or tracheotomy, independent of baseline values. CONCLUSION Our findings support the clinical utility of circulating calprotectin as a complementary biomarker in COVID-19 management.

title: Temporal trends in reported vector-borne diseases in China before and after the onset of COVID-19 from 2004 to 2023.
abstract: BACKGROUND Vector-borne diseases (VBDs) continue to pose a public health burden in China. However, changes in the reported incidence and mortality of VBDs during the COVID-19 period remain insufficiently characterized. METHODS We analyzed five major VBDs-typhus, dengue, leishmaniasis, malaria, and epidemic encephalitis B (EEB)-in China from 2004 to 2023. Province- and age-specific surveillance data for 2004-2020 were obtained from the Chinese Center for Disease Control and Prevention, whereas national aggregate data for 2021-2023 were obtained from the National Health Commission. Accordingly, spatial and age-specific analyses were restricted to 2004-2020, while national trend analyses were extended through 2023. Annual trends were evaluated using Joinpoint regression, monthly seasonal patterns were assessed using STL decomposition, monthly changes after January 2020 were evaluated using interrupted time-series analysis, and expected monthly trajectories for 2020-2023 were estimated using SARIMA models trained on pre-COVID data. RESULTS From 2004 to 2020, incidence and mortality of VBDs declined significantly, especially for malaria, dengue, and EEB, and spatial hotspots were concentrated mainly in southern provinces. Compared with 2013-2019, overall incidence and mortality during 2020-2023 were 59.86% lower (95% CI: -60.36 to -59.36; P < 0.001) and 83.72% lower (95% CI: -87.86 to -78.18; P < 0.001), respectively. Malaria and EEB showed the largest reductions, whereas typhus and leishmaniasis changed less markedly. However, these declines should be interpreted cautiously because they may reflect a combination of COVID-19-era public health measures, pre-existing long-term trends, disease-specific control programs, and possible surveillance disruption. CONCLUSIONS During the COVID-19 period in China, reported VBD incidence and mortality decreased substantially. However, it would be overly simplistic to attribute these changes entirely to COVID-19-related interventions, as other factors were also likely involved. These findings highlight the need for reliable surveillance and reporting during public health emergencies, together with forecasting tools that can be adapted to changing conditions, to support future vector-borne disease control.

title: Antimicrobial Resistance Trends in COVID-19 Patients with Hospital Infection in Intensive Care: A Retrospective Study in Central Italy, 2020-2022.
abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) was exacerbated by COVID-19 pandemic. This study describes prevalence and trends of AMR in patients with diagnosed severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infection admitted during 2020-2022 to the intensive care unit (ICU) in Molise region, central Italy. A retrospective study was conducted, including patients aged ≥ 18 years with at least one positive bacterial or fungal culture during ICU stay. Data were related to patient demographics, ICU outcomes, healthcare-associated infections, and antimicrobial susceptibility profiles. During the 2020-2022 period, 103 ICU admissions met the inclusion criteria, yielding 268 isolations, of which 157 underwent antimicrobial susceptibility testing. Apart from high proportion of Candida albicans , Gram-negative bacteria predominated, with Pseudomonas aeruginosa , Klebsiella pneumoniae , Escherichia coli , and Acinetobacter baumannii among the most frequent. Resistance to beta-lactams and carbapenems was consistently high, while it ranged from 53.8% to 66.7% to fluoroquinolones and remained above 50% to aminoglycosides. Tetracycline resistance showed significant year-to-year variation, increasing in 2022 compared with both 2020 and 2021. AMR rates in COVID-19 patients in ICU were persistently high throughout the pandemic, with critical resistance levels in Gram-negatives, underlining the need to reinforce infection prevention and control measures and antimicrobial stewardship programs and align prescribing practices with World Health Organization AWaRe recommendations, even during public health emergencies.

title: Shifts in invasive pneumococcal disease epidemiology following the SARS-CoV-2 pandemic in Madrid, Spain: insights from a six-year hospital-based study
abstract: Abstract Background Invasive pneumococcal disease (IPD) is influenced by vaccination strategies, circulating serotypes and respiratory viral activity. The COVID-19 pandemic substantially altered respiratory infection dynamics. The aim of the study was to evaluate temporal changes in IPD incidence, clinical characteristics and serotype distribution before, during and after the COVID-19 pandemic. Methods We conducted a retrospective study of all IPD cases diagnosed between January 2018 and December 2023 at a tertiary hospital in Madrid, Spain. IPD was defined by isolation or molecular detection of Streptococcus pneumoniae from normally sterile sites. Demographic, clinical, microbiological and virological data were analysed, together with available respiratory viral testing results, although testing was not systematic and viral coinfections may have been underdetected. Incidence rates were calculated using the hospital catchment population. Temporal patterns of IPD and population-level respiratory virus detections were compared descriptively. Results A total of 315 patients were identified, including 256 adults (81.3%) and 59 children (18.7%). Pneumonia was the most frequent clinical presentation (76.5%). Adults had a higher prevalence of comorbidities (78.1%) and mortality (11.3%), whereas children were generally healthy and more frequently required intensive care (67.8%), largely due to empyema-related management rather than increased disease severity. Overall, 68.6% of isolates were serotyped; serotypes 8 and 3 predominated. The annualized incidence of IPD decreased from 15.4 cases per 100,000 inhabitants (95% CI, 13.0–18.0) before the pandemic to 6.7 (95% CI, 5.5–8.2) during the pandemic period, followed by a partial recovery to 10.8 (95% CI, 7.4–15.1) in the post-pandemic period. Incidence calculations were restricted to patients residing within the hospital catchment area ( n = 284). Respiratory viral coinfection was documented in 18.4% of cases and was more frequent in children (39%). Serotype 11A showed the highest proportion of penicillin resistance. Conclusion IPD incidence declined sharply during the pandemic and increased again thereafter, coinciding with substantial changes in respiratory virus circulation. The persistent circulation of serotype 3 and the emergence of non-vaccine serotypes underscore the need for continued surveillance and updated vaccination strategies.

title: Ischemic stroke after bivalent mRNA COVID-19 vaccination and influenza vaccination during the 2022-2023 season: a multi-site self-controlled case series study.
abstract: Background The Vaccine Safety Datalink (VSD) detected a statistical signal for ischemic events (ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attack) following bivalent mRNA COVID-19 vaccination through prospective surveillance during 2022-2023. Although multiple studies from other surveillance systems and countries reported no increased risk, important methodological limitations remained. study addressed those limitations by evaluating the ischemic stroke risk following bivalent mRNA COVID-19 vaccination, influenza vaccination, and their same-day coadministration using an event-dependent self-controlled case series (SCCS) design. Methods Study outcomes included first-ever ischemic stroke (primary outcome), first-in-1-year ischemic stroke (secondary outcome), and ischemic events (exploratory outcomes), identified using ICD-10-CM codes in inpatient and emergency department settings during September 1, 2022-March 31, 2023, among individuals aged ≥12 years across eight VSD sites. Analyses were conducted separately for Pfizer-BioNTech and Moderna bivalent vaccines, with relative incidences (RI) and 95% confidence intervals (CI) estimated for 1-21-day and 1-42-day risk intervals, using person-time outside these intervals as the control period. Subgroup analyses were performed by age group (12-64, ≥65 years) and history of documented SARS-CoV-2 infection. Results A total of 6510 first-ever ischemic strokes were identified among more than 6.8 million participants. Among recipients of Pfizer-BioNTech bivalent COVID-19 and influenza vaccines, no statistically significant increased risk of first-ever ischemic stroke was observed following bivalent COVID-19 vaccination (RI = 0.94; 95% CI: 0.63-1.41), influenza vaccination (RI = 0.95; 95% CI: 0.82-1.10), or same-day coadministration (RI = 1.15; 95% CI: 0.88-1.49) within 1-21-day risk intervals; findings were similar for 1-42-day intervals. Comparable null results were observed for Moderna vaccine and across all subgroups, secondary, and exploratory outcomes. title: COVID-19 Vaccine Injury Compensation Claims in Israel: Characteristics, Approval Rates, and Factors Associated with Compensation
abstract: Abstract Background Vaccine-injury compensation programs (VICPs) are an essential component of national immunization programs, yet little data has been published regarding the characteristics of submitted claims or factors associated with compensation decisions. We analyzed all COVID-19 vaccine injury compensation claims (VICC) submitted and assessed in Israel. Methods We conducted a cross-sectional study of all COVID-19 VICC submitted between February 2021 and March 2026. Data from all adjudicated claims were retrospectively analyzed under MoH Helsinki Committee approval (#008-2026). Standardized demographic, clinical, and causality assessment data were collected by all adjudicating specialists. Factors associated with claim approval were evaluated using univariate and multivariable analyses. Results Overall, 313 claims submitted by 268 individuals were adjudicated by five specialists; 69 (22%) claims involving 67 (25%) individuals were approved for compensation. Approval was independently associated with the absence of a relevant prior comorbidity (aOR 0.3, p = 0.022), claims following the first two vaccine doses (aOR 0.3 for ≥ 3 vs. 1–2 doses, p = 0.013), and a shorter interval from vaccination to symptom onset (aOR 0.97/day, p = 0.001). Approval rates did not differ according to adjudicating specialist, legal representation, sex, ethnicity, psychiatric comorbidity, vaccine type, or injury severity. The most frequently compensated conditions included myocarditis/pericarditis (n = 52 claims, 42% approved), facial palsy (n = 18, 44%), and inflammatory skin diseases (n = 14, 57%), whereas no cardiovascular, thrombotic, or neoplastic conditions were approved. Compensation decisions were strongly associated with established causality assessment criteria, including temporal association, absence of alternative explanations, and supportive epidemiological evidence. Conclusions Approximately 40 COVID-19 VICC were submitted per million vaccinated individuals in Israel, of which one-quarter were approved. Compensation decisions were consistently associated with established causality assessment principles rather than demographic or procedural factors. These findings provide the first comprehensive description of the Israeli COVID-19 VICP and contribute to greater transparency regarding vaccine injury compensation.

title: Severity-stratified, longitudinal cis-eQTL mapping enables high-sensitivity detection of candidate causal genes for critical COVID-19
abstract: Host genetic variation influences heterogeneity in infectious disease severity. Genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have identified 69 lead single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) associated with critical COVID-19, but most lack known regulatory mechanisms. To date, the genetic cis-regulatory effects of critical COVID-19 GWAS lead SNPs have not been systematically characterized across acute illness and convalescent phases in a COVID-19 specific cohort. Here, performing severity-stratified, longitudinal cis-expression quantitative trait loci (cis-eQTL) mapping and colocalization with critical COVID-19 GWAS signals, we find that host cis-regulatory effects vary across clinical severity and disease phase. We analyzed peripheral blood mononuclear cells from 1,031 patients in the Immunophenotyping Assessment in a COVID-19 Cohort (IMPACC), a prospective multicenter study of adults hospitalized with COVID-19, profiled across 10 timepoints spanning acute illness and convalescence. We identified 23 GWAS lead SNPs that colocalized with cis-eQTLs at 26 candidate causal genes, with 16 detectable only when severity stratification and longitudinal sampling were incorporated. A colocalized, protective allele (chr19:4,717,660) at the TMIGD2 locus upregulated TMIGD2 expression exclusively during the acute phase in the prolonged-critical/fatal cohort, with no detectable effect in the rapid-recovery cohort. Our results show that host genetic effects on critical COVID-19 can be context-dependent, with cis-regulatory effects varying across clinical severity and disease phase. Severity-stratified, longitudinal cis-eQTL designs have greater sensitivity to identify candidate causal genes for critical COVID-19 GWAS associations than single-timepoint cross-sectional studies. Significance StatementGenome-wide association studies have identified 69 loci associated with life-threatening COVID-19, but most lead SNPs, the strongest association signal at each locus, lie outside protein-coding regions and act via unknown effects on gene regulation. We analyzed paired genetic and gene expression data from 1,031 hospitalized COVID-19 patients in IMPACC, sampled across ten timepoints and stratified by clinical severity. This analysis linked 23 of these risk variants to candidate genes, more than doubling the single-timepoint yield. Many effects appeared only in specific severity cohorts or timepoints. In critically ill patients early in hospitalization, the GWAS-associated allele increased expression of TMIGD2, a costimulatory receptor that amplifies T cell activation and may support antiviral responses. These variant-gene pairs warrant functional validation.

title: Fitting and Selection of Within-Host Models for SARS-CoV-2 Infection
abstract: Abstract The main question in model selection for longitudinal RT-qPCR data is whether improvements in fit justify the additional parameters of more complex within-host models. We compared a target-cell-limited model (TIV), an eclipse-phase extension (TEIV), and a fractional-order TIV using infection waves reconstructed from SARS-CoV-2 cycle-threshold (Ct) measurements in a National Basketball Association cohort. Each trajectory was fitted on the Ct scale by maximizing a right-censored Gaussian likelihood using hybrid global–local optimization. Model selection was based primarily on the small-sample corrected Akaike information criterion (AICc), computed from the censored likelihood; while robustness to the choice of information criterion was assessed using the Akaike information criterion (AIC) and Bayesian information criterion (BIC). Among 868 evaluable trajectories, the unpenalized likelihood ranking identified TEIV as the clear best-fitting model in 34.0% of cases, fr-TIV in 30.2%, and TIV in 3.3%; the remaining 32.5% were effectively tied. After accounting for model complexity, AICc clearly favored TIV in 97.8% of trajectories and fr-TIV in 0.5%, while 1.7% were effectively tied; TEIV was not a clear winner in any of the trajectories. Thus, for these short, sparsely sampled Ct-only trajectories, TIV provided the best-supported parsimonious effective description. This does not imply that eclipse-phase or memory-like dynamics are biologically absent, but rather that the simpler TIV model is favoured by standard information criteria for the limited information contained in these data.

title: Endophytic extract from Zanthoxylum piperitum as a promising source of anti-SARS-CoV-2 agents
abstract: Endophytic fungi produce secondary metabolites that protect their host plants from external threats, and this symbiotic system represents a promising source of antiviral compounds. In this study, we evaluated the anti- severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) activity of culture extracts from endophytic fungi isolated from Zanthoxylum piperitum. Among the 12 isolates tested, six exhibited significant antiviral activity in SARS-CoV-2-infected cells, and three of these showed distinct inhibitory effects on the viral 3C-like (3CL) protease. Chemical analysis of the active extracts identified sapinopyridione-produced by a Botryosphaeria endophyte-as the principal active metabolite. This compound displayed potent anti-SARS-CoV-2 activity, with a half-maximal inhibitory concentration (IC 50 ) of 2.45 μM (0.58 μg/mL). These findings suggest that sapinopyridione derivatives are promising lead compounds for the development of antiviral agents targeting SARS-CoV-2.

In this study, we evaluated the anti- severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) activity of culture extracts from endophytic fungi isolated from Zanthoxylum piperitum. Among the 12 isolates tested, six exhibited significant antiviral activity in SARS-CoV-2-infected cells, and three of these showed distinct inhibitory effects on the viral 3C-like (3CL) protease. Chemical analysis of the active extracts identified sapinopyridione-produced by a Botryosphaeria endophyte-as the principal active metabolite. This compound displayed potent anti-SARS-CoV-2 activity, with a half-maximal inhibitory concentration (IC 50 ) of 2.45 μM (0.58 μg/mL). These findings suggest that sapinopyridione derivatives are promising lead compounds for the development of antiviral agents targeting SARS-CoV-2.

title: Beyond 99%: Auditing Leakage, Shortcuts and Calibration in COVID-19 CT Classification
abstract: Public CT benchmarks for COVID-19 report slice-level accuracy above 99%, yet slices from one scan are near-duplicates and most datasets ship without patient IDs. We audit a MobileNetV3-Large classifier on a 19,685-slice, three-class CT dataset (non-COVID, COVID, non-informative) along four axes: leakage, shortcuts, external validity and calibration. Replacing a random slice split with a group split on recovered pseudo-patients lowers accuracy from 99.42% to 97.18%, and to 95.39% when groups follow file order. The error rate rises 4.9 to 8.0 times, and recall of COVID slices falls from 99.6% to 96.0% and 88.8%. Scalar acquisition features alone reach 0.996 balanced accuracy under a slice split and 0.630 under a group split (chance 0.333), and models trained without the lungs, or with only the lungs, both reach about 93%. On two external sites, discrimination drops (AUROC 0.83 on Sao Paulo; 0.86 for COVID lesion slices against normal patients in Tehran), and every model scores community-acquired pneumonia as more COVID-like than COVID (AUROC 0.43 to 0.49). Calibration does not transfer: binary ECE rises from 0.02 in-domain to 0.19 to 0.53 externally, and temperature scaling recovers at most 0.034. Because the main dataset has no patient IDs, we tested our grouping against true IDs on the Tehran cohort. It recovers patients poorly (adjusted Rand index at most 0.29). A nearest-neighbor probe scores 0.998 under a random slice split, 0.551 under a true patient split and 0.717 under our recovered groups, so the slice-versus-group gaps we report are lower bounds on true patient-level leakage.

title: An Oral Antiviral Combination Against Severe COVID-19 Enabled by the Synergistic Mechanisms of Action of Auranofin and Remdesivir.
abstract: ABSTRACT Auranofin, an FDA‐approved oral anti‐rheumatic drug, was previously shown by our group to restrict Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus‐2 (SARS‐CoV‐2) replication and pathology in preclinical models. Here, we systematically characterized its mechanism of action (MOA) through biochemical drug‐protein interactions, cell‐based mechanistic assays, and preclinical efficacy studies. Auranofin directly binds and inhibits SARS‐CoV‐2 MPro while simultaneously targeting multiple stages of the viral life cycle, disrupting endosomal trafficking, suppressing Spike S1/S2 proteolytic processing, impairing syncytia formation, and attenuating NF‐κB‐driven proinflammatory signaling. In cell culture, Auranofin demonstrated robust synergy with Remdesivir but competed with the MPro inhibitor Nirmatrelvir, informing rational combination design. In mice infected with the SARS‐CoV‐2 Delta variant, the oral combination of Auranofin and the Remdesivir prodrug GS‐621763 outperformed monotherapy, markedly reducing viral replication, inflammatory cytokine responses, and lung pathology, and improving clinical outcomes. These findings establish a multi‐target antiviral MOA of Auranofin and provide a mechanistic rationale for an all‐oral antiviral combination regimen against COVID‐19.

title: Snail restricts SARS-CoV-2 entry by limiting ACE2 expression as part of broader remodelling of epithelial determinants of viral tropism
abstract: ABSTRACT Pre-existing state of the host cell is a major determinant of the host susceptibility to viral infection. Here, we identify the epithelial-mesenchymal transition transcription factor Snail as a host restriction factor for SARS-CoV-2. Snail loss markedly increased SARS-CoV-2 replication, whereas Snail overexpression and complementation restricted viral replication. Transcriptomic analysis of Snail knockout cells revealed remodelling of epithelial surface-associated programs, including apical membrane, brush border, and junctional pathways. ACE2, the cellular receptor for SARS-CoV-2, was among the genes upregulated in Snail knockout cells. Snail negatively regulated ACE2 transcription, leading to reduced ACE2 transcript and protein abundance and, consequently, lower SARS-CoV-2 entry. Consistent with this, ACE2 promoter activity was higher in Snail knockout cells, which was reduced following Snail complementation. As a means to counter Snail’s antiviral functions, SARS-CoV-2 infection progressively depleted Snail protein in different cell culture models, while SNAI1 transcript abundance was surprisingly maintained or increased under the same conditions. Proteasome inhibition and protein-turnover analyses failed to account for this depletion. We find that SARS-CoV-2 infection resulted in reduced association of SNAI1 with polysomes at later stages of infection coinciding with virus-induced host translational suppression, resulting in lower protein synthesis. Together, these findings identify Snail as a regulator of the epithelial entry landscape that limits ACE2-associated SARS-CoV-2 entry and shapes cellular permissiveness, with broader implications for cellular determinants of viral tropism. SARS-CoV-2, in turn, progressively depletes this short-lived antiviral regulator, revealing how virus-induced translational shutoff can remodel pre-existing host cell states and thereby alter cellular susceptibility during infection. IMPORTANCE Cellular permissiveness is a major determinant of viral tropism. Host transcriptional programs are well known to shape cellular identity and surface composition, but their contribution to viral susceptibility is less often viewed as a form of host restriction. We previously showed that the epithelial-mesenchymal transition transcription factors Snail and Slug restrict multiple RNA viruses. Here, we show that Snail also limits SARS-CoV-2 infection by restricting ACE2 expression and by remodelling the epithelial surface landscape. SARS-CoV-2 neutralizes this threat by translationally repressing SNAI1 as part of the global translation suppression. We show that loss of Snail remodels surface-associated cellular programs and establishes a more permissive state. Together, these findings connect two aspects of host-virus interaction: transcriptional programs that establish cellular permissiveness and viral processes that can subsequently alter them. They position Snail as a broader regulator of the cellular landscape that influences viral entry and tropism.

title: Age-dependent differences in SARS-CoV-2 entry-factor expression and innate immune responses between pediatric and adult liver organoids
abstract: Background Since early 2022, a global surge in cases of severe acute hepatitis of unknown origin (AHUO) in children has been reported, with no definitive aetiology established. Epidemiological evidence suggests a potential link to SARS-CoV-2 infection, particularly during Omicron-predominant periods, yet the mechanisms underlying the apparently higher susceptibility of children to SARS-CoV-2-related liver injury remain poorly understood. This study used non-tumorous (tumor-adjacent) liver organoids derived from pediatric and adult donors to compare viral RNA accumulation and host immune responses to SARS-CoV-2 wild-type (WT) and Omicron (BA.1/BA.2) variants, aiming to explore the possible role of SARS-CoV-2 in pediatric acute hepatitis. Methods Liver organoids were established from non-tumorous (tumor-adjacent) liver tissue of three adult patients with hepatocellular carcinoma and three pediatric patients with hepatoblastoma, collected between February and December 2022. Organoids were infected with SARS-CoV-2 WT, Omicron BA.1 or BA.2 at a multiplicity of infection (MOI) of 0.1. Viral loads in supernatants and intracellular viral RNA were quantified by RT-qPCR at 24 and 48 h post-infection (hpi). At 48 hpi, RNA-seq was performed to profile transcriptomic changes and pathway enrichment. Additionally, single-cell RNA-seq data were used to compare baseline expression of SARS-CoV-2 entry-associated genes between pediatric and adult hepatocytes. Results Pediatric hepatocytes showed significantly higher basal expression of entry-related genes, including ASGR1, KREMEN1, CTSB, CTSL, and VIM, than adult cells. Both pediatric and adult liver organoids were permissive to WT and Omicron, but Omicron BA.1/BA.2 yielded higher intracellular viral RNA levels than WT, with notably higher intracellular viral RNA burden in pediatric organoids. RNA-seq revealed that Omicron infection induced a more pronounced innate-immune-associated transcriptional response in pediatric organoids—encompassing interferon signaling, RIG-I-like receptor and Toll-like receptor pathways—alongside relative downregulation of adaptive immune-pathway transcripts. In adult organoids, transcriptomic divergence between Omicron and WT was less pronounced. Compared with adults, Omicron-infected pediatric organoids upregulated interferon-γ signaling and other innate immune-associated transcriptional programs, while downregulating adaptive immune-pathway transcripts; key receptors such as ACE2 and TMPRSS4 remained consistently higher in pediatric organoids across all viral strains. Conclusion Pediatric liver organoids accumulate higher levels of Omicron viral RNA than WT-infected organoids and mount a stronger innate-immune transcriptional response alongside relative downregulation of adaptive immune-pathway transcripts, correlating with elevated expression of viral entry factors. These age-dependent in vitro differences raise the hypothesis that SARS-CoV-2, particularly Omicron, could contribute to hepatocyte injury in children; however, this organoid-based model does not include patients with acute hepatitis of unknown origin and cannot establish a causal or epidemiological link, which will require dedicated prospective clinical and mechanistic studies.

title: SARS-CoV-2 Gamma Variant In Vivo Model Demonstrates Severe Pathogenicity and Unique Transcriptomic Signatures Compared to Alpha, Delta, and Omicron Variants
abstract: Since 2019, SARS-CoV-2 variants of concern (VOCs), Alpha, Gamma, Delta, and Omicron, have exhibited distinct transmissibility and severity profiles. In Brazil, Gamma caused high mortality pre-vaccination, yet its underlying pathological mechanisms remain poorly understood. We evaluated VOC pathogenesis in K18-hACE2 transgenic mice (n = 8/group) by integrating clinical monitoring, lung histopathology, immunohistochemistry (F4/80, Ly-6G, CD4, CD8, Spike), and transcriptomics. Alpha, Gamma, and Delta induced severe weight loss, high clinical scores, and 100% mortality within seven days, whereas Omicron caused milder outcomes and survival despite similar pulmonary viral loads (107–108 copies/μL). Histopathology showed intense inflammation and hyperemia across all VOCs, with hierarchical clustering revealing a unique profile for Gamma. Transcriptomics identified 117 core upregulated genes, but Alpha and Gamma modulated a broader gene set. Gamma upregulated components of the alternative complement pathway (Cfb), heightened inflammatory mediators, and downregulated tissue adhesion genes. These results demonstrate that the Gamma variant phenotype is driven by extensive transcriptomic remodeling, whereas Omicron elicits an attenuated response, providing key insights into variant-specific mechanisms.

title: MULTIVALENT ACE2 ENGAGEMENT ACTIVATES PIEZO1-SPHINGOMYELINASE SIGNALING IN SARS-COV-2 SPIKE-MEDIATED CELL-CELL FUSION
abstract: SARS CoV 2 Spike not only fuses the viral envelope with host membranes to deliver viral RNA but also drives syncytium formation, a process that may contribute to viral spread and pulmonary pathology. Although the conformational transitions in Spike triggered by ACE2 engagement are well characterized, the host cell signaling events initiated by Spike-ACE2 interactions remain less understood. Here, we examine how Spike activates acid sphingomyelinase (ASM) in ACE2 expressing A549 cells and how this activity promotes cell-cell fusion. Using ASM-deficient and complemented cells, exogenous ceramide, pharmacological perturbations, and a split-NeonGreen fusion assay, we support a fusion-promoting pathway in which Spike-induced ACE2 clustering activates the mechanosensitive ion channel PIEZO1, triggering lysosomal exocytosis. Secreted ASM, together with intracellular neutral sphingomyelinase, generates ceramide that enhances syncytium formation, likely through activation of protein phosphatases PP1 and PP2A. Our results suggest that these phosphatases promote fusion by facilitating actin cortex detachment and reducing actomyosin tension through dephosphorylation of ERM proteins. Our findings highlight dynamic changes in membrane lipid composition and membrane-cytoskeleton interactions as regulators of fusion and signaling in SARS-CoV-2 infection and, potentially, other viral and cellular systems.

title: Functional and mechanistic characterization of SARS-CoV-2 NSP15 reveals metal-dependent regulation and inhibition by direct-binding small molecules
abstract: Abstract The SARS-CoV-2 nonstructural protein 15 (NSP15) is a uridine-specific endoribonuclease involved in viral RNA processing and immune evasion, thereby contributing to viral pathogenesis. Although NSP15 has been structurally characterized in several studies, which report its endoribonuclease activity and regulatory features, important functional and regulatory gaps remain unaddressed, including quantitative stability, metal ion regulation, and inhibitor-binding kinetics. To address these gaps, we used an integrated approach to investigate NSP15 regulation and inhibition. Thermochemical stability studies indicated moderate NSP15 stability, with cooperative unfolding characterized by a Cm of 1.68 M urea and a Tm of ∼70°C. Urea–PAGE activity measurements revealed a strong metal ion dependence, with Mn2+ as the optimal activator and marked stimulation compared with Ca2+, Mg2+, and Zn2+. Biophysical experiments using SPR and fluorescence quenching confirmed a direct protein–ligand interaction with dissociation constants of ∼1–4 μM. Consistent with these results, the compounds inhibited endoribonuclease activity with IC50 values of ∼8–30 μM. Alanine substitution of catalytic residues H235A and H250A completely abolished cleavage, while S294A within the B1 pocket, a uridine-specificity determinant, reduced activity by 51%–67% (10–50 nM), markedly weakened inhibitor binding, and increased inhibition susceptibility. Importantly, docking and simulation studies revealed stabilized active-site dynamics driven by strong polar interactions, as evidenced by solvent-accessible surface area, hydrogen-bonding, RMSD, RMSF, and radius of gyration (Rg) analyses, underscoring the coordinated contribution of polar contacts and hydrophobic interactions in the inhibitor-bound active-site conformation. Collectively, the present work provides quantitative, mutational, and functional characterization, forming a foundation for designing NSP15-specific antivirals.

title: Myelodysplastic syndrome after COVID-19 infection in a living-donor kidney transplant recipient: a case report and literature review
abstract: Abstract Background Myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS) after kidney transplantation is rare, and its association with coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) is unclear. Case report A 57-year-old man was treated with maintenance hemodialysis for end-stage kidney disease presumed to have been caused by chronic glomerulonephritis diagnosed 10 years earlier. After 1 year, he received an ABO-compatible living-donor kidney transplant from his sister. Renal graft function remained stable thereafter, with serum creatinine levels ranging from 1.49 to 1.62 mg/dL. Two years before presentation, he was hospitalized for COVID-19 that did not respond to oral molnupiravir but resolved after intravenous remdesivir therapy. However, following the COVID 19 infection, nucleated red blood cells and immature myeloid cells were persistently observed in his peripheral blood. Laboratory analyses showed hemoglobin 16.3 g/dL, white blood cell count 5700/μL, neutrophil count 2896/μL and platelet count 117,000/μL. Bone marrow aspiration revealed 1.4% myeloblasts, dysplastic erythroid cells with nuclear atypia, and megakaryocytes with poor platelet production and release, leading to a diagnosis of MDS. Cytogenetic analysis revealed trisomy 8, and Wilms’ tumor 1 messenger RNA (WT1 mRNA) expression was elevated to 690 copies/μgRNA, suggesting a risk of leukemic transformation. Although hematopoietic stem cell transplantation was considered because of his age, no suitable related donor was available, as the kidney donor sister had developed rheumatoid arthritis. Registration with the bone marrow donor program is currently under consideration. Conclusions We experienced a case of MDS diagnosed after COVID-19 in a kidney transplant recipient. Persistent appearance of immature blood cells after COVID-19 infection may warrant careful hematological evaluation in immunocompromised patients, including kidney transplant recipients.

title: Retrospective Prediction of COVID 19 Emergency Department Visits Using SARS CoV 2 Wastewater Activity
abstract: Aim: This registered retrospective study assessed whether SARS-CoV-2 wastewater activity improved prediction of COVID-19 emergency department visit percentages beyond recent clinical trends. Subject and Methods: Public CDC wastewater and aggregate emergency department data were extracted October 12, 2026. Expanding-window ordinary least squares models compared clinical history and seasonality with the same predictors plus three-week mean log wastewater activity. Paired one-week targets spanned July 5, 2025–September 12, 2026. Equal-state mean absolute error (MAE) improvement received a 95% hierarchical bootstrap interval. The outcome was a published aggregate clinical surveillance percentage. Results: Thirty-nine states contributed 2,383 paired predictions. Baseline and enhanced MAE averaged 0.09454 and 0.09139 percentage points. Improvement was 0.00315 percentage points (95% interval −0.00290 to 0.00968). Mean relative improvement was 3.68% (−2.69% to 11.73%), below the prespecified 10% benchmark. Longer-horizon and shifted-predictor intervals also crossed zero. Conclusion: The registered primary comparison did not establish improved prediction accuracy. These results use revised historical data and do not establish real-time forecasting performance or validated warning intervals.

source_records.title: Retrospective Prediction of COVID 19 Emergency Department Visits Using SARS CoV 2 Wastewater Activity
source_records.abstract: Aim: This registered retrospective study assessed whether SARS-CoV-2 wastewater activity improved prediction of COVID-19 emergency department visit percentages beyond recent clinical trends. Subject and Methods: Public CDC wastewater and aggregate emergency department data were extracted October 12, 2026. Expanding-window ordinary least squares models compared clinical history and seasonality with the same predictors plus three-week mean log wastewater activity. Paired one-week targets spanned July 5, 2025–September 12, 2026. Equal-state mean absolute error (MAE) improvement received a 95% hierarchical bootstrap interval. The outcome was a published aggregate clinical surveillance percentage. Results: Thirty-nine states contributed 2,383 paired predictions. Baseline and enhanced MAE averaged 0.09454 and 0.09139 percentage points. Improvement was 0.00315 percentage points (95% interval −0.00290 to 0.00968). Mean relative improvement was 3.68% (−2.69% to 11.73%), below the prespecified 10% benchmark. Longer-horizon and shifted-predictor intervals also crossed zero. Conclusion: The registered primary comparison did not establish improved prediction accuracy. These results use revised historical data and do not establish real-time forecasting performance or validated warning intervals.
