title: COVID-19 in the States
abstract: Abstract This chapter analyzes how the COVID-19 pandemic tested democratic capabilities at the subnational level. It argues that the crisis exposed not only core dimensions of state capacity but also the relational forms of power needed to secure public cooperation in highly unequal societies. It shows that national-level analyses overlook these dynamics by focusing narrowly on formal democracy and fixed bureaucratic resources, whereas the subnational level better captures how state agencies interact with civil society to coordinate high-touch health and welfare responses. It explains why state governments in India became the central actors during the pandemic and how political competition, state–society relations, and local institutions shaped state performance in health and welfare responses. These factors were key in mobilizing resources, inducing compliance, and mitigating inequalities. In doing so, the chapter demonstrates that subnational democratic capabilities are critical both for crisis response and for strengthening equitable state action more broadly.

title: The Broadly Neutralizing DEV_K57 Antibody, Isolated from a Convalescent Patient, in Complex with the SARS-CoV-2 RBD
abstract: The continuous evolution of SARS-CoV-2 necessitates broadly neutralizing antibodies for robust therapeutics. In this study, we isolated 1824 single B cells from a COVID-19 convalescent donor and obtained 91 pairs of nucleotide sequences potentially encoding VH/VL domains. From this library, we generated and evaluated a panel of 38 recombinant monoclonal antibodies. Among this panel, we identified DEV_K57 as a broadly neutralizing human IgG1 antibody targeting the SARS-CoV-2 RBD. DEV_K57 exhibited in vitro neutralization breadth against diverse variants, demonstrating subnanomolar IC50 values. This in vitro efficacy was translated in vivo. In a Syrian hamster model of SARS-CoV-2 Delta infection, DEV_K57 significantly reduced viral RNA and infectious titers in both the upper and lower respiratory tracts, conferring a favorable safety profile with minimal histopathological damage. To elucidate its mechanism, we performed comprehensive biophysical and structural analyses. Biolayer interferometry revealed a high picomolar binding affinity to the RBD Delta. Furthermore, size-exclusion chromatography coupled with small-angle X-ray scattering and computational modeling uncovered a unique, stable dimeric architecture of the DEV_K57 Fab-RBD complex in solution, with a binding interface distinct from previously characterized structures. These findings underscore the value of rapid antibody isolation for pandemic preparedness against future emerging biological threats.

title: The Impact of the COVID-19 Pandemic on the Epidemiology of Candidemia and the Distribution of Candida Species
abstract: Candidemia is a critical bloodstream infection with high mortality rates, particularly in intensive care units. Several studies have reported an increase in the incidence of candidemia in intensive care units (ICUs) and changes in distribution of causative Candida species during the COVID-19 pandemic. This retrospective study aims to evaluate changes in the distribution of Candida species isolated from blood cultures from ICUs in the Medical Microbiology Laboratory of Yalova Training and Research Hospital in the periods before (2016–2019) and after (2020–2024) the COVID-19 pandemic. Blood cultures were incubated using the Render BC128 and DL-Bt 112 automated blood culture systems; species identification was performed using the VITEK® automated identification system in both periods. Analyses revealed a statistically significant increase in the isolation rate of Candida albicans in post-pandemic period (from 65.2% to 84.0%; p=0.033) and a significant decrease in isolation rate of Candida parapsilosis (from 15.2% to 2.0%; p=0.019). No significant differences were observed in other Candida species. Data indicate that COVID-19 pandemic has led to a significant change in species distribution of candidemia agents. In particular, increase in isolation frequency of C. albicans and the significant decrease in C. parapsilosis point to the need to review clinical management approaches and empirical antifungal treatment strategies. It is thought that changes in infection control practices and differentiations in patient profiles and intensive care dynamics during pandemic may have influenced this distribution. Our findings once again emphasize importance of regular surveillance, rapid species-level diagnostic methods, and antifungal susceptibility monitoring in clinical practice for candidemia.

title: Fraud and corruption in emergency grant funding: lessons from South Africa's COVID-19 relief and an agenda for research
abstract: Emergency relief is particularly exposed to fraud and corruption because funds must be disbursed quickly, often without adequate mechanisms to verify the legitimacy of intended beneficiaries. This review article examines that risk through South Africa's response to the COVID-19 pandemic, whose support package was estimated at R500 billion. Based on a narrative review of academic literature, official sources and documented cases, the article does not report primary empirical data. It first sets out a conceptual framework that brings together deterrence theory, the moral hazard inherent in grant funding, the weak controls typical of under-resourced non-profit organisations and the tension between speed and control in emergencies. It then synthesises the published evidence on the South African case: the special COVID-19 Social Relief of Distress (SRD) grant administered by the South African Social Security Agency (SASSA), salary-related and identity-related fraud, abuses of the Unemployment Insurance Fund's Temporary Employer-Employee Relief Scheme (TERS), and the exclusion of informal workers. Next, it examines the social and economic consequences for beneficiaries described in the literature. The article offers anti-fraud governance recommendations organised around prevention, detection and response, and proposes a research agenda built on a qualitative case study with real interviews of beneficiaries, officials and experts. It concludes that fraud will only be durably reduced if grant providers and implementing organisations jointly build an anti-fraud culture that is visible in day-to-day work.

title: Strategi Kampanye Komunikasi Publik Satgas Covid-19 Nasional dalam Penanganan Covid-19
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia generated significant impacts on public health and the national economy, reflected in rising confirmed cases, economic contraction, and increasing unemployment resulting from physical distancing policies. These conditions required society to adapt to new behavioral norms through structured and effective public communication. This study aims to analyze the public communication campaign strategy implemented by the National COVID-19 Task Force in managing the pandemic and to identify the supporting and inhibiting factors influencing its implementation. The research employed a qualitative approach within a constructivist paradigm using a case study design. Data were collected through in-depth interviews with the public communication division and community members and were analyzed interpretatively. The findings indicate that the campaign strategy was systematically designed with informative and persuasive objectives to enhance public awareness and encourage behavioral change. Messages were science-based and delivered by credible communicators with authentic voices. Furthermore, stakeholder mapping was conducted to strengthen collaborative support, contributing to the development of active and sustainable public participation in pandemic management.

The research employed a qualitative approach within a constructivist paradigm using a case study design. Data were collected through in-depth interviews with the public communication division and community members and were analyzed interpretatively. The findings indicate that the campaign strategy was systematically designed with informative and persuasive objectives to enhance public awareness and encourage behavioral change. Messages were science-based and delivered by credible communicators with authentic voices. Furthermore, stakeholder mapping was conducted to strengthen collaborative support, contributing to the development of active and sustainable public participation in pandemic management.

title: The clinical and economic effects of cancelled or delayed ECT treatment during the COVID-19 pandemic: A scoping review
abstract: Introduction Electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) is a highly effective and essential treatment for patients suffering from severe mental illness, including treatment-resistant depression and catatonia. Delaying ECT treatment leads to worsening symptoms, which require more repeat ECT treatments for patients to recover, and increases wait times for others. During the COVID-19 pandemic, many ECT facilities significantly reduced or cancelled their ECT services. The overall clinical and economic effects of these delayed and cancelled ECT treatments are unknown. Methods We conducted a scoping review of studies assessing the clinical and economic effects of missed or cancelled ECT treatment during the COVID-19 pandemic among patients ≥ 18 years. We searched MEDLINE, Embase, and PsycINFO (inception to March 2024). Three independent reviewers performed screening and extracted data. Results were summarized narratively. Results Of 365 articles screened, a total of 11 articles met eligibility criteria for inclusion in this review. There was consistent evidence across all included studies to suggest that cancelling and reducing ECT treatment was associated with patient relapse, hospitalization, and need for new treatment. Only one of the included studies reported economic outcomes, with the findings suggesting that cancelled and reduced ECT led to significantly increased healthcare costs. Conclusion Our findings highlight that delaying access to critical services, such as ECT, can result in negative clinical outcomes and greater healthcare spending. ECT facilities should prioritize maintaining access to treatment, both presently and during future emergencies, especially for patients with the greatest need, such as those with treatment-resistant disorders or who require more frequent ECT treatments.

title: Transfer Learning CNN for BRCA1 Gene Variant Classification Using a SARS-CoV-2 Detection Architecture
abstract: This study aims to develop a one-dimensional Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) using Transfer Learning to classify BRCA1 gene variants into Benign and Pathogenic classes based on their clinical significance. Method: BRCA1 variants obtained from ClinVar were processed into 200 bp DNA sequence windows centered on the variant position and transformed using One-Hot Encoding into 200 × 4 representations. The CNN was trained through three stages: pretraining, Transfer Learning with frozen convolutional layers, and Fine-Tuning. Model performance was evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, specificity, F1-score, ROC-AUC, and confusion matrix. Results: The final model achieved 84.70% accuracy, 85.28% precision, 85.70% recall, 83.59% specificity, 85.49% F1-score, and 91.50% ROC-AUC on 4,588 unseen test sequences. Fine-Tuning increased training accuracy from 90.27% to 90.92%, with a best validation accuracy of 85.03%. Novelty: This study demonstrates the adaptation of a CNN architecture previously applied to SARS-CoV-2 detection for BRCA1 DNA sequence classification. The findings indicate that the adapted architecture can learn meaningful sequence patterns and provide a promising computational approach for BRCA1 variant classification.
journal: Journal of Electrical Engineering and Informatics

title: Performance Analysis of CNN and LSTM for SARS-CoV-2 Detection Based on Genomic Sequence Data
abstract: This study compares the performance of Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) architecture implemented with a bidirectional configuration for binary SARS-CoV-2 detection from genomic sequence data. A total of 8,273 sequences were programmatically retrieved from NCBI, comprising 2,000 SARS-CoV-2 sequences and 6,273 sequences from other viruses. Sequences were standardized to 30,000 bases through padding or truncating and transformed using one-hot encoding. A stratified split produced 5,977 training, 1,055 validation, and 1,241 test samples. Because the experimental generator processed only complete batches of 32, final evaluation covered 1,216 of the 1,241 test samples; 25 samples that did not form a complete batch were not included in the reported metric calculations. Both models used Adam, binary cross-entropy, a maximum of 10 epochs, and EarlyStopping. CNN achieved 99.75% accuracy, 98.99% precision, 100% recall, 99.49% F1-score, and 1.0000 ROC-AUC, with 3 misclassifications. LSTM achieved 97.04% accuracy, 94.48% precision, 93.20% recall, 93.84% F1-score, and 0.9953 ROC-AUC, with 36 misclassifications. CNN required 399 seconds for training and 8 seconds for prediction, compared with 3,157 and 29 seconds for LSTM. The contribution is a controlled head-to-head comparison under a shared genomic preprocessing and training pipeline. The observed classification-efficiency advantage of CNN is specific to the dataset, implemented architectures, Google Colab/NVIDIA T4 hardware environment, and training configuration used in this experimental run and should not be interpreted as universal superiority over recurrent architectures.
journal: Journal of Electrical Engineering and Informatics

title: Structural basis for the broad-spectrum inhibition of the coronavirus main protease by Zevotrelvir.
abstract: Beta-coronaviruses have caused three major coronavirus outbreaks, underscoring the urgent need for broad-spectrum antivirals. The coronavirus main protease (M pro ) is an ideal drug target due to its high conservation and absence of human homologs. Zevotrelvir (EDP-235) is an oral M pro inhibitor with broad-spectrum activity against betacoronaviruses, but its molecular mechanism remains unclear. Here, we systematically evaluated Zevotrelvir against SARS-CoV-2 M pro and its mutants (G15S, M49I, K90R, S144A), as well as SARS-CoV and MERS-CoV M pro , using enzyme activity assays, crystallography, and molecular dynamics simulations. Zevotrelvir potently inhibited SARS-CoV-2 M pro (IC 50 = 23 nM) and maintained micromolar activity against mutants and other coronaviruses. Structural analysis revealed that Zevotrelvir forms a conserved covalent bond with the catalytic C145 (C148 in MERS-CoV) via its nitrile warhead, while its spirolactam and trifluoroindole groups occupy the S1', S1, S2, and S4 subsites through an E166-centered hydrogen bond network and hydrophobic interactions. Notably, conformational asymmetry was observed within the M pro dimer, with the trifluoroindole moiety rotating ~80° in protomer B. Molecular dynamics simulations confirmed complex stability and identified the key hydrogen bonds. This study elucidates the molecular basis of Zevotrelvir's broad-spectrum inhibition, informing its clinical development and next-generation drug design.

title: Resistance to technological innovation: the case of teleconsultation before and during COVID-19
abstract: Purpose This study analyzes resistance to technological innovation in the healthcare field, focusing on the formal, long-term adoption of teleconsultation in medical practice, which became established during the COVID-19 pandemic. Different institutional studies on resistance to change were analyzed to evaluate their capacity to explain the phenomenon. Design/methodology/approach Qualitative interpretive research was conducted involving documentary research and interviews with professionals from public and private domains, including health regulation organizations and individual practitioners, to capture their understandings of the issue. Findings The results showed that the primary hindering factors were the need for physical examination, the risk of deteriorating remuneration conditions for doctors, and insufficient undergraduate training in telemedicine. Research limitations/implications Thus, the study infers that institutional logics of the same order can coexist, accommodating contradictions between them. Medical autonomy, a principle of democratic logic upheld by part of the professional community and the imperative of public health emergencies, characteristic of professional logic, provoked a rapid response, constituting the driving pressures for the adoption of teleconsultation. Originality/value Technological innovation tends to face resistance during implementation, but under favorable conditions, it becomes consolidated alongside the previous practice. Traditional professional logic resisted the introduction of the new logic represented by teleconsultation until confronted by the pandemic, when it was compelled to adapt to the circumstances.

title: Progressive IgG Agalactosylation in Severe COVID-19: What Drives G0 Enrichment? Comment on Vinicki et al. Longitudinal Changes in IgG N-glycome Are Associated with Disease Severity and Mortality in COVID-19 Patients. Viruses 2026, 18, 960
abstract: Progressive enrichment of agalactosylated IgG G0 glycoforms has been repeatedly associated with severe and fatal COVID-19. Similar hypogalactosylated IgG phenotypes have also been described in persistent viral infection, post-infectious immune-mediated disease, and autoimmunity, suggesting that these conditions converge on a broader pathological immune response pattern. Evidence from autoimmune and inflammatory conditions indicates that persistent inflammatory signaling can remodel B-cell and germinal-center glycosylation pathways, thereby reducing IgG Fc galactosylation. Despite the substantial literature documenting these changes across different pathological conditions, the upstream processes that initiate and sustain progressive G0 enrichment remain largely unresolved, and no unifying upstream mechanism has been established across these conditions. We suggest that xenosialylation may represent one upstream amplification mechanism. Exogenous N-glycolylneuraminic acid (Neu5Gc) can be incorporated into human glycoconjugates, while humans possess heterogeneous anti-Neu5Gc repertoires. During intense antiviral antibody production, Neu5Gc-bearing IgG could be recognized by pre-existing and/or evolving anti-Neu5Gc responses, promoting immune-complex formation, clearance, and inflammatory amplification. The model predicts a temporal sequence linking Neu5Gc-bearing antigen-specific IgG, anti-Neu5Gc repertoire engagement, xenoimmune inflammation, and subsequent G0 enrichment, providing a directly testable mechanistic framework.

title: Características clínicas dos pacientes infectados por SARS-COV-2 hospitalizados no Vale do São Lourenço (2020–2023) Clinical characteristics of patients infected with SARS-COV-2 hospitalized (2020–2023)
abstract: Introdução: A pandemia da COVID-19 impôs desafios substanciais aos sistemas de saúde, evidenciando a necessidade de caracterizar o perfil clínico dos pacientes hospitalizados para subsidiar o planejamento assistencial e a alocação de recursos. Objetivo: Descrever o perfil sociodemográfico, clínico e os desfechos de pacientes internados por COVID-19 no Vale do São Lourenço, Mato Grosso, entre janeiro de 2020 e dezembro de 2023. Materiais e métodos: Trata-se de estudo descritivo, observacional e retrospectivo, realizado em hospital municipal de referência regional. Foram incluídos pacientes residentes nos municípios de São Pedro da Cipa, Juscimeira, Dom Aquino e Jaciara, com diagnóstico confirmado por RT-PCR (detecção do RNA do SARS-CoV-2 por biologia molecular) ou por teste rápido de antígeno (TR-Ag), com identificação de proteínas virais em amostras de swab nasal ou nasofaríngeo. Excluíram-se registros com dados incompletos ou que não atenderam aos critérios de inclusão. A coleta foi realizada por meio do sistema Fiorilli Software, contemplando variáveis como idade, sexo, sinais e sintomas, tempo de internação, município de residência e desfecho. A análise estatística foi conduzida no Microsoft Excel 2020. Resultados e Discussão: Observou-se predominância do sexo masculino (n=106; 21,2%), especialmente na faixa etária de 50 a 69 anos. Os sintomas mais frequentes foram hipoxemia (n=155; 31,1%), astenia (n=117; 23,4%), tosse (n=115; 23,0%) e dispneia (n=102; 20,4%). A maioria dos pacientes apresentou quadro moderado a grave, com necessidade de transferência para Unidade de Terapia Intensiva em 29,5% dos casos (n=147). Foram registrados 21 óbitos no período analisado. Conclusão: Os achados evidenciam o predomínio de manifestações respiratórias e evolução clínica significativa, reforçando a importância da vigilância epidemiológica e da caracterização clínica para o aprimoramento de protocolos assistenciais e estratégias de saúde pública no enfrentamento da COVID-19.

Foram incluídos pacientes residentes nos municípios de São Pedro da Cipa, Juscimeira, Dom Aquino e Jaciara, com diagnóstico confirmado por RT-PCR (detecção do RNA do SARS-CoV-2 por biologia molecular) ou por teste rápido de antígeno (TR-Ag), com identificação de proteínas virais em amostras de swab nasal ou nasofaríngeo. Excluíram-se registros com dados incompletos ou que não atenderam aos critérios de inclusão. A coleta foi realizada por meio do sistema Fiorilli Software, contemplando variáveis como idade, sexo, sinais e sintomas, tempo de internação, município de residência e desfecho. A análise estatística foi conduzida no Microsoft Excel 2020. Resultados e Discussão: Observou-se predominância do sexo masculino (n=106; 21,2%), especialmente na faixa etária de 50 a 69 anos. Os sintomas mais frequentes foram hipoxemia (n=155; 31,1%), astenia (n=117; 23,4%), tosse (n=115; 23,0%) e dispneia (n=102; 20,4%). A maioria dos pacientes apresentou quadro moderado a grave, com necessidade de transferência para Unidade de Terapia Intensiva em 29,5% dos casos (n=147). Foram registrados 21 óbitos no período analisado. Conclusão: Os achados evidenciam o predomínio de manifestações respiratórias e evolução clínica significativa, reforçando a importância da vigilância epidemiológica e da caracterização clínica para o aprimoramento de protocolos assistenciais e estratégias de saúde pública no enfrentamento da COVID-19.

title: Bronchoscopy and tracheostomy in COVID-19 patients
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic led to an unprecedented surge in critically ill patients, 5 to 20% of whom required invasive mechanical ventilation.Mortality in this group was substantial, and survivors often faced prolonged hospital stays.In this context, bronchoscopy became an invaluable tool for both the diagnosis and management of severe complications in the Intensive Care Unit.Bronchoalveolar lavage demonstrated greater diagnostic sensitivity than nasopharyngeal swabs.However, as an aerosol-generating procedure, bronchoscopy was strictly classified as either urgent or elective, with an emphasis on protecting healthcare personnel, preventing cross-transmission, and optimizing resource utilization.Tracheostomy was subject of considerable debate regarding its timing.During the pandemic, it was recommended to delay the procedure for 14 to 21 days to allow viral load and the risk of transmission to decrease.The procedure played a strategic role in facilitating ventilator weaning, reducing the need for deep sedation, and improving critical care bed turnover.Safety was reinforced through protocols that included planned periods of apnea during key surgical steps and close coordination between the anesthesia and surgical teams.The health crisis reshaped respiratory management, underscoring the importance of a multidisciplinary approach focused on protecting both patients and healthcare professionals.
journal: NCT Neumología y Cirugía de Tórax (English Edition)

title: Individual Resilience as Human Capital Stock: Neighborhood Social Capital, Environmental Perceptions, and Dynamic Pathways Across COVID-19 Phases
abstract: This study, grounded in the social ecological theories, investigates how the pathways linking neighborhood relationships, perceived environmental quality (PEQ), and individual resilience (IR) differed between the COVID-19 pandemic and the post-pandemic period. The empirical focus is on Chinese international students (CIS) in the UK, who experienced a unique form of “double exclusion” during the pandemic. Multi-phase data collection was conducted through questionnaire survey using a pre-then-post design ( n = 146). Specifically, exploratory factor analysis (EFA) was conducted to validate the dimensions of resilience as a contextual and dynamic construct, followed by a higher-order mediation model using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) to explore relationships between main latent constructs both during the pandemic and its aftermath. EFA confirmed sample adequacy (KMO > 0.9, Bartlett’s test p < 0.001) and validated the identification of first-order latent constructs for IR. Findings from PLS-SEM analysis revealed that during the pandemic, both structural and functional dimensions of neighborhood relationship were associated with IR through distinct mediation effects of PEQ. In the post-pandemic period, however, the pattern of associations differed: the mediation effect of PEQ on the relationship between structural neighborhood ties and IR was no longer significant, while PEQ remained a full mediator in the relationship between functional dimensions of neighborhood relationship and IR. These findings highlight the dynamic nature of IR as a stock of human capital. Neighborhood-based social capital functions as the primary investment, while perceived environmental quality acts as the efficiency channel through which this investment is translated into resilience outcomes. This interpretation offers an account of how resilience protection and accumulation may differ between crisis and post-crisis contexts.

title: Both sides of the CEO-to-employee pay ratio: evidence from the COVID-19 pandemic
abstract: Purpose Given that pay ratios did not decline following the Dodd-Frank disclosure mandate, we investigate how investors interpret these disclosures across normal and crisis periods. Exploiting the Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic to highlight variation in managerial talent and ability, we assess whether high pay ratios reflect efficient contracting or managerial opportunism and examine links to performance and chief executive officer (CEO) power. Design/methodology/approach We examine market reaction to CEO-to-employee pay ratio disclosures for S&P 1500 firms for 2018–2021. Using the COVID-19 pandemic as a macroeconomic shock, we define the event date as the Definitive Proxy Statement (Schedule 14A) (DEF 14A) filing and estimate a panel model with firm fixed effects. We control for firm, CEO, and industry characteristics and incorporate both traditional and social media sentiments as additional controls for the broader information environment surrounding proxy filings. Cross-sectional and robustness tests further distinguish between optimal contracting and rent-extraction explanations. Findings While announcement-period returns were negatively associated with pay ratios in 2018, this relation weakens and disappears during the COVID-19 period. This evidence is consistent with the possibility that investors place relatively greater weight on managerial ability considerations during the COVID-19 period, although the event-study design does not fully isolate the pay ratio component from other contemporaneous proxy disclosures. Firms with higher pay ratios exhibit stronger operating performance and higher valuation, particularly during the pandemic. Positive market reactions remain strongest in large firms and in firms with weaker CEO power. Originality/value This paper is the first to examine market reactions to pay ratio disclosures during the COVID-19 shock, providing a setting that sharpens identification between competing theories. It also links pay ratio levels to broader issues of employee treatment and within-firm inequality, offering a novel and integrated perspective on what high pay ratios reveal about managerial ability and firm dynamics.

title: ‘Reaching and Teaching’: Understanding the Supercomplexity of Primary Teachers’ Work in an Area of High Social Deprivation During the COVID-19 Pandemic
abstract: Abstract This chapter explores the supercomplexity of primary teachers’ work in four northern English schools serving communities of high social deprivation during the COVID-19 pandemic. Based on a multiple case study, it shows how teachers’ safeguarding, pastoral and welfare roles expanded during the pandemic, requiring sustained family engagement amid overlapping social, economic and digital disadvantage and in response to shifting policy guidance. Framed by Barnett’s (2000a) notion of supercomplexity, the analysis identifies five overlapping themes: evolving definitions of vulnerability, mediating learning through homes, the emotional labour of care, rapid pedagogical and organisational adaptation and re-evaluation of educational aims beyond high-stakes accountability. While teachers demonstrated remarkable adaptability; developing hybrid provision, restructuring Early Years pedagogy and prioritising wellbeing, the moral weight of this labour remained largely unrecognised in policy. This chapter argues for teacher education and system design that centre adaptability, relational care and professional judgement, positioning teachers as co-constructors of educational meaning and essential agents in building resilience for future crises.
journal: Schools and Families on the Frontline

title: Widening the Gap? The Impact of COVID-19 Restrictions on Education for Students With Special Educational Needs and Disabilities in an English Special School
abstract: Abstract This study explores how COVID-19 restrictions impacted on the provision of education for children and young people with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND), from the point of view of four parents and the headteacher at a special school in the North of England. Thematic analysis of the data through Bronfenbrenner’s bioecological theory and Biesta’s domains of education contextualised the effects of school closures and policies on the people and systems that students engage with, as well as how they both interact with one another. While existing research has largely examined the impact of school closures and remote learning, this case study highlights the critical role of specialist provision in supporting families and maintaining student wellbeing. Findings reveal how the pandemic exacerbated existing inequalities and exposed the marginalisation of SEND learners within policy and practice. The study calls for a radical reframing of education through a social model of disability, advocating for inclusive environments and pedagogies. Although focused on only one special school, insights offer valuable lessons for mainstream and specialist settings alike. Wellbeing must be embedded in educational policy and practice to better support all learners moving forward.

title: Reimagining Secondary Schools as a Result of the COVID-19 Pandemic: A Qualitative Study
abstract: Abstract This chapter reports the findings of a qualitative study that set out to examine the experiences and priorities of English state-funded secondary schools during the COVID-19 pandemic. It considers how historical and contemporary policy eras have shaped the capacities of schools to respond to the challenges posed by the pandemic. Research took place within three schools with different types of governance: an inner-city new build that is part of a multi-academy trust, a Faith School and a Maintained School. It purposively recruited staff across a range of roles (senior leader, teaching and non-teaching support) to gain a complete picture of school approaches. Findings were as follows: going into the pandemic, each school identified challenges around staff recruitment, budgetary pressures, social deprivation and an increasing special educational needs and disabilities register. In the early days of school closure, schools utilised their existing pastoral structures to support children and families with varying degrees of success. As the pandemic evolved, all staff found themselves taking on new activities outside of their remit, which enabled a better understanding of the families and communities that they served. The authors conclude that in taking almost total responsibility for the welfare of pupils and their families during the pandemic, participating schools – whatever their governance – continued to resist neoliberal-driven educational policy that focuses purely on the classroom and excellent teaching. Learning from the pandemic suggests that there is a strong case to re-imagine schools as integral to communities and furthermore, that there is an appetite to achieve this.

title: Epidemiología del SARS-CoV-2 en la práctica odontológica: transmisión, carga viral salival y bioseguridad Epidemiology of SARS-CoV-2 in dental practice: transmission, salivary viral load and biosafety
abstract: Objetivo: sintetizar la evidencia sobre la transmisión del SARS-CoV-2 en la práctica odontológica, la carga viral salival y las medidas de bioseguridad. Método: revisión sistemática con síntesis narrativa en PubMed y SciELO (2012-2025); se incluyeron 15 estudios. Resultados: la saliva y los aerosoles de los procedimientos odontológicos son vías relevantes de transmisión. La detección molecular del virus en saliva respalda su papel como reservorio y como muestra diagnóstica. Los colutorios antisépticos reducen el virus in vitro, pero su efecto clínico sobre la carga viral salival es limitado. El triaje, la protección personal, el control de aerosoles y la teleodontología fueron las medidas centrales. Conclusión: la bioseguridad debe mantenerse como norma permanente.

title: Decomposing the decline in life expectancy at birth by cause of death during the COVID-19 pandemic in Canada
abstract: Background: Life expectancy at birth has increased in Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development countries and across the globe over the past few decades, until 2019. However, this trend was disrupted by the COVID-19 pandemic, which saw a significant decrease in life expectancy in Canada and many other countries. Few studies to date have decomposed the life expectancy gap by cause of death observed during the pandemic in a Canadian context. Data and methods: Death counts were generated from the Canadian Vital Statistics - Death database. Life tables were created using Chiang's method. The Arriaga method for decomposing a life expectancy gap was implemented by comparing life tables between the periods of 2017 to 2019 and 2020 to 2022 by province and sex. Results: COVID-19 was the single largest contributor to the life expectancy decline in Canada between the periods of 2017 to 2019 and 2020 to 2022, reducing life expectancy at birth by 0.46 years for both sexes. Opioid-related deaths, another significant contributor to the life expectancy decline, reduced life expectancy by 0.22 years for both sexes. By contrast, cancers contributed to a slight increase (+0.17 years) in life expectancy between the two periods. Interpretation: Although COVID-19 was the most significant driving force in declining life expectancy during the pandemic in Canada, increased opioid-related deaths, potentially related to the indirect effects of the pandemic, also played a significant role in the notable life expectancy decline. A greater understanding of the indirect impacts of the COVID-19 pandemic in terms of mortality, including the harms related to substance use and abuse, will be possible as more information on the causes and circumstances of death is made available.

By contrast, cancers contributed to a slight increase (+0.17 years) in life expectancy between the two periods. Interpretation: Although COVID-19 was the most significant driving force in declining life expectancy during the pandemic in Canada, increased opioid-related deaths, potentially related to the indirect effects of the pandemic, also played a significant role in the notable life expectancy decline. A greater understanding of the indirect impacts of the COVID-19 pandemic in terms of mortality, including the harms related to substance use and abuse, will be possible as more information on the causes and circumstances of death is made available.

title: Pacientes con COVID-19 grave en cuidados intensivos: revisión narrativa Patients with severe COVID-19 in intensive care: a narrative review
abstract: Objetivo: analizar las características clínicas, la mortalidad, los factores de riesgo y los tratamientos de los pacientes con COVID-19 grave ingresados en unidades de cuidados intensivos. Método: revisión narrativa de literatura indexada en PubMed y SciELO; se seleccionaron 15 documentos: cohortes, un metaanálisis y ensayos clínicos aleatorizados. Resultados: en Europa, cerca de tres cuartas partes de los pacientes críticos eran varones y la mitad tenía hipertensión. La mortalidad en cuidados intensivos descendió del 60 % al 36 % durante 2020, pero en América Latina alcanzó el 59 % en Brasil y el 47,8 % en Medellín. La edad, la diabetes, la obesidad y la hipoxemia grave aumentaron el riesgo de muerte. La dexametasona, el tocilizumab y la posición prona en pacientes despiertos mejoraron los desenlaces. Conclusión: el pronóstico depende de la gravedad al ingreso y de la aplicación de tratamientos con eficacia demostrada.

title: Alteraciones hepáticas en pacientes con COVID-19 y estrategias terapéuticas: revisión narrativa Liver abnormalities in patients with COVID-19 and therapeutic strategies: a narrative review
abstract: Objetivo: describir la frecuencia, el significado pronóstico y el manejo terapéutico de las alteraciones hepáticas en pacientes con COVID-19. Método: revisión narrativa de la literatura indexada en PubMed y SciELO entre 2020 y 2022; se seleccionaron 15 documentos: seis estudios observacionales, cinco revisiones y cuatro ensayos clínicos aleatorizados. Resultados: la alteración de las pruebas hepáticas osciló entre el 14 % y más del 50 % de los pacientes hospitalizados, predominó la elevación de aminotransferasas y fue más frecuente en la enfermedad grave. En la India, la mortalidad fue del 19,6 % con disfunción hepática frente al 2,1 % sin ella. La dexametasona redujo la mortalidad en pacientes con oxígeno o ventilación; lopinavir/ritonavir, hidroxicloroquina e interferón no mostraron beneficio. Conclusión: las alteraciones hepáticas son frecuentes y suelen ser transitorias, pero señalan mayor gravedad; su manejo exige vigilancia bioquímica y ajuste de fármacos potencialmente hepatotóxicos.

title: Mechanical ventilation in COVID-19
abstract: COVID-19 can progress to a critical condition with acute respiratory distress syndrome, characterized by alveolar collapse, exudative infiltrate with an intense inflammatory response, which can progress to biotrauma and multiple organ failure.In cases of severe respiratory failure refractory to oxygen therapy or non-invasive support, invasive mechanical ventilation is indicated based on clinical and blood gas analysis criteria.This constitutes a life-support therapy aimed at maintaining gas exchange while pulmonary recovery occurs.During the pandemic, different COVID-19 phenotypes with respiratory compromise were described, ranging from relatively preserved compliance and predominantly impaired perfusion (phenotype L) to presentations like classic acute respiratory distress syndrome with high elastance, pulmonary edema, and greater recruitment potential (phenotype H).These phenotypes can evolve dynamically, which explains the clinical heterogeneity and the variable response to interventions such as prone positioning.Initial ventilation programming should be individualized, usually using volume-controlled modes, and continuous monitoring, including static and dynamic variables; this is essential for ventilatory optimization and reducing ventilator-induced lung injury.Furthermore, alveolar recruitment and prone positioning are key strategies in moderate to severe respiratory distress syndrome, with evidence of reduced mortality when implemented early and for an extended period.
journal: NCT Neumología y Cirugía de Tórax (English Edition)

title: Cardiovascular complications of COVID-19
abstract: SARS-CoV-2 infection is associated with a broad spectrum of cardiovascular manifestations that significantly increase morbidity and mortality.Acute myocardial injury, detected by elevated cardiac troponins, occurs in 10-25% of hospitalized patients and serves as an independent predictor of mortality, particularly in critically ill patients and those with pre-existing cardiovascular disease.Acute complications include acute myocarditis, rhythm disorders, heart failure, and cor pulmonale.The pathophysiology is multifactorial, involving direct viral damage via ACE2 receptors, oxygen supply-demand mismatch, and the "cytokine storm."In the post-acute phase (≥ 4 weeks), an elevated risk of arrhythmic events, heart failure, and coagulation disorders persists.The cardiovascular safety profile of current antiviral and immunomodulatory therapies varies, ranging from an increased risk of arrhythmias to a reduction in long-term cardiac complications.Cardiovascular complications of COVID-19 are frequent and heterogeneous.Close monitoring of biomarkers and echocardiographic evaluation are essential for timely management, both in the critical stage and during the long-term follow-up of survivors.
journal: NCT Neumología y Cirugía de Tórax (English Edition)

title: An Analysis of Hospital Capacity and Available Data during the COVID-19 Pandemic
abstract: Abstract Introduction One of the major concerns throughout the COVID-19 pandemic was whether health facilities had sufficient capacity to meet demands for care. Many states used healthcare capacity metrics to make decisions about the implementation of population-based disease mitigation measures. Methods Using facility-level data from the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services to examine hospital capacity and bed availability over the course of the COVID-19 pandemic, we calculated inpatient occupancy rates for hospitalizations of all-causes and COVID-19 and compared them across states, counties and on the national level. Results We found that in the aggregate, the national supply of staffed inpatient beds remained relatively constant during the pandemic despite the repeated stress of multiple COVID-19 waves. However, there was substantial heterogeneity among states and counties. Nationally, there was little association between the total availability of staffed hospital beds and reported COVID-19 cases. Conclusion Understanding how hospital capacity responds to pandemic waves is essential for future pandemic preparedness. Improved data systems, clearer staffed bed definitions and strategic capacity management are essential to ensure health systems can handle other health threats.

title: Clinical utility of procalcitonin testing in critically Ill COVID-19 patients: a two-center retrospective cohort study
abstract: Procalcitonin (PCT) is particularly sensitive to bacterial infections due to its response to specific bacterial cytokines. Even though viruses generally do not induce these cytokines, PCT levels are frequently ordered for viral infections in practice. However, among patients with COVID-19, it remains unclear whether baseline PCT measurements or change in PCT levels overtime are strongly associated with bacterial co-infection and clinical outcomes. Therefore, this study evaluated the association between baseline and dynamic procalcitonin (PCT) levels and microbiological and clinical outcomes in critically ill patients with COVID-19. A two-center retrospective cohort study included adult critically ill patients with COVID-19 who were hospitalized in intensive care units (ICUs) between March 2020 and December 2021. Eligible patients were divided into two sub-cohorts: those with PCT values < 0.25 ng/mL and those with values ≥ 0.25 ng/mL. The primary outcome was the rate of positive bacterial and fungal cultures within five days. Propensity score (PS) matching with a 1:1 ratio was used. Regression analyses were performed as appropriate. PCT monitoring was performed as part of routine clinical care rather than under a standardized prospective protocol, and dynamic PCT analyses were therefore based on clinically obtained follow-up values within the predefined window. A total of 553 patients were included. After PS matching, 184 patients were included in each group. Patients who had a baseline PCT ≥ 0.25 had higher odds for the positivity of bacterial and fungal cultures; however, this was not statistically significant (OR 1.36 (CI 0.75, 2.45); p-value = 0.29 and OR 2.07 (CI 0.60, 7.11); p-value = 0.24, respectively). In the subgroup analysis based on the change in PCT from baseline, 30-day mortality was significantly higher in the PCT increase group in both the crude and regression analyses (40.4% vs. 25%; p-value = 0.02 and OR 2.07 (CI 1.08, 3.92); p-value = 0.02, respectively). Our findings show that dynamic increases in procalcitonin correlate with higher mortality rates and poorer outcomes, while baseline PCT did not show a statistically significant association with early microbiological outcomes, limiting its utility as a stand-alone marker of bacterial or fungal co-infection. These findings support a cautious interpretation of PCT in critically ill COVID-19 patients, with greater emphasis placed on its dynamic trends rather than baseline values alone.

title: A Review of Changing Patterns of Pediatric Respiratory Infections in the Pre- and Post-COVID-19 Era: A Global and Indian Perspective
abstract: Respiratory tract infections remain an important cause of illness in children, and their epidemiology has changed noticeably during and after the COVID-19 pandemic. Non-pharmaceutical interventions, including masking, school closure, distancing, improved hand hygiene, and reduced travel, were associated with a fall in several common respiratory viruses, particularly influenza and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), while rhinovirus/enterovirus continued to circulate in many settings. After restrictions were relaxed, many countries reported delayed or out-of-season activity of RSV, influenza, human metapneumovirus, and other respiratory pathogens. Multiplex molecular platforms such as the BioFire Respiratory Panel have helped document these shifts by enabling rapid, simultaneous detection of multiple viral and bacterial agents. This narrative review summarizes pre-pandemic, pandemic, and post-pandemic respiratory pathogen patterns with emphasis on pediatric infections, global observations, and Indian data. It also discusses the role of immunity gaps, disrupted routine immunization, altered healthcare-seeking behavior, co-detection, and regional variation in India. Strengthening respiratory virus surveillance, improving access to multiplex diagnostics in sentinel centers, restoring routine immunization, and integrating influenza, RSV, and COVID-19 prevention strategies into pediatric public health planning are essential in the post-COVID period.

title: [Attitudes of school principals towards classroom ventilation in the Region of Murcia (Spain) after COVID-19].
abstract: Objective COVID-19 remains a highly communicable disease in poorly ventilated closed environments. In Spain, prevention guidelines on transmission in schools were developed, emphasizing the need for adequate ventilation. In the Region of Murcia, the last update of these guidelines was carried out in 2022. The objective of this research was to evaluate the attitudes and behaviors of the principals of public schools in this region towards preventive ventilation measures in classrooms after the end of the COVID-19 health emergency. The level of compliance with these measures during the 2023/24 academic year and the intentions to comply for the 2024/25 academic year were analyzed, as well as the factors that hinder and those that would help adequate ventilation. Methods A cross-sectional study was conducted between October 14 and November 15, 2024. Through email, and using the Microsoft Forms platform, the 518 directors of public schools in the Region of Murcia were contacted, finally obtaining 91 responses, which were analyzed quantitatively and qualitatively. Results 77% of schools lack HVAC systems or portable air purification devices and CO2 sensors. Regarding compliance with the recommendations, on a scale [0,1], an average of 0.71 was obtained for the 2023/24 academic year and 0.76 for 2024/25. Thermal comfort, external noise and scarce teacher collaboration were identified as the main limiting factors, while the need for more economic and material resources was identified as the essential element for improvement. Conclusions The principals of public schools in the Region of Murcia continue to show a favorable attitude and behavior towards classroom ventilation after the COVID-19 health emergency. However, there are severe obstacles to achieving better indoor air quality conditions in classrooms: most facilities lack HVAC systems or purifiers and CO2 meters, which makes it a constant challenge to maintain natural ventilation in the face of noise, lack of thermal comfort, and lack of awareness on the part of teachers, among other factors. Public investment in improving infrastructure is essential to make schools a much safer place against aerosol transmission of diseases.

title: Theological paradigms of Church-State relations in Zimbabwe during the COVID-19 pandemic
abstract: This article examines how models of church–state relations were expressed in Zimbabwe during the COVID-19 pandemic, using utilitarian reasoning as a key analytical lens. Drawing on theological, historical, legal, and social science sources, it considers four major paradigms: state-controlled church, church-controlled state, separation of church and state, and a symbiotic church–state relationship. Through a qualitative synthesis of official records, scholarly literature, and legal frameworks, the study analyses how pandemic governance shaped the interaction between religious institutions and the state, particularly in relation to public health measures, religious freedom, and institutional autonomy. The findings show that state control was dominant, marked by selective enforcement of regulations and the instrumental use of religious actors to support political authority. Framed within utilitarian thought, the article contributes to broader debates on church-state relations in Africa and highlights important theological implications for ecclesiology, human rights, and religious practice in times of crisis. Contribution: This article offers a unique scholarly contribution by providing a comprehensive theological analysis of church–state relationship models as manifested in Zimbabwe during the COVID-19 pandemic. It further interrogates the ethical and theological appropriateness of the predominant state-controlled church model, drawing on utilitarian arguments and examining the role of faith in public health. Utilitarian ethics is a moral philosophy that holds that the best action is the one that maximises overall happiness or well-being for the greatest number of people. It brings into conversation the Kairos document’s categories, State theology, Church theology, and Prophetic theology, highlighting their Zimbabwean manifestations and evaluating their suitability in pandemic governance. This critical engagement bridges gaps in literature by integrating ecclesiological theory with ethical analysis, offering new perspectives for theologians, sociologists, and policymakers on safeguarding religious rights, community welfare, and institutional integrity in times of emergency.

source_records.title: Theological paradigms of Church-State relations in Zimbabwe during the COVID-19 pandemic
source_records.abstract: This article examines how models of church–state relations were expressed in Zimbabwe during the COVID-19 pandemic, using utilitarian reasoning as a key analytical lens. Drawing on theological, historical, legal, and social science sources, it considers four major paradigms: state-controlled church, church-controlled state, separation of church and state, and a symbiotic church–state relationship. Through a qualitative synthesis of official records, scholarly literature, and legal frameworks, the study analyses how pandemic governance shaped the interaction between religious institutions and the state, particularly in relation to public health measures, religious freedom, and institutional autonomy. The findings show that state control was dominant, marked by selective enforcement of regulations and the instrumental use of religious actors to support political authority. Framed within utilitarian thought, the article contributes to broader debates on church-state relations in Africa and highlights important theological implications for ecclesiology, human rights, and religious practice in times of crisis. title: Admission Acute Brain Dysfunction and In-ICU Mortality in a Single-Center Pre-Vaccination Romanian COVID-19 Cohort:A Retrospective Observational Analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Critically ill COVID-19 patients frequently develop organ dysfunction and acute brain dysfunction with features overlapping sepsis-associated encephalopathy (SAE). Real-world cohorts from Eastern European intensive care during the pre-vaccination period are scarce. METHODS: We retrospectively analysed 389 consecutive adults with RT-PCR-confirmed SARS-CoV-2 admitted to a single regional Romanian tertiary ICU during 2020-2021, entirely preceding population-level vaccination. Organ dysfunction was defined as admission SOFA≥2, and acute brain dysfunction was op-erationalised from admission Glasgow Coma Scale and neurological SOFA (the acute brain dysfunction [ABD] proxy). Associations with in-ICU mortality were examined descriptively, with pre-specified sensitivity analyses restricted to non-ventilated pa-tients to address sedation confounding. RESULTS: In-ICU mortality was 65.8%. The ABD proxy was present in 49.6% of the cohort; mortality was 96.9% in ABD-proxy-positive patients versus 45.9% in those with preserved consciousness, an absolute difference of 51.0 percentage points, which was of similar magnitude (49.4 points) in non-ventilated patients, arguing against sedation as the sole explanation. Higher inflammatory markers accompanied the ABD proxy, and the association between admission acute brain dys-function and mortality was consistent across analyses. CONCLUSIONS: Admission acute brain dysfunction was strongly associated with in-ICU mortality, and this association persisted in non-ventilated patients. The findings are descriptive associations within an extreme, single-center pre-vaccination cohort under surge conditions; they are not causal, and should not be generalised to vaccinated or contemporary critical care.

title: Riesgos laborales en profesionales de la salud bucal durante la pandemia de COVID-19: revisión sistemática Occupational risks among oral health professionals during the COVID-19 pandemic: a systematic review
abstract: Objetivo: sintetizar la evidencia sobre los riesgos laborales de los profesionales de la salud bucal durante la pandemia de COVID-19 y las medidas propuestas para controlarlos. Método: revisión sistemática con síntesis narrativa en PubMed y SciELO (2012-2025); se incluyeron 15 estudios: revisiones, ensayos clínicos, estudios transversales y retrospectivos. Resultados: el riesgo biológico por aerosoles, gotas y contacto estrecho fue el principal riesgo descrito, seguido de las exposiciones a sangre y punzocortantes y del riesgo psicosocial, con agotamiento profesional y percepción elevada de riesgo. Las medidas incluyeron triaje, equipos de protección, control de aerosoles y colutorios previos al procedimiento. Conclusión: la pandemia aumentó y diversificó los riesgos laborales en odontología, por lo que se requieren protocolos permanentes de bioseguridad y de protección de la salud mental.

title: Letter to the Editor: Coronavirus disease 2019, multisystem inflammatory syndrome, and children’s hearts: Finding answers with cardiac magnetic resonance imaging
abstract: The article refers to “Persistent long-term subclinical myocardial changes in multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children revealed by cardiac magnetic resonance and galectin-3” by OV et al published in the World Journal of Clinical Pediatrics , multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children (MIS-C) associated with coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) and its cardiovascular complications. MIS-C frequently causes cardiovascular complications, including coronary artery dilatation, low left ventricular (LV) ejection fraction, diastolic dysfunction, myocarditis, and pericardial effusion, decreases over time, usually resolving within 6-9 months after the disease onset. Echocardiographic evaluations reveal mild to moderate LV dysfunction, resolving within two weeks. Severe dysfunction normalizes after approximately 1.5 months. Global longitudinal strain proves valuable for detecting subclinical myocardial damage. Long-term effects based on cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (CMRI) data indicate the persistent myocardial edema and/or fibrosisupto12 months after the initialevent. Signs of interstitial fibrosis were found in 7.7% of patients during a one-year follow-up period. CMRI is an important additional method in the assessment of children who have experienced multisystem inflammatory syndrome in COVID-19, especially in patients with persistent symptoms or abnormal data from other cardiac findings.

title: Insights from wastewater surveillance of SARS-CoV-2 in skilled nursing facilities: comparing virus concentration methods for wastewater and correlating wastewater virus concentrations with clinical infections, Georgia, USA, 2022
abstract: ABSTRACT A pictographic representation of the text abstract showing wastewater and epidemiologic data flow and data integration. To understand the utility of healthcare facility-level wastewater surveillance (WWS) for severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), it is important to correlate wastewater SARS-CoV-2 RNA detection with the number of clinical infections. WWS for SARS-CoV-2 was performed at three skilled nursing facilities (SNFs) over 25 weeks. Electronegative membrane filtration (enMF) and Nanotrap® Magnetic Virus Particles (NP) virus concentration methods were compared. Extracts were tested by droplet digital polymerase chain reaction. Spearman's correlations (ρ) between wastewater virus RNA concentrations and infection counts were calculated. From split wastewater samples, enMF recovered higher SARS-CoV-2 RNA concentrations than NP. Combining data from all facilities, the median concentrations were 53.0 versus 38.6 gc/100 mL for enMF and NP, respectively (p = 0.001). Using enMF, correlations were moderate to strong at SNF A (ρ ranged 0.67–0.86, all p-values <0.001). Weak to moderate correlations may reflect the sampled manhole not representing the entire facility (SNF B, ρ ranged 0.47–0.72, p-values ranged <0.001–0.12) and longitudinal data gaps from summer heat and equipment maintenance (SNF C, ρ ranged 0.14–0.59, p-values ranged<0.01 to 0.52). WWS can be a valuable tool for tracking dynamics of SARS-CoV-2 infections in healthcare facilities.

title: COVID-19 vaccination and persistent post-COVID symptoms among primary health care users in a rural district of Albania: A cross-sectional study
abstract: Background: Long COVID remains a frequent consequence of SARS-CoV-2 infection, and vaccination may influence its occurrence and course. Evidence from primary health care in Southeastern Europe remains limited. We aimed to assess the association between COVID-19 vaccination status and persistent post-COVID symptoms among primary health care users. Methods: A cross-sectional study was conducted in March 2025 among 49 adult primary health care users in a predominantly rural area of northern Albania. A structured questionnaire recorded sociodemographic characteristics, COVID-19 and vaccination history, and persistent post-COVID symptoms. Groups were compared with Fisher’s exact and Mann–Whitney U tests, and odds ratios (OR) were adjusted for sex with the Mantel–Haenszel method. Results: Mean age was 50.1 ± 19.7 years and 57.1% were women; 34.7% reported previous COVID-19 and 40.8% were vaccinated. Among the 17 previously infected participants, infection preceded vaccination in most vaccinated participants. Long COVID was reported by 40.0% of vaccinated and 85.7% of unvaccinated participants (p = 0.134). Vaccinated participants reported fewer persistent symptoms (0.9 ± 1.2 vs. 2.1 ± 1.2; p = 0.046) and fewer neurological symptoms (10.0% vs. 85.7%; p = 0.004; sex-adjusted OR 0.10, 95% CI 0.01–0.90). Conclusions: In our study, COVID-19 vaccination, received mostly after infection, was associated with a lower burden of persistent symptoms, particularly neurological symptoms. Larger longitudinal studies are needed to confirm these findings.

title: Comparative effectiveness of proactive exposure management and illness-based exclusion strategies for COVID-19 in healthcare personnel.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether COVID-19 exposure management in healthcare personnel (HCP) reduced presenteeism, occupational exposures and cases, comparing contact tracing and self-reporting exposure to standard illness management (i.e. DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study. SETTING: Large academic medical center, ambulatory and acute care. PARTICIPANTS: HCP COVID-19 exposure and case records (N = 30,102) collected at the University of North Carolina Medical Center, March 2020 through June 2021. METHODS: Among COVID-positive HCP, we measured hours worked while infectious and symptomatic, onward exposures, and secondary cases caused. Using negative binomial regression, we estimated mean count differences for each outcome comparing contact-tracing and self-reporting to standard illness management. We calculated the "number of encounters needed" to prevent one additional outcome (e.g., single onward exposure) by multiplying count differences by the proportion of exposure management encounters that identified a case. RESULTS: Contact tracing and self-reporting exposures captured a higher proportion of asymptomatic cases (14 and 18%) than standard illness management (5%). Both strategies reduced infectious work time by ~8 hours and presenteeism by ~3.5 hours. We found large relative reductions in onward exposures (62% contact tracing, 66% self-report) and secondary cases (79%, 100%), but small absolute reductions. Preventing one secondary case required identifying >1,000 traced contacts or >350 self-reports. CONCLUSIONS: Compared with standard illness management, COVID-19 exposure management reduced infectious work time, presenteeism and onward exposures, but preventing secondary cases was highly inefficient. Layered with comprehensive institutional mitigation strategies, exposure management provided limited case prevention benefits. Presenteeism was common and remains an important healthcare safety challenge.

title: A novel model demonstrating that human immune cells promote multiorgan SARS-CoV-2 dissemination and human T cells limit anti-viral innate immunity
abstract: Introduction Despite extensive studies, many questions remain regarding the pathology and mechanisms behind Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19), and particularly on post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC). Methods Because existing mouse models cannot recapitulate human immune responses, we developed a human immune system (HIS) mouse model with physiologic expression of hACE2. Results and discussion After intranasal infection, persistent viral RNA was observed in multiple organs for 8 weeks, despite the generation of human SARS-CoV-2-specific T cell responses. Human immune cells increased the presence of viral RNA in the lung and non-pulmonary tissues. COVID-19-related pathology was recapitulated in the lungs, with fibrosis peaking at 14 days post-infection. Immune activation was detected in the lungs, hearts, intestines and brains of acutely infected mice and persisted at 8 weeks in the heart and lungs. The presence of human T cells correlated with attenuated innate antiviral transcriptional signatures in the lung, where a persisting cytotoxic mature CD4+ T cell population with JAK-STAT activation was enriched in infected mice. Thus, human T cells mount an antigen-specific but ultimately dysfunctional response, while paradoxically suppressing the innate interferon response, permitting chronic interferon activation and long-term persistence of viral RNA, recapitulating several immunologic and histopathologic features associated with PASC. This model will uniquely facilitate understanding of virus-human immune dynamics and therapeutic approaches to PASC-related immunological features.

title: COVID-19 as an Anthropological Challenge: Changes in the Behavioral Models of Chinese Society
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic has become one of the most significant global crises of the 21st century, affecting not only public health but also fundamental forms of human existence, social interaction, cultural continuity, and human relationship with nature. It has served as a powerful factor in accelerating the sociocultural moderniza-tion of Chinese society. This article examines the changes in behavioral models of Chinese society under the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic within the context of philosophical and anthropological knowledge. These patterns are analyzed across such dimensions as “human-being”, “human-society”, “human-self”, “human-culture”, and “human-nature”. It is shown the change in behavioral models have led to the emergence of a new type of “domestic existence”, the digitalization of interpersonal communication, a rethinking of social distanc-ing, the strengthening of collectivist values, the actualization of traditional culture in a new format, and in-creased environmental reflection.

title: Criminalisation and Covid-19: examining the use of the criminal law as a response to the pandemic
abstract: This thesis seeks to examine the use of the criminal law as a response to the Covid-19 pandemic in Scotland. The onset of the pandemic resulted in extraordinary restrictions on civil liberties, made enforceable through criminalisation of ordinary social activity. A wealth of academic literature exists on the proper scope and limits of the criminal law, seeking to identify principles to guide legislators in deciding what conduct should, or should not, be criminalised. It is therefore surprising that so little attention has been paid by criminal lawyers and theorists to this unprecedented expansion in the criminal law. These theoretical perspectives can provide a framework for examining criminalisation in this context: by providing a normative basis for analysing whether and how these offences might be justified, and against which to review how these were used in practice. Whilst the existence of these offences was itself significant, given the scope of their prohibitions, an account of Covid-19 criminalisation which focused only on the content of legislation would be an inherently limited one. The new offences created cannot be fully understood without seeking to understand the approach taken by those charged with their enforcement. To that end, empirical research has been undertaken in the form of a case review exercise authorised by the Crown Office and Procurator Fiscal Service. This provides the most comprehensive examination of the reporting and prosecution of these offences in Scotland which has been attempted to date. A number of trends emerge from this research, which are set out and analysed. The findings from the empirical research are then drawn together, along with insights from criminal law theory, to reflect upon how the rationale for criminalisation was understood, and to explore the implications for future practice.

title: A Phenomenological Inquiry into Post-Traumatic Growth Among Nurses Who Worked on the Frontline of COVID-19
abstract: Objective: Research has demonstrated significant adverse psychological outcomes among nurses working on the frontline during the COVID-19 pandemic. However, some nurses also experienced post-traumatic growth (PTG) while navigating these experiences. This study aimed to identify the key elements that facilitated PTG among nurses who worked on the frontline in the UK during the pandemic and to explore what nurses believed policymakers and practitioners could do to support growth in others negatively affected by frontline work. Methods: A qualitative design was used to explore participants’ subjective lived experiences. Twelve nurses who had worked closely with COVID-19 patients in UK hospitals were recruited through professional organisations, nursing support groups, professional and personal networks, participant snowballing, and NHS Staff Wellbeing Hubs. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews and analysed using Template Analysis, guided initially by an a priori coding template derived from existing PTG literature while allowing themes to emerge inductively from participants’ accounts. Results: Four top-level themes were identified: individual characteristics, coping strategies, organisational and environmental considerations, and interpersonal factors. Participants described reflective and self-aware qualities, compassion, advocacy, previous experiences of difficulty, and work-related characteristics as relevant to their experiences of growth. Coping mechanisms included boundary setting, mindfulness, avoidance, emotional numbness, and consideration of mortality. Organisational and environmental factors included camaraderie, moments of joy, opportunities for learning and development, good leadership, and access to psychological support. Interpersonal factors included professional and personal relationships, community acts of kindness, and appropriate psychological support. Participants also identified the importance of long-term support, improved access to psychological services, and changes to aspects of NHS culture. Conclusion: PTG among frontline nurses appears to involve an interaction between individual characteristics, coping strategies, relationships, and the organisational and environmental context. The findings suggest that support should be responsive to individual needs and should provide opportunities for nurses to process and make meaning of distressing experiences. Trauma-informed leadership, appropriate psychological support, and opportunities for reflection and debriefing may help support nurses following experiences of frontline work.
journal: Journal of Modern Nursing Practice and Research

title: A Crisis within a Crisis: COVID-19 and Democratic Governance in Five Democracies
abstract: Crises have long been a litmus test for the strengths and weaknesses of governance structures particularly for democracies whose institutions are supposed to-by virtue of their legitimacy-withstand the risk of both the unconventional outcomes of and responses to a crisis. The resilience of this dynamic is constantly being tested, especially when the crisis involves an invisible adversary that threatens public health. Therefore, the instruments of democratic legitimacy become an important unit of analysis in understanding how contemporary systems of pandemic governance navigate the sphere of tension in which legitimacy is not only continually negotiated but expected to survive-if not flourish. This dissertation aims to understand the implications of how these democratic pressures unfolded under the COVID-19 pandemic. From this analysis, the study found that stable democracies such as Canada, France, and New Zealand adopted stringent measures, whereas backsliding democracies like the United States and the United Kingdom adopted mild measures. On the public reaction side, the United States, France, and the United Kingdom demonstrated that persistent inequality shaped the public’s response to crisis measures more strongly than stringency levels. Most notably, democratic erosion in the case of the United States and the United Kingdom was closely associated with inequality, which in turn also conditioned the way in which the public reacted under the pressures of the pandemic.

title: Statistical distributions for O3 and NO2 in Campo Grande before, during, and after COVID-19: a comparative analysis
abstract: The main objective of this study was to identify the probability distributions that best fit ozone (O3) and nitrogen dioxide (NO2) concentrations in Campo Grande, Brazil, considering three distinct periods: pre-COVID-19 (2005–2019), COVID-19 (2020), and post-COVID-19 (2021–2025). Monthly concentrations were analyzed using Lognormal, Gamma, Weibull, Log-Logistic, and Gumbel probability distributions. Model performance was evaluated using graphical analyses and the Akaike Information Criterion (AIC), Bayesian Information Criterion (BIC), Kolmogorov–Smirnov (K–S), and Anderson–Darling (A–D) statistics. The extension of the dataset through 2025 provided a broader temporal basis for assessing whether the patterns observed during the pandemic persisted in subsequent years. Mean O3 concentrations were 260.17 DU, 265.87 DU, and 278.08 DU during the pre-COVID-19, COVID-19, and post-COVID-19 periods, respectively, whereas mean NO2 concentrations were 2.97 × 10 15 , 3.11 × 10 15 , and 3.20 × 10 15 molecules/cm 2 , respectively. The best-fitting probability distribution varied among periods and pollutants. During the post-COVID-19 period, the Weibull distribution showed the strongest overall support for both O3 and NO2. Overall, the extended analysis indicates that post-COVID-19 pollutant concentrations did not simply return to pre-pandemic mean levels. However, these temporal differences should not be attributed exclusively to the COVID-19 pandemic because meteorological variability, biomass burning, traffic, industrial emissions, and other factors may also influence atmospheric pollutant concentrations.

title: Assessment of the Association between Myocarditis (New-onset Heart Failure) and COVID-19 and COVID-19 Vaccination
abstract: Introduction: Myocarditis is a rare but significant cardiovascular complication that may occur after receiving COVID-19 vaccines, particularly in younger individuals. The majority of cases have been reported after receiving mRNA-based vaccines, while inactivated and viral vector-based vaccines have been associated with fewer occurrences. Despite this, myocarditis is much more common and results in a poorer prognosis following COVID-19 infection. However, the relationship between myocarditis post-vaccination and its potential mechanisms remains unclear due to limited information. Methods: This study investigated patients with myocarditis (new-onset heart failure) who had received the COVID-19 vaccine and those who had been infected with COVID-19 between March 2021 and March 2023 in Farshchian Cardiovascular Hospital in Hamedan. The data was analyzed using Stata version 14 software and Python. Results: Among 146 myocarditis patients, unvaccinated individuals had higher rates of hypertension, diabetes, obstructive pulmonary disease, and substance abuse, and exhibited more severe cardiac issues like mitral regurgitation and ventricular dysfunction. Vaccinated patients had better lab results and fewer severe symptoms. A model identified advanced age and cardiovascular dysfunction as key mortality risks, suggesting vaccination may mitigate severe cardiac complications and improve outcomes. Conclusion: The findings of this study show that although there is a risk of myocarditis as a side effect following the COVID-19 vaccination, its severity is far less than the occurrence following the COVID-19 infection, with fewer complications and a better prognosis. However, more studies are still necessary to complete the existing findings and clarify their unknown aspects.

title: Acute kidney injury in patients with COVID-19 receiving mechanical ventilation
abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) has emerged as one of the most frequent and prognostically relevant complications in hospitalized patients with COVID-19, particularly among those with acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) requiring invasive mechanical ventilation.During the pandemic, the National Institute of Respiratory Diseases (INER) in Mexico City was designated as a national referral center for critically ill patients, facing an unprecedented burden of severe respiratory failure and COVID-19-associated AKI.This narrative review integrates international and national evidence on the epidemiology, pathophysiology, diagnosis, and management of COVID-19 and associated AKI, explicitly incorporating the clinical and scientific experience generated at INER.We discuss the high incidence of AKI observed in Mexican cohorts, the distinction between community-acquired and hospital-acquired AKI, and the central role of lung-kidney crosstalk in patients with ARDS.Particular emphasis is placed on the impact of mechanical ventilation strategies, especially driving pressure and reduced lung compliance, as key determinants of adverse kidney outcomes.We also review the role of urinary biomarkers for early detection of kidney injury and a stage-based management approach that includes conventional kidney replacement therapies and adjunctive extracorporeal support strategies.The INER experience highlights the importance of early nephrology involvement in the care of critically ill patients and the generation of local evidence to improve kidney-related outcomes in COVID-19.
journal: NCT Neumología y Cirugía de Tórax (English Edition)
