title: Potential drug-drug interactions in patients with Covid-19 in a public hospital in Brazil
abstract: Objective: To analyze the potential drug-drug interactions (pDDIs) of Covid-19 patients in a Brazilian public hospital. Methods: Cross-sectional, retrospective, descriptive, and analytical study conducted through the evaluation of medical records between March and November 2020. Drugs were categorized according to the Anatomical Therapeutic Chemical (ATC) classification system. The pDDIs were verified using the "drugs.com" database. Results: 79.7% of patients had pDDIs, totaling 483 possible interactions involving 113 different drugs. Among the pDDIs, 10.5% were classified as severe, 66.5% as moderate, and 23.0% as mild. The most common pDDIs involved anti-infective and cardiovascular drugs. Several factors were correlated with a higher occurrence of pDDI, such as being between 60 and 79 years old, hypertension, concurrent use of 4 to 7 drugs or more than 8 drugs, admission to the ICU, previous use of drugs for the cardiovascular system, prescription of anticoagulants, systemic hormonal preparations such as corticosteroids, and anti-infective agents for systemic use. On the other hand, being between 20 and 39 years old, using three or fewer drugs simultaneously, and staying less time hospitalized were associated with a decrease in the risk of pDDIs. Conclusion: Covid-19 patients have a high prevalence of pDDIs, demonstrating the need to identify and monitor their occurrence in public health institutions in order to increase patient safety.

title: Working Remotely from Home During and Post-COVID-19
abstract: Abstract The chapter reviews and analyzes the merits and challenges of people with disabilities in the United Kingdom and United States regarding working from home in the post-pandemic period when a return to office was mandated by both governments. Both countries had similar legislation regarding reasonable accommodations for people with disabilities. The Equality Act 2010 in the United Kingdom was comprehensive, covering disability as one of nine “protected characteristics.” The US ADA Title I focused exclusively on the employment of people with disability. The UK policy showed much more willingness to regulate the labor market during the pandemic and the post-pandemic period and allowed remote working. The US policy demonstrated less interference in the labor market during the pandemic and post-pandemic. The UK government was concerned with employer pushback on remote working and tended to disproportionally affect workers with disability regarding flexible arrangements. The UK policy recognized the right to flexible work, and employees with disabilities still had stronger protection under the “reasonable adjustment” framework. The US federal policy-imposed return-to-office mandate led to a rise in ADA lawsuits regarding the denial of remote work as a reasonable accommodation. The United States carried out the “essesntial functions” test, meaning the key legal question in many US cases was whether remote work eliminated an “essential function” of the job. Although courts aligned with employers vis-à-vis employees’ claims for working remotely, judges in some circuits started considering an employee’s remote work after the pandemic.
journal: Prospects for Employment of Persons with Disabilities in the Post-COVID-19 Era

Although courts aligned with employers vis-à-vis employees’ claims for working remotely, judges in some circuits started considering an employee’s remote work after the pandemic.

title: UK and US Policies Regarding Employees with Disabilities During and Post-COVID-19 Pandemic and in a Few Low-Middle-Income-Countries
abstract: Abstract During the COVID-19 pandemic, the United Kingdom and United States prioritized flexible working arrangements and adjustments for employees with disabilities, particularly those at higher risk. In the post-pandemic period, both nations have focused on solidifying these flexible arrangements but have also faced criticism over potentially regressive policies related to disability benefits. The UK approach focused on the expansion of access to work. However, the UK government proposed significant welfare reforms aimed at pushing more people into work. The United States prioritized post-pandemic Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC) guidance that solidified the legal precedent for remote work as a reasonable accommodation under the ADA. Employers were required to evaluate renewed requests for remote work based on individual circumstances rather than reverting to pre-pandemic policies. Employers were expected to ensure a safe return-to-office (RTO) process but were not required to eliminate essential job functions to accommodate remote work. Finally, case law in the United States continued to evolve regarding what constituted an “undue hardship” for employers denying remote work, often referencing the successful remote work period during the pandemic. The COVID-19 pandemic disproportionately affected employees with disabilities in Low-Middle-Income-Countries (LMICs), exacerbating preexisting inequalities in employment, income, and access to services. Post-pandemic policies required a more comprehensive and systematic approach to address the deeper structural barriers to inclusion.

title: Prevalence and factors associated with post-COVID-19 conditions in older people: SABE Study (health, well-being, and aging)
abstract: Objective: To analyze the prevalence and factors associated with post-COVID-19 conditions in older residents of São Paulo. Methodology: This epidemiological study used logistic regression to assess factors associated with post-COVID-19 conditions. Results: The prevalence of post-COVID-19 conditions in older adults was 17.6%, and the factors associated with this condition were prior hospitalization for COVID-19 (odds ratio, 3.78) and dependence in activities of daily living (odds ratio, 3.67). Conclusions: Dependence in activities of daily living and hospitalization due to COVID-19 were associated with post-COVID-19 conditions in older adults. Public health strategies should be prioritized to focus on protecting the most vulnerable groups.

title: CICP COVID-19 Injury Table: Registered Prediction
abstract: This registration records four predictions (P1 to P4) about how the number of claims filed with the Countermeasures Injury Compensation Program (CICP) will respond to the proposed COVID-19 Countermeasures Injury Table (RIN 0906-AB31), posted before the notice of proposed rulemaking. The predictions were fixed in July 2026 from HRSA data dated no later than July 1, 2026, and are posted without revision. The attached document states the predictions, their basis in the author’s working paper on Vaccine Injury Table amendments, and the scoring plan (effective date plus fifteen months). The two attached CSV files are the prediction grid and the denied-claim composition from which Table 1 is computed.

title: Comparative Evaluation of the Inactivation of SARS-CoV-2 and Human Coronavirus 229E against Sodium Hypochlorite
abstract: Introduction: Surface disinfection is one of the important non-pharmaceutical intervention measures that help prevent the spread of Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2). Disinfectants with an efficacy claim against Human Coronavirus strain 229E (HCoV-229E) have been used for the disinfection of SARS-CoV-2; however, the comparative susceptibility of these two viruses to chemical disinfection has not been well defined. To address this, laboratory data were generated to compare the level of inactivation of human coronaviruses HCoV-229E and SARS-CoV-2 to a common antimicrobial agent, sodium hypochlorite (NaOCl), on a hard non-porous surface. Methods: A hard surface-based Quantitative Method (QM) was used to evaluate the viral inactivation efficacy by three treatments of NaOCl against HCoV-229E and SARS-CoV-2. For each treatment, viral inoculum containing soil load was applied onto a stainless steel carrier and dried. The inoculated carrier was exposed to NaOCl or a control fluid and held for five minutes. Following the exposure time, a neutralizer was added, and the sample was serially diluted and inoculated onto host cells to determine the number of infective units. The resulting Log10 of the density for control and treated carriers was used to generate Log10 reduction (LR) values for comparative statistical evaluation. Results: The mean LR ± standard error (SE) for HCoV-229E was 0.96 ± 0.09 (n=10) at 500 ppm NaOCl, 2.41 ± 0.15 (n=10) at 1,000 ppm NaOCl, and 4.54 ± 0.13 (n=10) at 1,500 ppm NaOCl. The mean LR ± SE for SARS-CoV-2 was 0.91 ± 0.24 (n=4) at 500 ppm NaOCl, 1.96 ± 0.26 (n=4) at 1,000 ppm NaOCl, and 4.23 ± 0.16 (n=4) at 1,500 ppm NaOCl. Both viruses were significantly responsive to the increasing concentrations of NaOCl. HCoV-229E had slightly higher mean LRs compared to SARS-CoV-2 at each NaOCl concentration; however, these differences were not statistically significant (p ≥ 0.067). Regression analysis using a linear mixed effects model (LMM) also indicates that the susceptibility of HCoV-229E and SARS-CoV-2 to NaOCl is comparable. Discussion: Understanding the antimicrobial tolerance of viruses can enhance public health response to viral infections. By determining the tolerance, the most appropriate antimicrobial agent can be chosen to disinfect surfaces contaminated with viral particles. Disinfection of highcontact surfaces can reduce the amount of fomite transmission and limit outbreaks. Conclusion: The data suggest that HCoV-229E and SARS-CoV-2 are statistically comparable in their susceptibility to NaOCl treatments.

title: Gene expression and polymorphisms of Toll-like receptor 7 among Iraqi COVID-19 patients
abstract: The immune system's defenses against viruses are boosted by releasing inflammatory cytokines and antiviral mediators by toll-like receptor families (TLRs). TLR7 is one of the members of this family (TLRs). Thus, this study aimed to look into its function and genetic variation in the development of COVID-19 disease and its recovery. The study was conducted on 90 patients (45 severe-critical cases and 45 mild-moderate cases), 50 recovered cases, and 89 healthy people using quantitative real-time and allele-specific PCR for gene expression and gene polymorphisms determination, respectively. The relative TLR7 gene expression ratio was significantly higher in COVID-19 patients compared to recovered and healthy controls. The present study showed that the folding rate of TLR7 gene expression in the severely critically ill group (58.3±28.6) was significantly higher (p < 0.046) than in the mild to moderate patient group (41.7±24.39). The same can be said for the Ct values ​​(16-26) and (27-36), which were (51.9±27.7) and (37.5±23.4), respectively, with a significant value (p<0.01). Moreover, it has been found that there was a positive correlation between classical biomarkers and gene expression of this receptor. Interestingly, the present study showed no significant difference in TLR7 gene SNPs, rs179010 C and T allele, and rs3853839 C and G allele (p = 0.801 and 0.461, respectively). Moreover, the rs179008-TLR7 mutant C allele was not found in the present study population. We therefore recommend the detection of the rs179008- TLR7 mutant T allele and other TLR7 SNP alleles in the Iraqi population. TLR7 gene expression is positively associated with the disease and its severity. Conversely, down-regulating TLR7 gene expression is linked to a quicker recovery from the illness mentioned above. However, the SNPs under investigation did not affect the disease's severity or the patient's ability to recover from it.
journal: Iraqi Journal of Bioscience and Biomedical

title: Targeting Nsp13: a screening and hit validation campaign to develop inhibitors of SARS-CoV-2 replication
abstract: The emergence of the SARS-CoV-2 virus and the subsequent Covid-19 pandemic caused a global shutdown in 2020. Five years on, the disease remains prevalent and is still listed by the WHO as a priority for research. This work describes the development and implementation of a screening campaign to discover inhibitors for the helicase of the SARS-CoV-2 and closely related viruses capable of blocking viral replication. The process involves the expression and purification of recombinant nsp13 protein, the development and implementation of high-throughput screening compatible biochemical and cell-based assays, the characterization of the mode of action of the identified inhibitors, and the testing of whether nsp13 inhibition is sufficient to block the replication of SARS-CoV-2 in infected cells.

title: Knowledge, attitudes, and practices towards COVID-19 and their sociodemographic associations among communities in selected districts of Sri Lanka
abstract: Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19), caused by the SARS-CoV-2 virus, created a profound global health crisis that reshaped health systems worldwide. Compliance with preventive measures such as mask-wearing, hand hygiene, and vaccination is influenced by people’s knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) in Sri Lanka. Understanding these dimensions and the factors associated with them is vital for effective pandemic preparedness and control. This study examined the KAP of Sri Lankans towards COVID-19, explored sociodemographic predictors, and compared the performance of Binary Logistic Regression (BLR) and Random Forest (RF) algorithms in classifying KAP levels. Responses were collected from 80 adults across four districts using an online questionnaire adapted from validated tools comprising 48 items. Confirmatory Factor Analysis (CFA) was employed to preliminarily assess and refine the measurement structure, while BLR and RF were applied to assess predictors. Results showed that 67.5% of respondents demonstrated good knowledge, 63.8% good practices, and 70.0% a positive attitude towards COVID-19. Education was significantly associated with all three KAP dimensions in the univariate analyses, while age and education were associated with knowledge and attitude, and education with practice. In the multivariable BLR models, Advanced Level (A/L) education was significantly associated with higher odds of good knowledge and attitude, while no predictor was statistically significant for practice. CFA supported a reduced measurement structure in which a subset of items showed satisfactory factor loadings across the three KAP dimensions. A comparison of classification performance revealed that BLR demonstrated higher Area Under the Curve (AUC), accuracy, recall, and F1-scores than RF across all three KAP dimensions, although RF achieved higher precision for knowledge and practice. These findings underscore the critical role of education in shaping public responses and suggest that different KAP dimensions may benefit from different analytical approaches. The study offers valuable insights for policymakers and health authorities in designing targeted health education campaigns to address sociodemographic disparities and strengthen community resilience. Despite limitations of sample size and convenience sampling, the research provides a foundation for future large-scale, representative, and longitudinal studies on KAP and similar contexts.

title: 2026-2027 COVID-19 vaccination.
abstract: The FDA has licensed 2026-2027 formulas of the mRNA COVID-19 vaccines Comirnaty, Spikevax, and mNEXSPIKE1 and the adjuvanted protein subunit COVID-19 vaccine Nuvaxovid. The vaccines are FDA-licensed for use in adults ≥65 years old and in persons aged 6 months-64 years (Spikevax), 5-64 years (Comirnaty), or 12-64 years (mNEXSPIKE, Nuvaxovid) who are at high risk for severe COVID-19 because of an underlying condition.

title: Procalcitonin Patterns at Admission and Discharge in Moderate and Severe Hospitalised COVID-19: A Single-Centre Retrospective Study
abstract: Procalcitonin (PCT) was widely used in the COVID-19 pandemic to help distinguish virus-induced inflammation from secondary bacterial infection but its use in COVID-19 is still controversial, especially in hospitals lacking routine microbiological facilities. This study aimed to describe admission PCT levels alongside inflammatory, haematological and coagulation parameters in hospitalised patients with moderate and severe COVID-19. Historical discharge PCT measurements were also reviewed but they could not be verified and are not reported as results. This retrospective single-centre descriptive study included adults with PCR-confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection admitted to a regional infectious diseases hospital in Bukhara, Uzbekistan, in 2020–2022 (moderate, n = 49; severe, n = 71), classified according to national guidelines and 20 adults without acute illness as a comparison group. PCT, C-reactive protein (CRP), ferritin, full blood count and coagulation parameters were measured at admission and discharge. This report is based on the aggregate results of the original doctoral dissertation (Bukhara State Medical Institute, 2024); individual patient records and original statistical output were not available for re-analysis. Data are presented descriptively as mean ± SEM, as labelled in the source tables. The significance results of the original analysis could not be verified and are not reported. Admission PCT was 0.39 ± 0.03 ng/mL in moderate and 0.75 ± 0.03 ng/mL in severe disease, compared with 0.03 ± 0.003 ng/mL in the comparison group. This severity-group difference is descriptive and was not tested; PCT was also among the supporting severity criteria, so it does not show an independent association with severity. CRP was almost identical across severity groups (19.6 ± 0.95 versus 20.3 ± 0.84 mg/L) and ferritin was lower in severe disease (186.23 ± 28.9 versus 242.6 ± 61.14 ng/mL). Discharge PCT values could not be verified, because the historical assay and its lower limit of quantification are not documented and the reported means were below 0.05 ng/mL; they are not reported as results. At discharge, mean D-dimer remained above the comparison-group mean but below the upper reference limit. In this aggregate data report, admission PCT was descriptively higher in severe than in moderate disease but this is not an independent association with severity. The discharge PCT values are unverified and do not support any conclusion. Without microbiological testing, these hypothesis-generating findings cannot distinguish bacterial involvement from severe virus-induced inflammation.

source_records.abstract: Procalcitonin (PCT) was widely used in the COVID-19 pandemic to help distinguish virus-induced inflammation from secondary bacterial infection but its use in COVID-19 is still controversial, especially in hospitals lacking routine microbiological facilities. This study aimed to describe admission PCT levels alongside inflammatory, haematological and coagulation parameters in hospitalised patients with moderate and severe COVID-19. Historical discharge PCT measurements were also reviewed but they could not be verified and are not reported as results. This retrospective single-centre descriptive study included adults with PCR-confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection admitted to a regional infectious diseases hospital in Bukhara, Uzbekistan, in 2020–2022 (moderate, n = 49; severe, n = 71), classified according to national guidelines and 20 adults without acute illness as a comparison group. PCT, C-reactive protein (CRP), ferritin, full blood count and coagulation parameters were measured at admission and discharge. This report is based on the aggregate results of the original doctoral dissertation (Bukhara State Medical Institute, 2024); individual patient records and original statistical output were not available for re-analysis. Data are presented descriptively as mean ± SEM, as labelled in the source tables. The significance results of the original analysis could not be verified and are not reported. Admission PCT was 0.39 ± 0.03 ng/mL in moderate and 0.75 ± 0.03 ng/mL in severe disease, compared with 0.03 ± 0.003 ng/mL in the comparison group. title: Mecanismos Inmunometabólicos de la Resistencia a la Insulina y sus Implicaciones en el Síndrome pos-COVID-19
abstract: La infección por SARS-CoV-2 desencadena una respuesta inflamatoria sistémica que trasciende el compromiso respiratorio y afecta de manera significativa al sistema endocrino-metabólico. El objetivo de este artículo de revisión fue analizar los mecanismos inmunometabólicos de la resistencia a la insulina y sus implicaciones en el síndrome pos-COVID-19. Se realizó una revisión narrativa utilizando datos extraídos de las bases de datos PubMed/MEDLINE, SciELO, ScienceDirect, Google Scholar, Web of Science y Scopus. Los resultados evidencian que el virus utiliza el receptor de la enzima convertidora de angiotensina 2 (ACE2), altamente expresado en el páncreas y tejidos metabólicos, para su ingreso celular. Esto provoca la regulación a la baja de ACE2, daño directo o indirecto en las células beta pancreáticas y alteración de las vías de señalización de la insulina a través de mediadores proinflamatorios como IL-6 y TNF-a. Asimismo, la tormenta de citocinas induce un alto estrés oxidativo que altera el metabolismo de la glucosa en el hígado y el tejido muscular, prolongando estas disfunciones dentro del síndrome pos-COVID-19. Estas alteraciones representan un desafío sustancial para la salud pública al elevar el riesgo de diabetes de nuevo inicio e intensificar complicaciones en la población. En conclusión, la resistencia a la insulina inducida por SARS-CoV-2 es una secuela inmunometabólica clave que exige nuevas estrategias epidemiológicas y terapéuticas integrales.

title: Impacto da COVID-19 na evolução clínica e prognóstico de pacientes com doença pulmonar obstrutiva crônica (DPOC): uma revisão integrativa.
abstract: Introduction: Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD) is a chronic respiratory condition that affects a substantial number of individuals worldwide, potentially impairing pulmonary function and quality of life. Following the COVID-19 pandemic, investigating the effects of SARS-CoV-2 infection in this population has become particularly relevant. Objective: To analyze the impact of COVID-19 on the clinical course and prognosis of patients with COPD, considering outcomes during the acute phase of infection and after recovery.Materials and Methods: An integrative literature review was conducted using PubMed, SciELO, and Google Scholar, covering studies published between 2020 and 2026 that investigated the impact of COVID-19 on the clinical course and prognosis of patients with COPD. Results: During the post-COVID-19 period, evidence indicated worsening dyspnea and disease control, as well as an increased frequency of exacerbations among patients who experienced severe SARS-CoV-2 infection. However, findings varied according to study design, COVID-19 severity, and the characteristics of the populations investigated. Conclusion: COVID-19 may be associated with clinically significant consequences in patients with COPD, particularly following severe infection. Nevertheless, further longitudinal studies are required to clarify the persistence of these effects and identify the prognostic factors involved.

title: Effect of the COVID-19 pandemic on amniocentesis and prenatal diagnosis in a western Chinese city
abstract: To evaluate the impact of the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic on prenatal diagnosis in a western Chinese city. We retrospectively investigated the clinical features of pregnant women underwent amniocentesis and the results of karyotyping and chromosome microarray analysis (CMA) during the COVID-19 pandemic. The pre-COVID-19 period (2019), lockdown period (2020–2022), and post-zero-COVID period (January 2023–July 2023) were evaluated and compared. The percentages of pregnant women underwent amniocentesis were 13.6% (3359/24704), 13.3% (6953/52137), and 13.3% (1227/9221) during the pre-COVID-19, lockdown, and post-zero-COVID period, respectively. The average ages of the women underwent amniocentesis were 31.37 ± 5.27, 32.07 ± 5.21, and 32.49 ± 4.96 years ( P < 0.05). The clinical indications for prenatal diagnosis that changed most obviously were advanced maternal age (AMA), fetal ultrasound anomalies (FUA), and abnormal maternal serum screening (MSS) during the three periods. The AMA and FUA increased, whereas the MSS decreased. No statistically significant difference was detected in the proportion of abnormal karyotyping (women underwent amniocentesis) and CMA results (women underwent CMA) across the three periods. The COVID-19 pandemic had a limited impact on prenatal diagnosis in the western Chinese city of Chengdu, except that the age of women underwent amniocentesis increased owing to pregnancy postponement resulting from the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: Cardiovascular adverse events of tocilizumab and baricitinib in COVID-19 and rheumatoid arthritis
abstract: Tocilizumab and baricitinib are used in rheumatoid arthritis (RA) and COVID-19, where acute hyperinflammation and systemic stress may amplify cardiovascular risk. Comparative evidence on indication-specific cardiovascular signals remains scarce; we therefore assessed these signals by indication. We analyzed the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System data from January 2010 to June 2025 to compare cardiovascular adverse events (CVAEs) associated with baricitinib and tocilizumab. Primary outcomes included 6 CVAE categories: cardiac arrhythmias, central nervous system vascular disorders, embolic and thrombotic events, ischemic heart disease, noninfectious myocarditis/pericarditis, and other cardiac disorders. Disproportionality was assessed using the information component (IC) and reporting odds ratio (ROR), stratified by pre- and post-COVID-19 Emergency Use Authorization (EUA) periods and indications (COVID-19 vs RA). Machine learning models were additionally trained to characterize risk patterns for each drug, with feature contributions interpreted using SHapley Additive exPlanations. Among 17,750,053 reports, 5994 CVAEs were identified (baricitinib, n = 965; tocilizumab, n = 5029). Disproportionality was higher in the post-EUA than the pre-EUA period for both baricitinib (IC, 0.84 [IC 025 , 0.59] to 1.51 [1.39]; ROR, 1.89 [95% confidence interval, 1.62–2.21] to 3.22 [2.98–3.48]) and tocilizumab (0.22 [0.16] to 0.54 [0.47]; 1.18 [1.14–1.23] to 1.50 [1.43–1.57]). Baricitinib for COVID-19 showed the highest disproportionality (IC, 2.90 [IC 025 , 2.70]; ROR, 11.95 [95% confidence interval, 10.33–13.83]). Gradient boosting machine achieved the highest AUROC (baricitinib, 0.728; tocilizumab, 0.702), and SHapley Additive exPlanations highlighted COVID-19 indication for baricitinib and RA for tocilizumab. Our findings suggest indication-dependent cardiovascular signals when immunomodulators are repurposed for acute viral infections, underscoring the need for context-aware evaluation in drug repurposing.

title: Self-Reported Changes in Sleep, Electronic Device Use, and Health-Application Uptake During the COVID-19 Lockdown: A Cross-Sectional Survey of Jordanian Internet Users
abstract: Background: The COVID-19 pandemic and related lockdowns have profoundly affected daily routines and lifestyle behaviors globally. Aims: This cross-sectional study is aimed at documenting the changes in sleep patterns, electronic device use, and health-application adoption during the lockdown period (COVID-19) among 2511 Jordanian internet users participating in an online convenience sample. Methods: An online survey was used to gather data on demographics, sleep habits, physical activity, diet, and digital health tool usage. Results: Among the surveyed participants, 39.9% reported increased sleep duration, 13.5% reported decreased sleep duration, and 46.6% reported no change. In multivariable logistic regression, participants aged 18–35 years (aOR = 1.95, 95% CI 1.28–2.99), single status (aOR = 1.77, 95% CI 1.39–2.26), health-related education (aOR = 1.38, 95% CI 1.01–1.88), and non-health or unemployed occupational status (aOR = 1.62 and 1.67, respectively) were independently associated with increased sleep duration. Increased electronic device use was independently associated with single status (aOR = 1.39, 95% CI 1.00–1.92) and higher educational attainment (aOR range 1.60–1.97). Among the 2138 participants who reported increased electronic device use, 70.7% reported online studying, and 67.8% reported leisure/spare time as reasons for the increase. Participants used nutrition, physical activity, and medical applications at 28.6%, 36.9%, and 35.2%, respectively. In adjusted models, female gender was independently associated with use of nutrition (aOR = 1.69, 95% CI 1.34–2.13), physical activity (aOR = 1.32, 95% CI 1.07–1.62), and medical applications (aOR = 1.41, 95% CI 1.14–1.73). Bivariate analyses were exploratory and used Monte Carlo exact tests where cell counts were sparse; individual nominal p-values should not be interpreted as confirmatory. Conclusions: These findings show substantial changes in sleep, electronic device use, and health-application uptake during the COVID-19 lockdown. This suggests that digital health interventions may be worth evaluating for promoting healthy behaviors during periods of restricted mobility. Because of the non-probability sampling strategy, retrospective self-report, and cross-sectional design, the findings should not be interpreted as evidence of causal effects. Further representative and longitudinal studies are warranted.

title: Coronavirus Diversity in an Italian Bat Population Sampled During the Pandemic in 2020
abstract: Evolutionary studies have established a correlation between human and bat coronaviruses (CoV), identifying bats as the natural reservoir for Coronaviridae. Over the past two decades, three major zoonotic spillover events have been described: Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome CoV (SARS-CoV) and Middle East Respiratory Syndrome CoV (MERS-CoV), which caused significant global outbreaks, and SARS-CoV-2, which triggered the COVID-19 pandemic. Despite these events, the true diversity of coronavirus species harbored by bats remains largely unmapped, even as the discovery of novel strains continues to accelerate. In this study, we analyzed 37 fecal swab samples collected in Northern Italy, targeting the bat genera Miniopterus, Myotis, and Rhinolophus. Coronaviruses were detected using a pan-coronavirus (Pan-CoV) nested RT-PCR in five bat samples: three tested positive for Alphacoronaviruses (Alpha-CoVs) and two for Betacoronaviruses (Beta-CoVs). Positive samples were subjected to Pan-CoV Illumina next-generation sequencing (NGS), and two samples yielded sufficient read depth for robust contig assembly. Phylogenetic analysis revealed the co-circulation of three distinct Alpha-CoVs within a Miniopterus schreibersii (M. schreibersii) fecal sample and the presence of a SARS-CoV-related strain in a Rhinolophus hipposideros (R. hipposideros) fecal sample. source_records.abstract: Evolutionary studies have established a correlation between human and bat coronaviruses (CoV), identifying bats as the natural reservoir for Coronaviridae. title: Rehabilitación respiratoria y funcional temprana tras neumonía asociada a COVID-19 en una persona mayor: estudio de caso con ejercicios progresivos en sedestac
abstract: Functional recovery after COVID-19-associated pneumonia may be limited by dyspnea, muscle weakness, chest pain, deconditioning, and loss of autonomy, particularly in older adults after prolonged hospitalization. This study aimed to describe the application and clinical-functional course of a progressive respiratory and functional exercise system in a woman older than 65 years during the early post-discharge phase. A descriptive single-case design with 30-day follow-up was conducted using clinical-functional observation, analysis of ventilatory mechanics, and graded motor tasks performed in a seated position. The participant had controlled hypertension and hypercholesterolemia and, after approximately 21 days of hospitalization, presented chest pain, occasional cough, fatigue, perceived breathing difficulty, and reduced muscle strength. The intervention comprised four progressive upper-limb tasks intended to promote scapulothoracic mobility, thoracic expansion, postural control, and muscular activation related to ventilatory mechanics. At day 20, an observationally favorable course was documented in movement tolerance and perceived breathing capacity; by day 30, greater functional autonomy and no reported episodes of breathlessness during usual activities were recorded. These observations must be interpreted cautiously because they derive from a single case and were not supported by standardized physiological outcomes. Current evidence supports individualized pulmonary rehabilitation after COVID-19, while emphasizing the need to rule out exertional desaturation, cardiac impairment, and post-exertional symptom exacerbation before exercise training. For future replication, the protocol should include objective monitoring, validated functional tests, symptom scales, and explicit stopping criteria. The case contributes a feasible low-resource sequence for early functional progression while highlighting the methodological and safety requirements necessary for stronger clinical inference.

title: Multi-omic analysis of post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC)
abstract: Millions of patients surviving COVID-19 infection develop post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC), a debilitating condition that severely disrupts quality of life. Limited data exists on PASC patient peripheral blood multi-omic landscape. We enrolled 155 individuals with self-reported PASC who were compared with 100 acutely ill COVID-19 patients and with 44 healthy subjects. State-of-the-art mass spectrometry and next-generation leukocyte RNA sequencing were conducted in the blood samples of these participants. PASC status was associated with failure to regain a healthy baseline molecular status in these patients and aberrations in multiple biological pathways, including sphingolipids, chromatin-associated processes, and others. A machine learning algorithm trained on patients’ data produced 9 top entities allowing PASC diagnosis with a mean precision-recall area under the curve (AUC) of 0.97. An interface tool was generated to facilitate rapid access to the presented data and enable further analyses. This work provides new mechanistic insights into PASC through integrated multi-omic and machine learning analyses, establishing a robust exploratory framework and data resources to guide future biomarker validation and clinical meta-analyses.

title: Aspekte der immunologischen Reaktion nach Kontakt oder Infektion mit SARS-CoV-2 in Hinblick auf immunzellvermittelte Langzeitimmunität und post-COVID-Syndrom
abstract: Zusammenfassend widmen sich beide Veröffentlichungen und meine damit verbundene wissenschaftliche Arbeit der Immunantwort gegen SARS-CoV-2. Einerseits was die anhaltende Reaktionsfähigkeit des Immunsystems gegenüber dem SARS-CoV-2-Virus im positiven, d.h. schützenden Sinne betrifft, andererseits bezieht sich die Arbeit auf anhaltende negative Auswirkungen einer SARS-CoV-2 Infektion, d.h. im Sinne einer Verlängerung der Symptomphase. Meine – als erstgenannter Autor in geteilter Erstautorschaft veröffentlichte, im Zentrum stehende – Arbeit ‘Detectable SARS-CoV-2 specific immune responses in recovered unvaccinated individuals 250 days post wild type infection’ zeigte eine anhaltende Reaktionsfähigkeit des Immunsystems nach Infektion einer zuvor naiven Bevölkerungsgruppe mit dem SARS-CoV-2-Wildtyp. Diese betrifft mehrere, zum adaptiven Immunsystem gehörige T Zellreihen (CD4+ TEM und CD4+ TEMRA), welche eine – im Vergleich zur Kontrollgruppe - gesteigerte Zytokinsekretion nach Stimulation mit SARS-CoV-2-Oberflächenantigenen zeigten. Zudem ließ sich dieser Effekt ebenfalls für eine Gruppe exponierter, jedoch nicht COVID-19-infizierter Personen zeigen, was eine Hintergrundaktivierung des Immungedächtnisses nahelegt und Hinweise auf eine im Hintergrund entstehende Schutzfunktion auch bei nicht Infizierten liefert. Weitere, ähnlich gelagerte Unterschiede bezüglich von B-Zell- antworten oder NK-Zellantworten zeigten sich in dieser Veröffentlichung nicht. Ebenfalls ergaben sich kein Hinweis oder signifikante Unterschiede auf eine Kreuzreaktivität zwischen SARS-CoV-2-Antikörpern und Antikörpern gegen die common cold coronaviruses (CCCs). Die – meine Ko-Autorenschaft umfassende – Veröffentlichung „Persistent immune abnormalities discrimnate post-COVID syndrome from convalescence“ zeigt Unterschiede zwischen rekonvaleszenten Infizierten und nicht rekonvaleszenten Infizierten im Vergleich mit einer Kontrollgruppe bezüglich innate lymphoid cells (ILCs) und deren Vorläuferzellen ILC-precursors (ILCPs). Diese Unterschiede geben einen Einblick in die immunologischen Unterschiede zwischen Rekonvaleszenz und prolongierten Symptomen einer COVID-19-Erkrankung im Sinne eines ’post-COVID-Syndroms’. Weiterhin zeigte sich eine Erhöhung verschiedener proinflammatorischer Zytokine (IL-8, IL6, IL-1Ra) in der Gruppe der ’post-COVID’-Probanden im Vergleichzur Gruppe der rekonvaleszenten Probanden als möglicher Ausdruck einer fortlaufenden Entzündungsreaktion in dieser Gruppe. Die Ergebnisse dienen somit als Anknüpfungspunkt für weitere Forschung an Langzeitfolgen einer COVID-19-Infektion, da sie einen möglichen, immunologischen Mechanismus fortlaufender Symptome und Einschränkungen darstellen.

title: Impact of COVID-19 Pandemic on the Financial Performance of Selected Public Sector Banks in India: An Empirical Analysis
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic imposed severe economic and operational challenges on the Indian banking sector. Public sector banks, because of their extensive role in financial inclusion, priority-sector lending and government-supported economic programmes, occupied a particularly important position during the crisis. The present study examines the impact of COVID-19 on the financial performance of selected public sector banks in India by comparing their performance during 2019–20 and 2020–21. Twelve financial indicators covering capital adequacy, credit deployment, liquidity, income generation, lending efficiency, profitability, asset utilization and leverage are examined. A paired sample t-test is used at the 5% level of significance to determine whether changes between the pre-COVID and COVID periods were statistically significant. The results indicate that Capital Adequacy Ratio, Credit Deposit Ratio, Net Profit Margin and Return on Net Worth experienced statistically significant changes. Capital adequacy, net profit margin and return on net worth improved, whereas the Credit Deposit Ratio declined significantly. Changes in Current Ratio, Interest Income to Total Fund, Loans Turnover, Non-Interest Income to Total Fund, Quick Ratio, Return on Assets, Total Assets Turnover and Total Debt to Owners' Fund were statistically insignificant. The findings demonstrate that public sector banks showed considerable resilience during the pandemic, particularly in capital adequacy and profitability, although credit deployment was adversely affected. The study concludes that regulatory support, improved capitalization and prudent financial management contributed to the resilience of public sector banks during the COVID-19 period.

title: Reducing Poverty and Income Inequality Through Zakat Redistribution During the COVID-19 Crisis
abstract: Poverty and income inequality remain persistent development challenges across many countries, including those with established zakat management systems. Although zakat is widely recognized as an Islamic social finance instrument capable of improving social welfare, empirical evidence regarding the effectiveness of zakat redistribution across different economic conditions, particularly before, during, and after the COVID-19 pandemic, remains limited. This study addresses this gap by examining whether zakat redistribution effectively reduces poverty and income inequality and whether its effectiveness is state-dependent across crisis and recovery regimes. This study employs the Pooled Mean Group Autoregressive Distributed Lag (PMG-ARDL) approach using quarterly panel data from eight countries covering the 2016-2025 period. Quarterly observations were generated through quadratic match-average interpolation. Two empirical models, poverty and income inequality, were estimated while controlling for GDP per capita, inflation, and the Human Development Index. The findings reveal that zakat redistribution exerts a significant negative effect on poverty in both the short and long run, with the strongest long-run impact occurring during the COVID-19 period. Regarding income inequality, zakat redistribution produces a significant long-run negative effect, whereas the short-run effect is significant only for the full-sample estimation. Robustness tests using Fully Modified Ordinary Least Squares (FMOLS) and Dynamic Ordinary Least Squares (DOLS) confirm the consistency of the PMG-ARDL estimates. These findings underscore the importance of strengthening zakat governance, collection, redistribution, and digitalization to enhance poverty alleviation and inequality reduction, particularly during future economic crises.

title: "Through Her Lens" Re-framing Private Lives of Northeast India during Covid 19 "A través de la perspectiva femenina” : El replanteamiento de las vidas privadas del noreste de la India durante la Covid-19
abstract: Northeast India has often been neglected by the mainstream epistemologies within the hierarchical power dynamics. Especially, women of that region have been politicized and peripheralized as “docile bodies” with certain sociocultural practices and naturalized constraints. During the COVID-19 pandemic and the subsequent lockdown, increasing gender disparities, well documented in Northeast India, have triggered chaos and uncertainty within the domestic space of the socially marginalized people. This article focuses on the crisis of spatiality, visibility, and the representation of gender struggle archived in the visual research initiative “Through Her Lens”. This initiative archived the experiences of women during the pandemic and encouraged photographic practices in the eight Northeast Indian states and Darjeeling Hills in collaboration with Zubaan Publishers Pvt. and Sasakawa Peace Foundation. This archive forms an alternative space for women to use their own electronic gadgets to capture different forms of hurdles in their daily lives and at the same time critique the socio-political realities and power relations during the Covid-19 pandemic. The article also highlights how a visual narrative of cultural experience within a virtual archive can acquire new intersubjectivities and agencies.

This article focuses on the crisis of spatiality, visibility, and the representation of gender struggle archived in the visual research initiative “Through Her Lens”. This initiative archived the experiences of women during the pandemic and encouraged photographic practices in the eight Northeast Indian states and Darjeeling Hills in collaboration with Zubaan Publishers Pvt. and Sasakawa Peace Foundation. This archive forms an alternative space for women to use their own electronic gadgets to capture different forms of hurdles in their daily lives and at the same time critique the socio-political realities and power relations during the Covid-19 pandemic. The article also highlights how a visual narrative of cultural experience within a virtual archive can acquire new intersubjectivities and agencies.

title: Comparison of COVID-19 mortality estimates from Centers for Disease Control and Prevention wide-ranging ONline data for epidemiologic research and the global burden of disease study in the United States, 2020–2023
abstract: Accurate estimation of cause-specific mortality is essential for public health decision-making, yet differences in surveillance methodologies may yield divergent results. This study compared the United States COVID-19 mortality estimates from 2020 to 2023 using the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention Wide-ranging Online Data for Epidemiologic Research (CDC WONDER) and the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) study. COVID-19 deaths were identified using ICD-10 code U07.1, and crude mortality rates and percent change were calculated. Across the study period, GBD reported 1,207,595 deaths compared with 1,004,208 deaths in CDC WONDER underlying-cause data, representing 16.8% higher cumulative mortality. Discrepancies were greatest in 2020–2021 but narrowed over time. When CDC WONDER data including underlying and contributing causes were examined, mortality estimates remained lower than GBD early in the pandemic but exceeded GBD estimates in 2022–2023. Both datasets demonstrated similar temporal declines in mortality. These differences reflect how each system ascertains, codes, and handles the cause of death. Registration-based and modeled estimates of COVID-19 mortality are therefore not directly interchangeable, and the choice of source can change conclusions about the scale of the pandemic and the share of excess mortality attributed directly to COVID-19.

title: 'Multiple Truths, Multiple Experiences’: Assembling the COVID-19 Pandemic in Relation to Disability
abstract: Drawing on assemblage theory, this dissertation examines how the COVID-19 pandemic in the UK has been assembled in relation to ‘disability’. It responds to Goggin and Ellis’s (2020) call to decipher and push back against the ‘enforcing of normalcy’ during the pandemic. The study is based on an online survey (n=198) and 21 semi-structured interviews, conducted eleven months into the pandemic, with self-identified disabled people, medics, students, people in low-income professions and two experts. Three themes emerged: risk management, normative behaviour and mutability. The analysis yields three insights. First, it identifies two mechanisms through which the assemblage of normalcy is maintained: the de-vulnerabilisation of the ‘normative’ population through the vulnerabilisation of the Other, and structured emotion. Second, it reveals the ambivalent materialisations of escaping normalcy. Disabled participants were both marginalised and included, both more ‘vulnerable’ and better equipped, and they both aligned with and resisted normative valuations. Third, it argues for intersectionality as a contingent analytic. During the pandemic, gender was ‘submerged’ as a risk category while ‘race’ and ability were brought into topological proximity. The ‘multiple truths, multiple experiences’ of the pandemic remain structured by affect, and the mutability of ‘disability’ remains ‘wild’.

title: Risk Groups and Essential Workers During COVID ‐19: Definitions and Vaccine Priority Strategies
abstract: ABSTRACT The coronavirus vaccine, available at the end of 2020, can be seen as a scarce resource where the nation state created hierarchies within the society in terms of who was in and who was out of a social group, with tangible effects of some receiving the vaccine faster than others. Through a comparative document analysis, this paper investigates how symbolic boundaries were made by looking at risk groups and essential workers as well as the vaccine strategies in Europe. While these two groups were theoretically constructed as either vulnerable or exposed during the pandemic, results indicate that group boundaries were in fact fluid. This finding adds to the literature on symbolic boundaries by showcasing how the state created social and medical hierarchies by classifying certain social and professional groups as worthy of protection but also how new classifications were created for a specific segment of the population during the COVID‐19 pandemic health crisis.

title: Sustainable Growth Rate Perusahaan di Indonesia Sebelum dan Saat Pandemi Covid-19
abstract: Penelitian ini akan mencoba mendeskripsikan sustainable growth rate perusahaan-perusahaan di Indonesia sebelum memasuki masa pandemi Covid-19 (tahun 2018-2019) dan saat masa pandemi Covid-19 (tahun 2020-2021). Sustainable growth rate merupakan tingkat pertumbuhan maksimum yang dapat dicanangkan oleh perusahaan jika pendanaan tersebut hanya didanai dengan sumber dana internal, atau tanpa mengubah struktur modal yang telah ada. Sebelum memasuki masa pandemi, rata-rata tingkat sustainable growth lebih tinggi jika dibandingkan dengan saat pandemi Covid-19. Memasuki masa pandemi, banyak perusahaan mengalami kesulitan dan tekanan finansial, atau mencoba bertahan saja. Bahkan, perusahaan lebih memilih strategi no growth, dan kebanyakan malah mempunyai pertumbuhan negatif. Kondisi perusahaan sebelum memasuki pandemi umumnya normal dan cenderung naik, kondisi finansial perusahaan juga lebih, dan perusahaan cenderung untuk mengambil strategi growth, bahkan mungkin tingkat growth yang diupayakan adalah melebihi sustainable growth rate. Tentunya memilih strategi pertumbuhan yang melebih sustainable growth rate membutuhkan suntikan dana eksternal yang lebih banyak dan mungkin juga membutuhkan beberapa kebijakan lain untuk mendukung pertumbuhan yang ditargetkan tersebut. Konsep sutainable growth rate digunakan di dalam penelitian ini untuk mengamati strategi pertumbuhan yang diambil oleh perusahaan di Indonesia yang listed di BEI selama kondisi perusahaan tidak mengalami tekanan finansial (yakni sebelum pandemi covid-19) dibandingkan dengan saat mengalami financially distressed (memasuki masa pandemi Covid-19). Kata Kunci: Financial distress; Non-financial distress; Sustainable Growth Rate (SGR);

title: LINKING SUSTAINABILITY PERFORMANCE TO STOCK RESILIENCE DURING AND AFTER COVID-19 CRISIS: EVIDENCE FROM SOUTHEAST ASIA
abstract: Background: The COVID-19 pandemic severely disrupted markets. While sustainability performance measured by ESG scores theoretically buffers against shocks, its efficacy in emerging markets with nascent sustainability frameworks remains underexplored. Method: We analyze a balanced panel of 1,395 observations from 279 non-financial Southeast Asian firms (2020–2024). Using OLS, lagged, and fixed effects models, we compare the impact of sustainability performance on stock resilience during the 2020–2022 and post-pandemic (2023–2024) periods. Findings: Sustainability performance (ESG scores) significantly enhanced stock resilience during the pandemic. However, this protective effect dissipated post-pandemic. Results confirm a statistically significant improvement in overall resilience following the crisis, as investors redirected their focus toward traditional financial fundamentals such as profitability and leverage. Conclusion: Sustainability performance acts as situational crisis insurance. Its risk-mitigation value is highly salient during systemic uncertainty but diminishes under stable market conditions. Novelty/Originality of this article: Unlike prior single-phase studies in developed economies, this research provides longitudinal evidence on the dynamic, state-dependent nature of sustainability performance across crisis and recovery phases within Southeast Asia’s early-stage ESG landscape.

title: Lecciones de las pandemias de influenza y de COVID-19 para la odontología: revisión sistemática
abstract: Objetivo: sintetizar las lecciones de los brotes históricos de influenza y de la pandemia de COVID-19 aplicables a la atención odontológica. Método: revisión sistemática con síntesis narrativa en PubMed y SciELO (2012-2025); se incluyeron 15 estudios: revisiones sistemáticas y narrativas, ensayos clínicos y documentos de análisis histórico. Resultados: la pandemia de 1918 mostró el valor de proteger al personal sanitario y la de 2009, el de los diagnósticos moleculares y del uso planificado de los antivirales. En odontología, la COVID-19 obligó a controlar los aerosoles, reforzar la bioseguridad, priorizar la atención urgente, evaluar colutorios antisépticos y atender el agotamiento profesional. Conclusión: la preparación odontológica exige protocolos permanentes de bioseguridad y planes de continuidad asistencial.

title: A scoping review of the socioeconomic effects of COVID-19 pandemic on poverty in Ghana
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic unleashed unprecedented disruptions globally, significantly impacting economies and exacerbating poverty, particularly in developing countries. With its emerging economy and substantial informal sector, Ghana provides a critical case for studying how the pandemic-shaped poverty levels. This scoping review aims to synthesize existing research on the effects of COVID-19 on poverty levels in Ghana, identifying the extent of economic impacts and the effectiveness of mitigative measures implemented by the government and other stakeholders. This review used Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR). Findings indicate a significant rise in poverty levels, with the informal sector, women, and rural populations disproportionately affected. Employment and income shocks were widespread during the pandemic period, exacerbated by local and international supply chain disruptions. While governmental social protection and economic policy measures provided crucial support, gaps in coverage and delivery challenged the effectiveness of the interventions. The COVID-19 pandemic revealed the structural vulnerabilities within Ghana&s;s economic and social systems. The review underscores the urgent need for targeted policy interventions that enhance economic resilience and ensure comprehensive social protection coverage.

title: Symptom‐Based Machine Learning Framework for Early Syndrome Coronavirus 2 ( SARS ‐ CoV ‐2) Infection Prediction
abstract: ABSTRACT Early and accurate identification of SARS‐CoV‐2 infection remains a critical challenge, especially in limited‐infrastructure healthcare settings where access to molecular diagnostics is restricted. This study presents a symptom‐based machine learning framework for rapid prediction of COVID‐19 infection using routinely collected clinical indicators. The dataset used in this work is openly accessible at https://redivis.com/datasets/rxta‐4v35cgyz , enabling full transparency and reproducibility. After comprehensive preprocessing, recursive feature elimination with a random forest estimator identified nine key predictors, including SpO 2 , fever, loss of smell/taste, shortness of breath, dry cough, fatigue, age, diabetes status, and respiratory rate. Multiple supervised learning algorithms—logistic regression, SVM, k‐NN, decision tree, random forest, and a stacked ensemble—were trained and evaluated using 10‐fold cross‐validation. The stacked ensemble model outperformed all baseline classifiers, achieving an accuracy of 0.87, balanced sensitivity (0.88) and specificity (0.86), and the lowest error rate (0.12), demonstrating strong robustness and generalization by leveraging complementary strengths of the base learners. The proposed framework is computationally lightweight, delivers prediction times under 50 ms, and is suitable for deployment in real‐time clinical decision‐support systems. These results highlight its potential as a scalable, rapid, and cost‐effective screening tool for early COVID‐19 detection in resource‐constrained environments. Furthermore, SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) and LIME (Local Interpretable Model‐agnostic Explanations) analyses confirm that the model's predictions are grounded in clinically valid symptom patterns, with SpO 2 and fever identified as the dominant global predictors, enhancing clinical transparency and trust. Statistical significance testing via McNemar's test confirmed that the stacking ensemble's performance improvements over all baseline classifiers are statistically significant ( p < 0.05 for all pairwise comparisons).

title: Dimensões Psicológicas de Profissionais de Enfermagem Durante a covid-19: Uma Abordagem Por Análise de Componentes Principais Psychological Dimensions Of Nursing Professionals During COVID-19: An Approach Using Principal Component Analysis Dimensiones Psicológicas De Los Profesionales De Enfermería Durante La COVID-19: Un Enfoque Basado En El Análisis De Componentes Principales
abstract: Introdução: A pandemia de COVID-19 expôs profissionais de enfermagem a elevados níveis de estresse, agravando sintomas depressivos e exaustão emocional. Objetivos: Este estudo buscou identificar as dimensões psicológicas associadas a sintomas depressivos nesses profissionais durante a pandemia, utilizando Análise de Componentes Principais (PCA). Metodologia: Pesquisa transversal e quantitativa com 290 profissionais de enfermagem de um hospital público em Minas Gerais. Os dados foram coletados online entre novembro de 2022 e fevereiro de 2023, utilizando o Inventário de Depressão de Beck (BDI). Resultados: A PCA revelou três componentes principais explicando 60,77% da variância. O primeiro componente (PC1), responsável por 46,96%, refletiu exaustão física e emocional, marcada por cansaço e distúrbios no sono. O segundo componente (PC2), com 7,71%, associou-se à percepção emocional, incluindo culpa e manifestações somáticas. O terceiro componente (PC3), com 6,10%, destacou mudanças comportamentais, como irritabilidade e percepção negativa da autoimagem. Discussão: Esses achados reforçam a necessidade de intervenções psicológicas e estratégias para reduzir a sobrecarga laboral e fortalecer a resiliência emocional. Conclusão: O estudo evidencia a relevância de ferramentas estatísticas como a PCA para compreender fenômenos psicossociais e contribuir para políticas públicas de promoção do bem-estar dos profissionais de saúde.

Os dados foram coletados online entre novembro de 2022 e fevereiro de 2023, utilizando o Inventário de Depressão de Beck (BDI). Resultados: A PCA revelou três componentes principais explicando 60,77% da variância. O primeiro componente (PC1), responsável por 46,96%, refletiu exaustão física e emocional, marcada por cansaço e distúrbios no sono. O segundo componente (PC2), com 7,71%, associou-se à percepção emocional, incluindo culpa e manifestações somáticas. O terceiro componente (PC3), com 6,10%, destacou mudanças comportamentais, como irritabilidade e percepção negativa da autoimagem. Discussão: Esses achados reforçam a necessidade de intervenções psicológicas e estratégias para reduzir a sobrecarga laboral e fortalecer a resiliência emocional. Conclusão: O estudo evidencia a relevância de ferramentas estatísticas como a PCA para compreender fenômenos psicossociais e contribuir para políticas públicas de promoção do bem-estar dos profissionais de saúde.

title: Social capital and firm resilience during COVID-19: Evidence from listed firms in Vietnam
abstract: Type of the article: Research ArticleAbstractThe issue of firm resilience to systemic shocks is gaining importance in emerging markets, where weak institutions force companies to rely on social capital as a proxy for legitimacy and resources. Yet it remains to be seen whether social capital functions as a uniform shield or as a more selective, context-dependent anchor under extreme stress. The study examines whether four components of firm social capital: CSR disclosure, CEO networks, political connections, and bank connections, are associated with firm performance in the crisis and recovery phases of the COVID-19 pandemic in Vietnam. The study estimates pooled OLS models with sector and year fixed effects and one-year lagged social capital measures using an unbalanced panel of 338 firms listed on the Ho Chi Minh City Stock Exchange from 2019 to 2024, with the post-crisis recovery period (2022–2024) as the reference category. During the recovery period, the composite social capital index is positively related to both operating performance and market valuation. Our results show that CEO networks are positively related to operating performance during the crisis, whereas bank connections are significantly and negatively related to market valuation. Political connections are not significantly related to performance during the crisis, but are strongly related to higher market valuation during the recovery. These results suggest that the value of social capital is not monolithic but depends on the particular relational channel and the phase of the crisis, with practical implications for managers, investors and policymakers in emerging markets.AcknowledgmentsThe authors acknowledge the support of the University of Economics and Law, Vietnam National University – Ho Chi Minh City (VNU – HCM).

title: A nationwide ecological time-series analysis found no stable temporal or predictive relationship between dengue and COVID-19 surveillance records in Mexico from 2020 to 2025
abstract: Using national surveillance records, we evaluated whether COVID-19 dynamics explain, anticipate, or improve prediction of weekly dengue surveillance-record burden in Mexico during 2020–2025. We analysed 1,085,869 dengue records and 20,632,470 COVID-19 records. Audit of daily symptom-onset coverage identified 10 incomplete dengue weeks clustered around year-end/source snapshot boundaries; these weeks were treated as missing rather than zero, leaving 8,695 state-week observations from 32 entities for inferential analyses. Primary weekly counts were transformed as log10(records + 1), with a population-standardized sensitivity analysis using fixed 2020 INEGI populations. We examined pooled, year-specific, pandemic/post-pandemic, state-specific seasonal, nonlinear time-adjusted and lagged associations, and performed a direct predictive ablation. The audited pooled association was inverse (Pearson r = -0.331, bootstrap 95% CI -0.349 to -0.312; Spearman rho = -0.311), but its direction and magnitude varied by year, from r = 0.096 in 2021 to r = -0.312 in 2023. Population standardization yielded r = -0.386, whereas removal of both state and calendar-week effects reduced the association to r = -0.049. After state-specific adjustment for year, cyclic epidemiological-week structure and nonlinear time, the pooled residual correlation was r = -0.055; after additional AR(4) prewhitening, the largest absolute lag correlation was 0.053. In the direct ablation, adding COVID-19 lags to dengue lags, seasonal week and state effects changed test RMSElog10 from 0.1753 to 0.1749 (delta = -0.0004; block-bootstrap 95% interval − 0.0019 to 0.0011). These findings support no stable direct temporal or predictive coupling between the two surveillance series; the pooled inverse association is primarily a feature of calendar-time and epidemic-regime structure.

title: Digital Transformation and COVID-19 Crisis Management: A Case Study of a University Hospital Centre in Batna
abstract: This study examines the relationship between digital transformation and COVID-19 crisis management at Benflis Touhami University Hospital Centre in Batna. It uses a case study design and a questionnaire completed by 101 healthcare and administrative staff. The data were analysed using descriptive statistics and simple linear regression. Digital transformation was assessed through five dimensions: digital strategic orientation, the digital environment, digital human resources, digital culture and awareness, and digital governance. The findings show a positive correlation between digital transformation and crisis management (R = 0.733). The model explains 53.7% of the variance in crisis management scores. Digital human resources recorded the lowest mean, whereas learning from the crisis ranked highest among the crisis management dimensions. The findings point to the importance of digital skills, proactive planning, and institutional coordination. Generalisation is limited, and the observed association does not establish causation.

title: SEQUELAS PÓS-COVID-19 EM CRIANÇAS: UMA REVISÃO DE LITERATURA
abstract: Já eram noticiados casos de sintomas persistentes após a fase aguda da infecção de COVID-19 desde o início da pandemia em 2019, principalmente em adultos. Apesar de mais brando em crianças, estudos recentes indicam que essa faixa etária pode também ser afeta por complicações pós aguda dessa doença. Nesse sentido o intuito dessa revisão foi analisar quais os principais sintomas e a fisiopatologia dessa afecção em crianças. Foi realizada uma busca por trabalhos prévios nas plataformas PubMed e LILACS utilizando os descritores “post covid”, “sequelae” e “children”, utilizando o operador booleano “AND”. Foram incluídos no estudo artigos publicados nos últimos 5 anos (2020-2025); de acesso livre; na faixa etária de crianças até 18 anos e artigos cujos estudos eram do tipo estudo observacional ou estudo clínico controlado. Foram excluídos os artigos fora do tema ou duplicados. Através dos estudos analisados foi observado que as sequelas mais frequentes foram fadiga, dores de cabeça e dispneia. Também foi relatada uma síndrome de acometimento de múltiplos sistemas. Embora não esteja completamente esclarecida, a fisiopatologia dessa doença parece estar relacionada com os receptores ECA-2 e a resposta do sistema imune inato. Em conclusão, ainda são necessários mais estudos para esclarecer os mecanismos dessa doença mesmo após a sua fase aguda, monitorando a longo prazo esses pacientes com covid-19 com ou sem sequelas.
journal: Revista Ibero-Americana de Humanidades, Ciências e Educação

title: Fear of COVID-19 and PTSD symptoms in adolescents: the mediating role of meaning in life and the moderating role of gender
abstract: Background The COVID-19 pandemic and related restrictions were associated with substantial mental health burdens among adolescents, including PTSD symptoms. Meaning in life may explain the association between fear of COVID-19 and PTSD symptoms, and this association may differ by gender. Objective This study examined the association between fear of COVID-19 and PTSD symptoms among Chinese adolescents, tested the distinct indirect effects of Presence of Meaning and Search for Meaning, and evaluated whether gender moderated the second-stage paths from both meaning dimensions to PTSD. Methods A cross-sectional study was conducted with 1,291 middle school students recruited through convenience sampling. Participants completed the FCV-19S, PCL-C, MLQ, and a demographic survey. The sample included 656 females (50.8%) and 635 males (49.2%), aged 11–18 years (M = 14.13, SD = 1.35). Analyses were conducted using IBM SPSS 27.0 and PROCESS macro version 4.1; age was included as a covariate in every mediation and moderated mediation equation. Results Fear of COVID-19 was positively correlated with PTSD symptoms ( r = 0.31, p < 0.001). After controlling for age, the indirect effect was significant through Presence of Meaning ( B = 0.059, 95% CI [0.031, 0.089]) but not Search for Meaning ( B = 0.005, 95% CI [−0.001, 0.015]); this pattern held in the parallel model (Presence: B = 0.060, 95% CI [0.032, 0.092]; Search: B = −0.002, 95% CI [−0.009, 0.004]). Gender moderated the second-stage Presence–PTSD path ( B = −0.159, p = 0.044; stronger among females) and the Search–PTSD path ( B = −0.231, p = 0.016; negative among females but not males). For Presence of Meaning, conditional indirect effects were significant for both males and females, whereas the index of moderated mediation was not significant (index = 0.012, 95% CI [−0.002, 0.034]); for Search for Meaning, conditional indirect effects were not significant. Conclusion In age-adjusted models, Presence of Meaning, but not Search for Meaning, showed a significant indirect association. Gender moderated the second-stage paths from both dimensions to PTSD, but the overall indirect effects did not differ by gender. These findings support distinguishing having meaning from seeking meaning; longitudinal research is needed to test causal or intervention implications.

title: Association Between Changes in the Employment Environment and Suicide Attempts During the COVID-19 Pandemic
abstract: Background: The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted employment, but whether distinct types of employment change are differentially associated with suicidal behavior remains unclear. This study examined the association between pandemic-related employment changes and past-year suicide attempts. Methods: We conducted a cross-sectional analysis of 172,970 adults aged ≥19 years who were economically active before January 2020, using data from the 2021 Korea Community Health Survey (KCHS). Employment change was classified as no change, job loss, deteriorated employment conditions or improved employment conditions. Survey-weighted multivariable logistic regression was used to estimate adjusted odds ratios (AORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Results: Overall, 520 participants reported a suicide attempt in the past year. Compared with no change, job loss (AOR, 2.548; 95% CI, 1.777–3.654) and deteriorated employment conditions (AOR, 1.435; 95% CI, 1.116–1.845) were associated with higher odds of suicide attempts, whereas improved employment conditions were not (AOR, 0.678; 95% CI, 0.302–1.521). Job loss was associated with higher odds than deteriorated employment conditions (AOR, 1.776; 95% CI, 1.230–2.564). The interaction was significant for age (p = 0.0130) and income (p = 0.0035), but not for sex (p = 0.1008). Conclusions: Job loss and deteriorated employment conditions were differentially associated with past-year suicide attempts. Because of the cross-sectional design, temporal order and causality cannot be established.

title: Determinants of Community Compliance With COVID 19 Health Protocols in Indonesia: An Integrative Literature Review
abstract: Background: Community compliance with health protocols was essential during the early COVID 19 pandemic. Understanding its determinants may inform preparedness for future respiratory outbreaks. Objectives: This integrative literature review synthesized Indonesian evidence on factors associated with community compliance with COVID 19 preventive protocols. Methods: Google Scholar was the documented search source. Of 31 initially identified records, 16 remained after restriction, and six studies met eligibility criteria. Eligible studies examined community compliance with preventive protocols and provided accessible full text. Findings were synthesized descriptively using a Health Belief Model informed framework. Results: Across six studies, compliance was associated with cognitive factors, including knowledge, awareness, perceived threat, and perceived barriers; motivational and social factors, including attitudes, concern, motivation, and social environment; and structural factors, particularly facility availability. Findings varied across study settings, suggesting that compliance reflected interactions among individual perceptions, social influences, and environmental opportunities. Conclusions: Community compliance during the early pandemic was associated with interconnected cognitive, motivational, social, and structural factors. These findings provide contextual lessons for designing integrated health promotion strategies and strengthening preparedness for future respiratory outbreaks.

title: Integrated mechanistic and serological analyses reveal determinants of antibody-dependent enhancement in respiratory coronaviruses
abstract: Background Antibody-dependent enhancement (ADE) is an important concern in viral infection, vaccine development, and antibody-based therapeutics. Although extensively studied in flaviviruses, the molecular mechanisms and epidemiological relevance of ADE in respiratory coronaviruses remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to investigate the epitope-specific mechanisms, cellular pathways, and population characteristics of ADE mediated by SARS-CoV-2 and MERS-CoV antibodies. Methods SARS-CoV-2 and MERS-CoV pseudovirus ADE models were established using Fcγ receptor-expressing cells. The effects of epitope-specific antibodies, Fc–FcR interaction blockade, and inhibitors targeting Fyn, neuropilin-1 (NRP1), endosomal acidification, cathepsins, and PIKfyve were evaluated. A CD32B-based ADE model was developed for retrospective analysis of 530 human serum samples collected from 2019 to 2026. Cytokine profiles were analyzed in 175 serum samples. Correlations between antibody levels, ADE and inflammatory markers were statistically evaluated. Results Antibodies targeting specific epitopes within coronavirus spike proteins induced ADE of both SARS-CoV-2 and MERS-CoV pseudoviruses in FcγR-expressing cells. ADE was abolished by blocking Fc–FcR interactions, confirming Fc receptor dependence. ADE induction showed a concentration- and viral load-dependent pattern, with higher viral loads requiring increased antibody concentrations for maximal enhancement. Pharmacological inhibition revealed substantial overlap between ADE and classical receptor-mediated viral entry pathways, involving Fyn signaling, NRP1, endosomal acidification, cathepsins, and PIKfyve. Analysis of clinical serum samples demonstrated a significant association between antibody levels and ADE, with ADE incidence peaking during 2023 and remaining elevated thereafter. Serum samples capable of inducing ADE exhibited altered levels of TNF-α and IL-12p70, indicating that there may be enhanced activation of Th1 and increased pro-inflammatory responses.

title: Computational Assessment of CKP-25 Binding at Receptor-Recognition Interfaces Across Diverse Human Coronaviruses
abstract: Background/Objectives: The continued emergence of novel coronaviruses motivates the search for small molecules that bind conserved features of the spike receptor-recognition interface across diverse species. CKP-25 was recently reported as a small-molecule inhibitor of the SARS-CoV-2 spike receptor-binding domain. This study aimed to assess computationally whether CKP-25 can maintain stable binding at receptor-recognition interfaces across phylogenetically diverse human coronaviruses. Methods: CKP-25 was docked to the spike receptor-binding regions of Middle East respiratory syndrome coronavirus (MERS-CoV), severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 1 (SARS-CoV-1), and human coronaviruses NL63, 229E, and HKU1 (HCoV-NL63, HCoV-229E, and HCoV-HKU1). SARS-CoV-2 (PDB 6M0J), for which CKP-25 has documented antiviral activity, was processed identically and included as an experimentally validated reference system. Each selected complex was subjected to three independent 100 ns all-atom molecular dynamics (MD) simulations initialized with different random velocities. title: Experiences of nurses in caring for patients with coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) in Eswatini, Southern Africa: A qualitative study
abstract: Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) posed significant and unprecedented caregiving challenges among nurses. The caregiving challenges were severe in developing countries where health-related resources were scarce. Therefore, the study aimed to explore and describe nurses' experiences caring for patients with COVID-19 in one of Eswatini's COVID-19-designated hospitals. A descriptive qualitative design was employed with 12 purposively sampled participants. All the participants had experience working in the COVID-19 wards. Data were collected through face-to-face interviews using a pretested semi-structured interview guide and an audio recorder. Collected data were analyzed thematically following Colaizzi’s descriptive method. Trustworthiness was strengthened through forward–backward translation and dual coding. The study participants consisted of six females and six males aged 31 to 54 years. Three themes emerged from the data: (1) Caregiving challenges, (2) Coping strategies, and (3) Perceived support needs during pandemics. Pandemics, such as COVID-19, can significantly impact nurses' professional caregiving. As such, nurse managers and policymakers must be cognizant of the nurses' challenges and address them accordingly by ensuring sufficient personal protective equipment, adequate and competent nursing personnel, and on-site structured mental health services. Future studies can explore the experiences of nurse managers and other healthcare professionals on COVID-19.

title: Impact of COVID-19 on marginalised sections of the society in selected Southern Africa
abstract: The emergence of the novel coronavirus presented a unique challenge to the world, given its unpreparedness to face such a highly contagious and deadly disease. Emergency measures had to be implemented to ensure the spread of the virus was arrested in the absence of a known cure or vaccine. Many countries adopted preventative measures that limited the movement and gathering of people due to the highly contagious nature of the virus. Criticism arose, however, as to the effectiveness of these measures, given the varied negative effects on different people, especially marginalised populations. The top-down approaches implemented to curb the virus disregarded existing systems of the poor that made their societies functional ( Corburn et al., 2020 ). This was because the majority in Southern African urban areas are in the informal sector, while they also reside in informal settlements.
