title: Active Learning framework for Antibody Binding Affinity Prediction
abstract: Antibody engineering campaigns must prioritise variants from large combinatorial libraries under limited assay budgets. We present a Gaussian process (GP) active-learning benchmark for antibody-antigen binding affinity prediction across eight public AbBiBench assays spanning influenza hemagglutinin antibodies CR6261 and CR9114 and AAYL-series scFv libraries against the SARS-CoV-2 Spike HR2 peptide. The framework embeds variable heavy and light (VH/VL) sequences with ESM-2 650M, trains GP surrogates over compressed protein-language-model representations, and evaluates kernel, acquisition, representation, classical featurisation, and labelling-budget choices under a unified budget of 10\% of each full pool with a label-blind seed and a fixed held-out evaluation split. Across the benchmark, Tanimoto+UCB has the highest mean Recall@2\% point estimate among tested kernel-acquisition configurations, achieving \textbf{57.8\%} mean Recall@2\% across five random seeds (68.3\% when scored against the acquisition-eligible pool), compared with 9.6\% for random selection -- a gap that is significant by a paired Wilcoxon test across datasets ($p=0.0078$); its point estimate is not significantly different from RQ+UCB or Tanimoto+EI at five seeds. We adopt the continuous Tanimoto kernel of \citet{gessner2024}. The same configuration recovers the largest fractions of top binders in the influenza libraries (74.2\% on \texttt{3gbn\_h1}, 82.7\% on \texttt{3gbn\_h9}, and 84.9\% on \texttt{4fqi\_h3}) while exposing harder AAYL combinatorial landscapes where recall remains lower and more variable. An additional three-seed representation ablation, run under the original protocol and not repeated after the evaluation corrections, ranked ESM-2 650M highest (mean Recall@2\% 0.673 $\pm$ 0.28) among ProtBert, AntiBERTy, AbLang2, ProGen2, and classical encodings. On BindingGYM, the same configuration matches or exceeds ALLM-Ab on two of three datasets using the 100-sample held-out test metric. Structure-mapped Integrated Gradients and KernelSHAP analyses recover CDR-region attribution patterns consistent with contact-derived paratope geometry, though threshold-free (AUROC) analysis shows this qualitative agreement is not matched by strong residue-level discrimination. These results support Tanimoto-kernel GP active learning as a simple, reproducible strategy for label-efficient antibody affinity optimisation with qualitative structural validation.

title: Adaptive platform trials: A revolution or a fleeting trend? A review of the strengths and limitations
abstract: Platform trials have gained significant attention in recent years, particularly during the COVID-19 pandemic, for their potential to deliver efficient and flexible clinical research. Designed to evaluate multiple interventions within a single, ongoing infrastructure, platform trials allow for dynamic trial modifications, such as adding or removing treatment arms. These features offer potential advantages over conventional randomised controlled trials, including resource optimisation, reduced participant numbers, and faster evaluation of new therapies. Despite these potential strengths, the design and implementation of platform trials are associated with several methodological and logistical challenges that may undermine their validity. This review critically evaluates the platform trial methodology, exploring its potential to revolutionise clinical research or serve merely as a transient innovation. We discuss key advantages such as infrastructure reusability, cost-effectiveness, and efficiency in comparative effectiveness research. However, we also highlight significant limitations. These include a frequent lack of blinding, reliance on non-concurrent control groups, and the use of response-adaptive randomisation, all of which may introduce bias, reduce statistical power, and compromise internal validity. Additional issues such as increased ethical and regulatory complexity, underreporting of negative results, and insufficient realisation of theoretical efficiencies further temper the enthusiasm for this design. Evidence from recent systematic reviews reveals that many platform trials do not fully exploit their potential—40% have not added new arms, and only a minority conduct appropriate statistical adjustments for multiple testing. Nevertheless, simulations suggest long-term cost and time savings compared to traditional randomised controlled trials, assuming adequate implementation. We conclude that platform trials are not inherently flawed, although must be designed and conducted with rigorous methodological standards. Their success depends on maintaining core principles of trial integrity—especially reducing the risks of systematic, random, and design errors—while navigating operational and regulatory challenges. Platform trials are likely to become an integral part of the clinical trial landscape, provided they supplement, rather than compromise, the foundations of evidence-based medicine.

title: Lipid Nanoparticle-mRNA Vaccines for Infectious Diseases: Making A Potent Platform Predictable
abstract: Lipid nanoparticle (LNP)-mRNA vaccines compressed the path from pathogen sequence to licensed product into less than a year and are now approved for two diseases, with more than twenty indications in clinical development. The platform's potency is no longer in doubt; its predictability is. We argue that progress is now limited by three interfaces that are engineered largely independently: the lipid-RNA interface, which sets encapsulation, internal structure and storage stability; the particle-cell interface, which sets tropism and the efficiency of endosomal escape; and the particle-immune interface, which sets the balance between adjuvanticity and reactogenicity. Quantitative design rules exist for the first interface, remain empirical for the second, and are almost absent for the third, which is why formulation development still proceeds by screening rather than by calculation. We review the molecular design of the mRNA payload, the chemistry, manufacture and intracellular trafficking of LNPs, the immunological chain that links innate activation to germinal-centre output, and the clinical evidence across COVID-19, respiratory syncytial virus, influenza, cytomegalovirus, HIV and other targets. We conclude by identifying the measurements and design rules that would make the next generation of LNP-mRNA vaccines predictable rather than empirical.

title: Bridging the Gap Between Infection Prevention Guidance and Dementia Care: A Qualitative Study of HealthcareProfessionals’ and Family Caregivers’ Experiences
abstract: Abstract Background Infection prevention guidance is essential to the safety of older people receiving care, but its implementation may be difficult when recommendations do not account for the cognitive, behavioural and sensory needs of people living with dementia. We explored how healthcare professionals and family caregivers received, communicated and adapted infection-related guidance during the COVID-19 pandemic, and what their experiences suggest for future dementia care. Methods We conducted semi-structured interviews via Microsoft Teams with 10 healthcare professionals and 10 family caregivers in the UK between August 2024 and February 2025. Interviews explored experiences of accessing, interpreting and communicating infection-related guidance. Data were examined using reflexive thematic analysis. Results Three themes described receiving, sharing and adapting guidance. Participants reported frequent changes, delayed or unclear messages and limited dementia-specific advice. Isolation, visiting restrictions and mask wearing were described as difficult to implement when they conflicted with cognitive needs, established routines or emotional wellbeing. Professionals and caregivers often interpreted and adapted generic guidance themselves. Participants valued trusted and timely information, individually tailored explanations, concise language, visual and audio materials, and accessible repositories of verified resources. Conclusions Participants’ accounts reveal a gap between general infection prevention recommendations and their practical use in dementia care. Guidance designed with people affected by dementia, caregivers, and frontline professionals, and offered in accessible formats with proportionate implementation options, may support more feasible, person-centred responses to future outbreaks. The effectiveness of such approaches requires evaluation.

title: Adoption Strategies and Workarounds in the Evolution of Information Infrastructures Integrating Health and Social Care Providers in Scotland: Multimethod Qualitative Case Study of the Key Information Summary.
abstract: Background care records are digital technologies designed to support information sharing and care coordination across fragmented health and social care systems. However, adoption and use of these technologies can vary across diverse health and care settings, with users using workarounds and other strategies to meet their specific information needs. In Scotland, the Key Information Summary (KIS) has been in use for over 13 years, sharing key patient information from general practitioners (GPs) with other health and care providers for future care planning. Objective Using the KIS as a case study, this study examines how various adoption strategies and workarounds have shaped the evolution of regional information infrastructures integrating health and social care in Scotland over time. Methods This multimethod qualitative study examined the various contextual factors influencing adoption and use of the KIS across diverse health and care settings. Data collection included interviews with KIS users from health and care settings, implementers, and vendors; documentary analysis of user guides, websites, reports, and policies; and observation of multidisciplinary team meetings and technology use. Data analysis involved a hybrid approach. The technology-people-organization-macroenvironment framework was applied to code interview, documentary, and observational data, followed by an inductive analysis informed by science and technology studies theories of information infrastructures, domestication, and workarounds to examine strategies and workarounds for adapting the KIS to local contexts and evolving needs. Results Data comprised 54 qualitative interviews, 59 documents, 2 websites, and 20 hours of observational field notes collected between April 2024 and March 2025. Findings indicate that adoption of the KIS varied across settings and over time due to misalignment between system design, evolving expectations of integrated care, and national initiatives during the COVID-19 pandemic that repurposed its use. Professional roles and associated information needs shaped differing expectations of what constituted useful information, generating tensions between users who relied on the KIS and GPs responsible for maintaining it. Formal workarounds enabled the extension of the health care-centric infrastructure into nonclinical settings to facilitate information sharing with GPs and, in some cases, supported clinician access to the KIS during system outages. Across settings, informal user-driven repair practices enabled diverse professionals to adopt and realign the KIS with its intended use. Conclusions This study demonstrates how regional information infrastructures integrating health and care evolve incrementally as they become embedded within local routines, practices, and existing systems. Adoption was shaped by professional roles, information needs, and users' capabilities, with formal workarounds extending infrastructures into new settings and informal, user-driven repair practices supporting ongoing use and maintenance. Policymakers and vendors must recognize that workarounds and user-driven repair practices are central to infrastructural growth and sustainability, and understanding these strategies can inform future technology development and innovation.

title: Viral Infection‐Induced Epilepsy and the Gut Microbiome Crosstalk
abstract: ABSTRACT Viral infections of the central nervous system (CNS) pose a significant risk for seizures, and in some cases, long‐term epileptogenesis. Seizure development following viral infection involves diverse CNS mechanisms, with emerging evidence that peripheral factors, including gut microbiome composition and immune‐inflammatory responses, also contribute. The gut microbiome is a multifaceted ecosystem with important roles in CNS health, and advances in sequencing have enabled investigation of host and microbial genomic changes associated with seizure development. While both animal and human studies link gut dysbiosis to epilepsy, including infection‐induced epilepsy, the specific effects of viral‐induced seizures on the gut microbiome remain unclear. Moreover, the influence of virus‐triggered epileptogenesis is not well understood. This review summarizes current knowledge on viral infections linked to seizures and highlights the limited but growing evidence for gut microbial changes in this context. We focus on Zika virus (ZIKV), West Nile virus (WNV), and herpes simplex virus‐1 (HSV‐1), all implicated in human epileptogenesis, though direct microbiome–seizure connections are still limited. We also discuss severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus‐2 (SARS‐CoV‐2), which causes neurological symptoms without consistently inducing seizures in rodent models despite neurological involvement, and Theiler's murine encephalomyelitis virus (TMEV), a murine virus widely used as a model of infection‐induced seizures because it induces strain‐dependent seizures in mice. Current evidence suggests associations among viral infections, gut microbiome alterations, and seizure occurrence; however, further causative studies are needed to define their roles and elucidate underlying mechanisms.

title: Analytical Validation of MethyLiverDx-Sigma, a Plasma cfDNA Methylation Assay for Hepatocellular Carcinoma Detection.
abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma surveillance relies on ultrasonography and alpha-fetoprotein, both limited in sensitivity for early-stage disease; aberrant methylation of circulating cell-free DNA (cfDNA) offers a promising blood-based approach. Reported here is the analytical validation of MethyLiverDx-Sigma (MLDx-s), an assay that detects methylated RNF135 and DNMT3A in bisulfite-converted plasma cfDNA by methylation-specific PCR with high-resolution melting (HRM), with GAPDH as an endogenous control. Performance was evaluated following CLSI EP05-A3, EP07, EP12-A2, and EP37. Precision of quantification cycle (C q ) and melting peak temperature (T m ) was assessed by variance-component analysis within one site and across two sites and two operators. Because precision studies used bulk bisulfite-converted reference DNA, the reported coefficients of variation (CVs) primarily characterize the PCR-HRM detection module; end-to-end variability in clinical plasma specimens may be higher. Interference and cross-reactivity were evaluated in low-positive and contrived-negative samples against reproducibility-derived limits, with dose-response testing of reactive substances. Detection was 100% at both levels, and every run met control-validity criteria. C q repeatability CVs ranged from 0.53% to 1.68%, and total reproducibility CVs ranged from 1.10% to 2.37%; all T m CVs were ≤0.20%. All 18 interferents and 16 microbial cross-reactants evaluated in low-positive samples met the predefined acceptance criteria. In negative samples, hemoglobin, SARS-CoV-2, and measles virus produced concentration-dependent non-specific amplification, and dose-response testing established their respective no-effect concentrations. These findings characterize the analytical precision and multisite reproducibility of the PCR-HRM detection module and the analytical specificity of MLDx-s, complementing its previously reported clinical performance for plasma-based HCC detection.

title: Unequal Contagion
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic was a global emergency, but its health, social, and economic effects were highly uneven. In India—one of the world’s most unequal democracies—the pandemic and the policies enacted in response unfolded across a hierarchical social landscape and uneven institutional terrain, producing sharply differentiated experiences of risk, protection, and loss. Unequal Contagion: Citizenship, Democracy, and the Politics of COVID-19 in India brings together an interdisciplinary group of scholars to analyze how long-standing patterns of inequality shaped pandemic experiences, how those inequalities were intensified by state responses, and how historically rooted forms of social mobilization and citizen–state relations helped, in some contexts, to mitigate their effects. Employing wide-ranging methods, from surveys to ethnography, the chapters examine how centrally imposed lockdowns, disruptions to health systems, and uneven welfare provision interacted with class, caste, gender, religious, and regional inequalities. Seemingly universal policy responses often amplified vulnerability, particularly among migrants, informal sector workers, women, and other marginalized groups, leaving many without access to livelihoods, healthcare, or protection from violence. But responses varied substantially across states and localities, reflecting differences in state capacity and the strength of connections between citizens, civil society organizations, and government institutions. By linking subnational variation in pandemic policy and welfare outcomes to historically embedded patterns of social mobilization and political engagement, the book advances a relational and intersectional account of governance under stress, offering insights into inequality, citizenship, and democratic politics in India and other unequal societies.

title: Plasma-activated solutions alleviate intestinal mucosal injury induced by pathogen-host interactions by modulating redox imbalance.
abstract: Background SARS-CoV-2 spike binds angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 (ACE2), but the mechanisms linking spike exposure to intestinal injury remain incompletely understood. We investigated whether plasma-activated solutions (PAS) alleviate spike-associated intestinal injury by regulating antioxidant signaling. Methods Intestinal injury was induced by recombinant spike receptor-binding domain exposure in humanized ACE2 mice pretreated with dextran sulfate sodium. Caco-2 and HCT116 cells were used for in vitro experiments. PAS was administered orally to mice or applied as plasma-activated culture medium to cells. Reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels, apoptosis, and tissue injury were assessed. Protein stability assays, co-immunoprecipitation, and pathway interventions were used to investigate the underlying mechanism. Results Spike exposure increased oxidative stress and epithelial apoptosis and enhanced the association between Kelch-like ECH-associated protein 1 (KEAP1) and nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (NRF2), accompanied by increased NRF2 ubiquitination, reduced NRF2 stability, and lower heme oxygenase-1 (HO-1) expression. PAS alleviated intestinal injury, reduced ROS accumulation and apoptosis, decreased KEAP1-NRF2 association, and increased NRF2 nuclear accumulation. NRF2 knockdown or pharmacological inhibition of HO-1 attenuated the protective effects of PAS. Conclusion PAS alleviates spike-associated intestinal injury in the experimental models examined, with the findings supporting a contribution of KEAP1-NRF2/HO-1 signaling to its protective effects.

Methods Intestinal injury was induced by recombinant spike receptor-binding domain exposure in humanized ACE2 mice pretreated with dextran sulfate sodium. Caco-2 and HCT116 cells were used for in vitro experiments. PAS was administered orally to mice or applied as plasma-activated culture medium to cells. Reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels, apoptosis, and tissue injury were assessed. Protein stability assays, co-immunoprecipitation, and pathway interventions were used to investigate the underlying mechanism. Results Spike exposure increased oxidative stress and epithelial apoptosis and enhanced the association between Kelch-like ECH-associated protein 1 (KEAP1) and nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (NRF2), accompanied by increased NRF2 ubiquitination, reduced NRF2 stability, and lower heme oxygenase-1 (HO-1) expression. PAS alleviated intestinal injury, reduced ROS accumulation and apoptosis, decreased KEAP1-NRF2 association, and increased NRF2 nuclear accumulation. NRF2 knockdown or pharmacological inhibition of HO-1 attenuated the protective effects of PAS. Conclusion PAS alleviates spike-associated intestinal injury in the experimental models examined, with the findings supporting a contribution of KEAP1-NRF2/HO-1 signaling to its protective effects.

title: Assessing primary health care network preparedness for future pandemics in Lebanon
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic exposed critical gaps in health system preparedness worldwide, particularly within primary health care (PHC). In Lebanon, disparities between rural and urban and INGO-supported and non-INGO-supported primary health care centers (PHCCs) may affect the ability of PHCCs to respond to future pandemics. The Health Emergency Preparedness, Response and Resilience (HEPR) framework provides a structured approach to assess facility-level preparedness. To assess PHC preparedness for future pandemics in Lebanon and identify gaps requiring improvement. A health facility survey was administered to 185 eligible PHCCs nationwide, with 169 responses (91.4%). Findings were mapped across the 5 HEPR domains and analyzed using descriptive and unadjusted bivariate statistics, with statistical significance set at p < 0.05. Preparedness varied across HEPR domains. Timely reporting of priority communicable diseases through the national surveillance system was reported by 99.4% of PHCCs, whereas no PHCC reported a formal feedback mechanism to systematically address community concerns. Only 53.8% of PHCCs reported having an emergency plan, indicating an important gap in facility-level emergency preparedness. Countermeasures were readily available, although availability varied across vaccines, medicines, laboratory networks, and essential supplies. PHC pandemic preparedness in Lebanon showed strengths in surveillance and access to countermeasures but persistent gaps in emergency coordination, workforce preparedness, risk communication, and sustainable financing. This study demonstrates how a national HEPR framework can be operationalized at the PHC facility level, offering a practical approach for strengthening preparedness in fragile and crisis-affected settings.

title: Barriers to Seeking Mental Health Support Among Nurses and Midwives in Sub-Saharan Africa: A Scoping Review
abstract: Abstract Introduction: Psychological distress is widespread among nurses and midwives, especially in sub-Saharan Africa (SSA), where evidence primarily reports on the prevalence and not on the situation of seeking help. This scoping review identified barriers reported to seeking mental health-related support among nurses and midwives in SSA, and the strategies reported to facilitate the help-seeking process. Methods: The review was carried out following the Arksey-O'Malley framework and was reported using the PRISMA-ScR. The following criteria applied to the studies: Eligible studies were peer-reviewed articles published in English from 2020 to 2026. Records were independently screened by two reviewers, and data were charted on a standardised form, with findings thematically aggregated on the individual, organisational, and socio-cultural levels. Results: Sixty-two-three records were identified, of which 598 were not duplicates, and 20 studies were selected. Less attention was directed at help-seeking. Personal factors such as low self-identification with symptoms, low awareness and utilization of services available, and informal coping were identified as individual barriers. The organisational barriers were limited workplace support, heavy workloads, and, in one study, counselling related to increased resilience. Socio-cultural barriers involved were stigma, neglect, and isolation, mostly associated with COVID-19 and psychiatric nursing, and not psychiatric nurses' mental health itself. There was no study that appraised an intervention to encourage help-seeking. Conclusion: There is limited evidence of help-seeking among nurses and midwives in SSA, and evidence is often indirect. There is a need for workplace support for mental health to be strengthened and for more people to be aware of services; future studies should directly explore help-seeking, take a case-by-case approach to including nurses and midwives, assess interventions, and incorporate under-represented areas

title: Integrated epidemiological and genomic characterization of respiratory bovine coronavirus in U.S. cattle 2020–2025
abstract: ABSTRACT Bovine coronavirus (BCoV) is an important contributor to the respiratory disease complex in cattle; however, integrated genomic and epidemiological data describing currently circulating respiratory BCoV strains in the United States remain limited. The objective of this study was to monitor respiratory BCoV at the genomic level and analyze its epidemiological patterns over five years, in addition to assess the pathological findings of the currently circulating BCoV in cattle. A total of 4,505 respiratory samples submitted to a diagnostic laboratory between January 2020 and November 2025 were analyzed, of which 693 (15.38%) tested positive for BCoV. Positivity was highest in young calves (0–40 days; 20.0%) and declined significantly with increasing age based on logistic regression analysis. Temporal trend analysis using locally estimated scatterplot smoothing and the Mann–Kendall test showed no significant monotonic change in BCoV detection during the study period. Co-infections were commonly detected between BCoV and other viral respiratory pathogens, while bacterial pathogens predominated in many samples. Lung tissues submitted from bovine respiratory cases were screened by qRT-PCR, and selected samples with high viral loads were subjected to next-generation sequencing. Complete genome sequencing identified four respiratory BCoV isolates (~31 kb), all clustering within genotype GIIb with recent U.S. Comparative genomic analysis revealed amino acid substitutions in structural and non-structural proteins that may influence viral attachment, replication, and tissue tropism. These findings provide updated epidemiological and genomic insights into respiratory BCoV circulating in U.S. IMPORTANCE This study demonstrates continued detection and genetic evolution of respiratory bovine coronavirus (BCoV) among diagnostic respiratory samples submitted from U.S. cattle, with 15.38% positivity observed among 4,505 submitted samples and a higher proportion of positive submissions from young calves. Whole-genome sequencing of lung-derived isolates revealed consistent clustering within genotype GIIb alongside ongoing molecular diversification, including amino acid substitutions in spike, hemagglutinin-esterase, nucleocapsid, and membrane proteins, and the emergence of a previously unrecognized putative alternative ORF near 4.8-kDa NSP. These findings highlight that respiratory BCoV is continuously evolving at the site of disease. The observed genetic changes provide critical targets to refine diagnostic assays, support updating of vaccine strains, inform antiviral development, and enable more effective, evidence-based management strategies for controlling respiratory BCoV in cattle, requiring potential experimental validation.

title: A Structured Decision-Support Framework for Technology Adoption to Advance Airport Sustainability and Resilience
abstract: Airports face challenges in integrating sustainability and resilience into their long-term operational plans due to climate change, regulatory mandates, financial constraints, and disruptions such as the COVID-19 pandemic. While technology adoption plays a key role in addressing these issues, many airports lack structured strategies for evaluating, selecting, and implementing sustainability and resilience-focused innovations. Technology is often adopted reactively, driven by crises or regulatory compliance, rather than through proactive, strategic planning. This study introduces an empirically supported decision-support framework that combines established technology adoption models, sustainability and resilience assessment logic, and airport-specific implementation needs into a structured process for sustainable and resilient technology adoption. The framework synthesizes engineering-based maturity assessment, strategic planning, cross-disciplinary implementation, and Envision-based sustainability and resilience criteria, providing a tool that merges engineering judgment with organizational, regulatory, and environmental considerations. It equips airport decision-makers with a practical methodology for aligning technological innovation with operational performance, sustainability objectives, and long-term adaptability. The framework was empirically supported through expert input and statistical analyses of survey responses representing 27 commercial airports across the United States. An illustrative case study demonstrates an application of the framework by translating strategic sustainability and resilience goals into actionable implementation steps. This study contributes to the body of knowledge by presenting an evidence-based decision-support methodology that bridges the gap among strategic commitments and implementation, supports decarbonization, operational resilience, and infrastructure sustainability, while providing practical guidance for planners, sustainability leaders, and policymakers.

title: Socioeconomic Disparities in Dental Diseases and Related Behaviors Among Adults in Japan, 2022: A Nationwide Cross-sectional Study
abstract: Objectives: Socioeconomic disparities in oral health have been widely reported worldwide, yet evidence among adults in Japan remains limited. This study aimed to examine the associations between socioeconomic status (SES) and both dental diseases and oral health-related behaviors in a nationally representative sample of Japanese adults. Methods: We analyzed data from 28,617 participants in the 2022 Japan “COVID-19 and Society” Internet Survey (JACSIS), a nationwide, cross-sectional, web-based questionnaire. The exposure variable was equivalent household income, categorized into quintiles. Outcomes included self-reported periodontal disease, dental caries, and four dental behaviors: Daily tooth brushing, daily snacking, annual preventive dental visits, and annual treatment dental visits. Logistic regression analyses were conducted using inverse probability weighting (IPW) to adjust for potential selection bias, adjusting for demographic, socioeconomic, health-related, and regional covariates. Results: Lower equivalent household income was significantly associated with higher odds of dental disease and lower engagement in preventive or treatment-related dental visits. Participants in the lowest income quintile were more likely to report periodontal disease (adjusted odds ratios [AOR], 1.32; 95% confidence interval (CI), 1.06–1.65) or dental caries (AOR, 1.63; 95% CI, 1.29–2.05) and less likely to undergo annual preventive dental visits (AOR, 0.59; 95% CI, 0.51–0.69) compared with those in the highest quintile. A dose–response relationship was observed for some outcomes. Conclusion: Clear socioeconomic disparities exist in both dental diseases and preventive behaviors among adults in Japan. Policies promoting preventive dental visits and reducing income-related inequalities are essential to achieving equitable oral health and mitigating broader health disparities.

title: Monitoring Air Pollution Dynamics of NO2 and SO2 in Sri Lanka Using Sentinel-5P from 2019 to 2024
abstract: Abstract Air pollution monitoring in developing nations is constrained by sparse ground-based infrastructure, making satellite remote sensing an essential alternative. This study analysed the spatiotemporal dynamics of nitrogen dioxide (NO 2 ) and sulfur dioxide (SO 2 ) across all 25 administrative districts of Sri Lanka from 2019 to 2024 using Sentinel-5P TROPOspheric Monitoring Instrument (TROPOMI) Level-3 satellite data integrated with Geographic Information Systems (GIS). Monthly raster maps were generated from Near Real-Time (NRTI) and Offline (OFFL) datasets processed through Google Earth Engine, with column densities converted to estimated surface concentrations in parts per billion (ppb). Results revealed persistently elevated NO 2 concentrations in the western coastal corridor (Colombo, Gampaha, and Kalutara), attributable to high traffic density, urban growth, and industrial activity. SO 2 hotspots were concentrated around industrial point sources in Puttalam and Kalutara, particularly near thermal power generation facilities. Both pollutants exhibited pronounced seasonal variability driven by southwest and northeast monsoon patterns, with lower concentrations recorded during high-rainfall months. A marked reduction in NO 2 was observed during the 2020 COVID-19 lockdown period, corroborating the anthropogenic origin of urban emissions. Comparison of NRTI and OFFL products demonstrated complementary utility for short-term event detection and long-term trend analysis respectively. These findings provide a cost-effective, spatially comprehensive framework for national air quality management and environmental policy planning in Sri Lanka.

title: LPNs/LVNs in Long-Term Care, Hospitals, and Home Health: A Comparative Analysis.
abstract: Background Demand for long-term care (LTC) in the United States is projected to surge, but the supply of LPNs/LVNs who constitute a large and growing segment of its workforce has stagnated. Purpose The aim of this study is to compare demographic and professional characteristics of the LPN/LVN workforce across LTC, hospital, and home health settings. Methods Data drawn from the 2024 National Nursing Workforce Survey were used to support a detailed descriptive analysis and binary logistic regression models examining potential drivers of emotional exhaustion in the LPN/LVN workforce. Results LPNs/LVNs in LTC tend to be more racially diverse than those in hospital and home health settings. They are also more likely to report working in rural areas, holding multiple positions, and drawing a higher median salary. LPNs/LVNs working in LTC are also more likely to report higher burnout, workloads, understaffing, and intent to leave compared to their counterparts in hospitals and home health settings. Conclusion Evidence suggests that the LTC workforce has yet to rebound from COVID-19-related attrition. This deficit, coupled with stagnant enrollment and licensure statistics over the past decade, alongside projected increases in demand for LPNs/LVNs in LTC across the country, underscores a tenuous and unsustainable future for the industry. To safeguard the care of vulnerable populations, interventions are needed that prioritize retention, incentivize reentry into practice, and deploy policies to expand the LPN/LVN pipeline.

title: Barriers and Enablers to Asynchronous Secure Messaging Use in Hospital-Based Ambulatory Specialty Clinics in Ontario, Canada: Convergent Mixed Methods Study.
abstract: Background The COVID-19 pandemic accelerated the adoption of virtual care, including patient-to-provider asynchronous secure messaging (ASM). However, while ASM offers access and convenience, the surge in message volume can increase physician workload and contribute to burnout. Furthermore, it has raised additional concerns about message appropriateness, medicolegal liability, and sustainability of this communication virtual care modality. Objective This study aims to explore the experience with ASM in Ontario in specialty ambulatory care to inform current practice support strategies. We sought to characterize messaging usage quantitatively while also exploring experience with messaging, contextual barriers, and facilitators qualitatively. Methods We used a convergent mixed methods design, analyzing aggregated electronic health record (EHR) usage and qualitative interview data. The study was conducted at a large ambulatory care hospital in Ontario, Canada, across four high-messaging specialty clinics: mental health, rheumatology, dermatology, and surgery. Quantitative data (October 2019 to Octtober 2022) included message volumes, response patterns, and timing. Semistructured interviews with physicians, nurses, administrative staff, and patients (n=19), conducted in 2022 explored ASM workflows, barriers, and facilitators. Quantitative data were analyzed descriptively, stratified by clinic. Qualitative data were analyzed using thematic analysis, informed by an interpretative phenomenological orientation. Findings from the two strands were then compared to identify areas of convergence and divergence. Results Message volumes surged post pandemic, particularly in mental health, ranging from about 6000 in surgery, rheumatology, and dermatology to close to 13,000 messages in mental health across the study period. Message rate per patient per month was 0.6 (SD 0.2; mental health), 0.5 (SD 0.2; rheumatology), 0.2 (SD 0.2; dermatology), and 0.2 (SD 0.1; surgery). Physicians averaged 12.6 (SD 8.0) messages/month (rheumatology) and 7.6 (SD 4.4) messages/month (mental health) in clinics without nursing support. Nurses handled 27.4 (SD 11.6) messages/month (surgery) and 19.2 (SD 14.1) messages/month (dermatology). Three percent (1263/38,370) to 10% (3619/36,022) of provider messages were sent outside regular hours. The majority of conversations (2156/6859, 46% to 6913/13,615, 62%) had only a single reply. Physicians reported challenging experiences due to increased workload, lack of compensation, and poor integration into local clinical workflows. High patient-to-physician ratios and limited nursing support for message triage were associated with a poor messaging experience. Patients and administrative staff valued messaging for its convenience, accessibility, and efficiency. A key finding was insufficient engagement across all user groups in decisions about messaging implementation. Conclusions The study highlights a disconnect between the high perceived value of ASM for patients and administrative staff and the challenging experiences of physicians. Successful implementation requires thoughtful integration into care models, clear guidelines for appropriate use, and proper triage and "channel management" to guide patients to appropriate modalities. Future research should explore triaging algorithms as part of a digital front door, specialty-specific variations, and the crucial role of nursing staff in message channel management.

Future research should explore triaging algorithms as part of a digital front door, specialty-specific variations, and the crucial role of nursing staff in message channel management.

title: Using the HPO framework to guide healthcare transformation: evidence from a five-year organizational case study
abstract: High performance in healthcare requires coordinated improvement across leadership, culture, processes and outcomes; yet, few frameworks combine an organization-wide diagnosis with an explicit transformation process. This study examines how the high-performance organization framework was used to guide a five-year transformation at a Dutch addiction treatment clinic and what contribution the framework plausibly made to the changes observed. A longitudinal organizational case study was conducted at the Tactus Intensieve BehandelKliniek. Two anonymous repeated cross-sectional diagnoses, conducted in 2017 and 2022, were combined with 22 semi-structured interviews, site visits, an internal progress review, an annual plan and operational indicators. The analysis reconstructed a document-supported chain linking diagnostic priorities, high-performance guided interventions, intermediate organizational changes and observed outcomes. Because respondent-level data and a comparison group were unavailable, the study does not estimate a causal treatment effect. The Intensieve BehandelKliniek’s average high-performance score increased descriptively from 5.1 in 2017 to 7.2 in 2022, while interviews indicated stronger trust, role clarity, collaboration and process discipline. Contemporaneous organizational records show that changes in leadership, communication, multidisciplinary teamwork and quality management formed the action bundle selected, coordinated and monitored through the high-performance transformation process rather than unrelated parallel initiatives. Client-related and flow indicators improved by 2022. Financial results remained volatile, but Intensieve BehandelKliniek’s 1.1% margin in 2022 was positive and modestly above aggregate benchmarks for the Dutch mental healthcare sector, supporting a cautious conclusion of sector-relative stabilization rather than sustained financial improvement. Staff perceived established high-performance routines as helpful during the COVID-19 crisis, but the design cannot test whether the high-performance organization transformation mitigated the effects of the crisis. The study contributes a five-year, mechanism-oriented account of how a high-performance organization framework can function as transformation architecture in healthcare. It identifies a contribution pathway from diagnostic sensemaking and focused prioritization, through managerial ownership, to the institutionalization of continuous improvement, while explicitly delimiting the causal claims that a single-case design can support.

title: Strategies for Teaching Store-and-Forward Teledermatology: A Survey of U.S. Dermatologists
abstract: Abstract Background Teledermatology, a vital component of the COVID-19 pandemic, involves transmitting images of skin conditions to dermatologists from other providers or patients directly. The swift adoption of store-and-forward (SAF) teledermatology in residency programs highlighted the need for structured resident education amidst patient care priorities and logistical challenges. Since utilization of teledermatology has grown, we recognized the importance of identifying the strategies faculty use to teach future dermatologists SAF teledermatology. Methods The study employed a seven-step medical education questionnaire design process. A national survey was distributed in July 2024 to 127 teledermatology educators. The survey included questions about program characteristics and the use and effectiveness of ten educational strategies. The responses from the questionnaire were summarized with descriptive statistics through Microsoft Excel, and free-response questions were categorized with inductive coding. Results 52 dermatologists (40.9% response rate) across all nine census bureau divisions of the US participated. The three strategies that teledermatology educators use most often include asking residents for differential diagnoses and leading diagnoses on images (n = 36 [92.3%]), reviewing relevant morphology (n = 36 [92.3%]), and describing systematic approaches to diagnosis and management (n = 31 [79.5%]). These three strategies were also rated as the most effective. Conclusions A systematic questionnaire development process identified critical educational strategies for teaching SAF teledermatology. These included soliciting diagnoses, reviewing morphology, and outlining diagnostic and management plans. Dermatology educators may consider utilizing these strategies to optimize teledermatology teaching to residents.

title: Chirality-Driven Photonic PCR Enables Label-Free Genetic Amplification
abstract: Photonic polymerase chain reaction (PCR) offers a rapid alternative to conventional thermal cycling for genetic amplification, but current platforms are limited by low photothermal conversion efficiencies and a dependence on bulky fluorescent monitoring systems 1–6 . Here we report a chirality-driven photonic amplification paradigm that achieves both accelerated nucleic acid replication and direct, label-free detection. By leveraging chiral plasmonic nanoparticles, we exploit their elevated absorption cross-sections to achieve exceptional light- to-heat conversion and rapid thermal relaxation, significantly accelerating heating and cooling rates during cycling. We show that localized chiral near-fields generated by these chiral plasmonic nanoparticles optimize DNA polymerase conformational dynamics, lowering the activation energy barrier for synthesis and boosting amplification efficiency. Furthermore, by tracking the reaction with circular dichroism spectroscopy, we directly monitor the intrinsic chiroptical signature of amplifying DNA, completely eliminating the need for external fluorescent dyes or labeled probes. We validate this system using SARS-CoV-2 E-gene plasmid DNA templates, demonstrating rapid, label-free amplification and single-copy detection within clinically relevant timelines. By bridging asymmetric photothermal dynamics with chiral-field-induced enzymatic activation, this work translates chiroplasmonic materials from fundamental physics into high-performance, point-of-care molecular diagnostics.

title: Experimental assessment of medical plastic waste pyrolysis and steam gasification for resource recovery.
abstract: Medical plastic waste (MPW) has become a major environmental concern due to its massive production in clinics and hospitals, and the limited recycling options, especially after the COVID-19 pandemic. In this context, thermochemical technologies represent a promising approach to simultaneously reduce and valorize this waste by producing three main streams of value: a gaseous, a liquid, and a solid stream. In this study, the thermochemical conversion of four representative categories of MPW (non-woven medical textiles, FFP2 face masks, Pasteur pipettes, and natural latex gloves) was experimentally evaluated under different operating conditions. The experiments were conducted in a laboratory-scale fluidized-bed reactor at temperatures between 750 and 850°C using N 2 at 8 NL min -1 or N 2 plus steam (6 NL min -1 N 2 + 2 NL min -1 steam) as the process atmosphere, in order to compare predominantly pyrolytic and steam gasification conditions. These conditions correspond to nominal freeboard residence times of approximately 2.4-2.6 s. The results revealed a strong influence of both feedstock composition and operating conditions. The gas composition varied significantly with the type of MPW, leading to H 2 and CO contents reaching up to 30 vol% and 20 vol%, respectively, both for FFP2 face masks under N 2 and at 750°C. Carbon conversion to the gas phase achieved a maximum of approximately 45%. Steam addition significantly reduced carbon retention in the char fraction, while the unaccounted carbon fraction remained substantial under several steam gasification conditions. Tar analysis showed that benzene, toluene and xylene (BTX) compounds predominated for polypropylene- and polyethylene- based MPW, whereas natural latex gloves exhibited a greater tendency towards the formation of substituted aromatic compounds, naphthalene derivatives and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons. Overall, these findings demonstrate the potential of thermochemical conversion to recover valuable products from selected MPW fractions and provide an experimental basis for identifying suitable feedstock-specific operating conditions. Further development towards industrial implementation will require consideration of process efficiency and environmental performance.

title: CXCL14 and Igsf8 are involved in double-stranded DNA and Alum adjuvant-mediated immune reaction.
abstract: The chemokine CXCL14 is known to bind CpG oligonucleotides and promote their uptake by dendritic cells and macrophages, thereby activating TLR9 in endosomes/lysosomes. However, it remains to be clarified whether CXCL14 also interacts with double-stranded DNA (dsDNA) and promotes its intracellular transportation. In this study, we demonstrate that CXCL14 forms a complex with dsDNA, and that this complex is internalized via immunoglobulin superfamily (Igsf) proteins. Furthermore, we found that stimulation with aluminum salt particles (Alum) adjuvant, which is involved in dsDNA-mediated innate immune responses, elicits IFN-β production in the presence of the CXCL14/dsDNA/Igsf8 complex. This result suggests that Igsf8-mediated intracellular delivery of the CXCL14/dsDNA complex is required for the Alum-induced Type I interferon responses. Finally, immunization with a SARS-CoV-2 spike protein together with the Alum adjuvant increased IgG1 antibody production in wild-type mice, but not in Igsf8-knockout mice. These results suggest that CXCL14 and Igsf8 are involved in the immune responses mediated by dsDNA and the Alum adjuvant.

title: Cooling related household expenditure proxies and heatstroke mortality in an ecological panel study of Japanese prefectures from 2013 to 2022
abstract: Heatstroke (ICD-10 T67) mortality in Japan concentrates among adults aged ≥ 65 years. Whether cooling-related household electricity expenditure modifies the temperature – mortality relationship remains uncertain across proxy operationalisations. Ecological panel of 47 Japanese prefectures, 2013–2022 (n = 470). A summer–shoulder electricity expenditure ratio (SSR’) was tested alongside three positive (carbonated drink, ice cream, mineral water) and two negative (gas, kerosene) expenditure proxies from the Family Income and Expenditure Survey, using Poisson regression with two-way fixed effects, prefecture-clustered robust standard errors, and offset on population aged ≥ 65 years. Five alternative thermal indicators provided sensitivity analyses. Temperature anomaly had a large main effect (IRR = 1.325, p < 0.001), robust across all thermal indicators. The primary temperature × SSR’ interaction was non-significant (IRR = 1.031, p = 0.252); carbonated drink reached nominal significance (IRR = 1.062, p = 0.019), with five of six proxies directionally concordant. The 2020 year fixed-effect was non-significant (IRR = 1.10, p = 0.39) despite the period’s highest temperature anomaly (+ 1.57 °C), and the 2020-excluded estimate matched the full sample—indicating that extreme heat, not COVID-19, drove the 2020 mortality peak. Substituting tropical-night counts (days with minimum ≥ 25 °C) for daytime peak temperature yielded a significant negative interaction with SSR’-electricity (IRR = 0.917, p = 0.017), suggesting that cooling-related expenditure specifically attenuates the effect of failed nocturnal cooling on heatstroke mortality. Behavioural and nocturnal heat dimensions, captured respectively through carbonated-drink expenditure and tropical-night exposure, warrant individual-level investigation as targets for heatstroke prevention.

title: From shopping to indulgence: longitudinal analysis of retail diversity of Bağdat Avenue in Istanbul, Türkiye
abstract: This study investigates adaptive resilience of high streets in emerging markets under a “triple shock”: the COVID-19 pandemic, hyperinflationary economic volatility and intense urban transformation. The study demonstrates how functional diversity acts as an enabler for high street evolution from a “transaction-oriented” structure to an “experience-oriented” cluster of activities. The study employs a longitudinal field investigation of a premier retail corridor of Bagdat Avenue, Istanbul, Türkiye. Data were collected through on-site surveys of 209 buildings including 318–368 retail units across 2020, 2021 and 2025. Functional diversity was operationalised through a standardized sectoral taxonomy and using non-parametric testing structural changes over time have been assessed. The study reveals that despite unfavourable economic conditions and subsequent uncertainty, vacancies declined dramatically between 2020 and 2025. This recovery was not a “return to the old normal” but a functional transformation. While financial services contracted due to digitalization and increasing rents, the avenue “bounced forward” through expansion of experience economy, specifically in cafe and restaurant, personal care and cosmetics and jewellery and accessories sectors. Although core retail functions remained structurally stable, the high street evolved from a transaction-oriented environment toward an “experience-oriented” indulgence environment. This study contributes to high street resilience theory by empirically demonstrating how functional diversity operates as a dynamic risk-mitigation mechanism under multiple concurrent external shocks. Findings from this research challenge narratives of high street decline and offer actionable insights for place-makers, investors and policy-makers seeking to enhance the adaptive capacity of prime urban retail streets.

title: Infantile amnesia results from differential memory retrieval in humans
abstract: Infantile amnesia, the inability to recall memories from our earliest years, is the most common form of forgetting in mammals 1 . Whether early memories never form, decay, or persist but become inaccessible remains unknown. Here, we investigated the nature of forgetting during the infantile amnesia period by longitudinally testing toddlers aged 18-24 months across the complete memory cycle from encoding, initial retrieval one day later, and delayed retrieval up to six months later, in a novel naturalistic episodic memory paradigm. Computational modelling revealed that forgetting during the infantile amnesia period was heterogeneous. Toddlers were as likely to retain the full memory as to lose it completely, while nearly a quarter retained only part of the memory. Encoding accuracy predicted which toddlers retained the full memory at the test one day later, but not at the delayed test up to six months on. Instead, a retrieval-specific EEG signature predicted complete, but not partial, memory retrieval, distinguishing which toddlers had retained the full memory before their behavioural response. Finally, leveraging the COVID-19 pandemic as a natural experiment, we found that maternal immune activation during pregnancy, as in rodents 2 , alters vulnerability to infantile forgetting in humans. Together, these findings show that early memories formed during the infantile amnesia period are not simply erased but persist in an increasingly inaccessible form, a transformation whose trajectory can be shaped by both the neural retrieval mechanism and the prenatal environment.

title: Stories from 'Who Cares?' : Cultivating a Community of Aging Care on the Sunshine Coast, British Columbia.
abstract: Background Canada's rapidly aging population poses unique challenges for rural and remote communities such as the Sunshine Coast, British Columbia. Objective Through creative community engagements and community-based participatory research, the Who Cares? project explored experiences of aging and approaches to care by gathering stories from across the Sunshine Coast. Methods Qualitative data were gathered from numerous community gatherings and twelve one-on-one interviews. Findings Reflexive and collaborative thematic analysis revealed that gaps in health services, staffing, and social supports, which were exacerbated by the COVID-19 pandemic, have since deepened isolation among older adults. Structural barriers included inadequate transportation, housing insecurity, and limited health care access. Findings also revealed that despite these stories of need, communities on the Sunshine Coast demonstrated resilience through informal care networks, volunteerism, and collaborative caregiving practices that transcended institutional settings. Discussion These findings point to the need for systemic and community-driven approaches to aging care that prioritize equity, accessibility, and proactive planning, while recognizing care as a shared responsibility embedded in relationships and community assets.

title: Planning for Calamity: Deep Uncertainty, Resilience, and the Next Catastrophe.
abstract: Healthcare disaster preparedness has advanced substantially during the past quarter century, yet catastrophes continue to expose vulnerabilities when events and system behavior differ from expectations. Experience from September 11, Hurricane Katrina, Superstorm Sandy, the Las Vegas mass shooting, and COVID-19 demonstrates that dissimilar catastrophes repeatedly stress many of the same interconnected components of healthcare delivery. Because the next catastrophe cannot be predicted reliably, preparedness must extend beyond anticipated events and prescribed responses to preserving essential function when assumptions fail. We distinguish capabilities-the resources, personnel, structures, processes, and services available to perform a function-from capacities that allow capabilities to remain usable or be reconfigured under changing conditions. We introduce ADSTARS (Absorptive, Distributive, Surge, Transformative, Adaptive, Reserve, and Sustainment capacities) as a synthesis of capacities supporting resilience. Planning for catastrophe should preserve not only what healthcare systems possess, but what they remain able to do when conventional arrangements fail.

title: Eco-sustainable organic solvent-free spectrophotometric method for the concurrent determination of a ternary pharmaceutical mixture.
abstract: In recent years, green analytical chemistry has become essential in pharmaceutical research, aiming to mitigate environmental hazards associated with conventional analytical practices. The current focus lies in optimizing analytical methods to achieve both environmental and economic sustainability. In this framework, three environmentally sustainable spectrophotometric methods were developed for simultaneous analysis of three co-formulated drugs: acetaminophen, dextromethorphan hydrobromide, and pseudoephedrine hydrochloride, which are often used to alleviate symptoms associated with COVID-19. The employed spectrophotometric methodologies include the double divisor-ratio spectra derivative method, the mean centering of double divisor ratio spectra method, and the dual wavelength in ratio spectrum method. The innovative techniques displayed good linearity within 25-350 μg/mL for dextromethorphan hydrobromide, 2-24 μg/mL for acetaminophen, and 100-1400 μg/mL for pseudoephedrine hydrochloride. The environmental sustainability of the proposed methods was evaluated using the Analytical Eco-Scale, analytical greenness metric, and the Green Analytical Procedure Index. Furthermore, complementary evaluations of blueness and whiteness were conducted through the Blue Applicability Grade Index and the Red Green Blue 12 metric, respectively. The collective outcomes of all evaluation metrics clearly demonstrated that the proposed methods possess enhanced environmental compatibility and sustainability relative to the existing techniques. The proposed methods were fully validated according to the International Conference on Harmonization recommendations. The developed methods offered a cost-effective and eco-friendly approach for concurrent determination of acetaminophen, dextromethorphan hydrobromide, and pseudoephedrine hydrochloride in their bulk substances, and pharmaceutical formulations.

title: Professional development for primary science teachers: a systematic literature review of international and Chinese research
abstract: This study systematically reviews professional development for primary science teachers, emphasizing digital competencies and science, technology, engineering and mathematics or STEM-oriented instruction. There were 30 peer-reviewed studies published between 2020 and 2024 analyzed from Scopus and China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI) databases, integrating international and Chinese perspectives. Quality assessment considered research design, instrument validity, data transparency, and alignment between findings and conclusions. The review identifies four professional development orientations: system-driven, innovation-driven, sustainability-oriented, and capacity-building. Chinese programs are largely centralized and policy-aligned, whereas international programs emphasize teacher autonomy, collaborative innovation, and long-term sustainability. The COVID-19 pandemic accelerated online and blended professional development adoption, revealing both opportunities for digital competency development and inequities in access. Findings contribute a cross-cultural synthesis of professional development structures, strategies, and outcomes for primary science teachers. Implications include designing scalable, equitable, and context-sensitive professional development programs, particularly in resource-limited settings such as rural China and developing countries. Future research should focus on longitudinal evaluation, cross-cultural comparisons, and rigorous assessment of digital competency integration to enhance teacher professional learning and inform policy and practice globally.

title: Artificial Intelligence for Intelligent and Privacy-Preserving Healthcare: A Survey of Medical Image Analysis, Multimodal Diagnosis, Semi-Supervised Learning, and Personalized Healthcare Systems
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly embedded in healthcare, from image-based diagnosis to patient-facing management tools, yet the supporting literature is fragmented across communities that rarely read one another. Motivated by the need for a coherent view, this survey examines four recent peer-reviewed studies that together span multimodal COVID-19 diagnosis, privacy-preserving learning on encrypted medical images, graph-refined semi-supervised pathology classification, and an AI-enabled mobile application for personalized healthcare management and doctor recommendation. Using a structured narrative methodology, the reviewed studies are classified into a five-category taxonomy, compared along technical dimensions, healthcare capabilities, and reported limitations, and synthesized into a layered view that treats imaging, multimodal fusion, privacy preservation, label-efficient learning, and personalization as complementary layers of intelligent healthcare rather than independent technologies. The synthesis indicates that each study advances one layer under its own experimental setting, and that none addresses privacy, label efficiency, multimodality, explainability, and clinical validation together. Recurring gaps include limited clinical validation, dataset constraints, unquantified generalization across institutions, privacy–performance trade-offs, and inconsistent evaluation protocols that prevent direct numerical comparison. Future directions include privacy-preserving multimodal learning, reduced reliance on annotations, explainable and robust models, integration of imaging with clinical records, and multi-site clinical validation. This review is not exhaustive, and no new experiments are presented.
journal: International Journal for Research in Applied Science and Engineering Technology

title: A Scoping Review of Human–Computer Interaction Research on the Accessibility of Data Visualizations: New Technologies, Procedures, and Designs
abstract: Data visualizations are vital for communication and decision-making, yet accessibility barriers limit their effectiveness for people with disabilities. While earlier literature reviews examined Human-Computer Interaction (HCI) research on visualization accessibility, there has not been an analysis that accounts for recent seismic shifts in software, hardware, design and experimental protocols due to Artificial Intelligence (AI), the COVID-19 pandemic, and greater awareness of accessible technologies. To analyze the impacts of this shift on accessible visualization research, we reviewed 280 HCI publications and coded target communities, visualization types, interaction types, and methods, contrasting articles published before and after 2021. Our corpus identified a sharp increase in publications after 2021 along with an expansion to a broader range of target communities, including people with CVD, IDD, and ADHD. Empirical and artifact contributions still dominate, with studies after 2021 showing a higher proportion of empirical studies. Participatory approaches are increasing but still remain limited. Research mainly focuses on charts and web-based, text-driven interactions, with articles after 2021 indicating a growing interest in multimodal and AI-driven systems. We further dissect this recent surge, positioning it against earlier work to identify trends, limitations, and open questions to guide future research.

title: Minimally processed cow's milk and early childhood asthma-related outcomes: exploratory findings from the early terminated MARTHA randomized trial
abstract: Background: Raw milk consumption has repeatedly been shown to be inversely related to asthma, respiratory infections, and allergies but carries a potential risk of life-threatening infections. The MARTHA trial (DRKS00014781) used minimally-processed pasteurized milk as a microbiologically safe proxy for raw milk and compared it against ultra-heat-treated milk for efficacy on atopic sensitization, asthma, and respiratory infections. Methods Healthy children were recruited through birth clinics in Germany. At 6 to 12 months, they were centrally randomized to obtain minimally-processed full-cream versus ultra-heat-treated semi-skimmed cow's milk daily until age 3 years. During the SARS-CoV-2 pandemic, recruitment was stopped, and the study was continued without confirmatory intention. The primary endpoint was shifted from asthma as composite parent-reported diagnosis of asthma or recurrent obstructive bronchitis until age 5 to atopic sensitization at age 3 years. Participants, caregivers, and study staff were blinded to group assignments. Results We randomized 130 individuals into each study arm. The intervention was unrelated to atopic sensitization (risk ratio, RR=1.13 [0.67-1.89]), which occurred in 28 individuals of the intervention (n=99) and 24 of the comparator group (n=96). Asthma showed a trend for an inverse association (hazards ratio, HR=0.55 [0.27;1.16], n=252), which was pronounced in the 82 children with a family history of asthma (post-hoc HR=0.30 [0.09;0.93]). The intervention was inversely associated with rhinitis and cough in the older half of the children (post-hoc RR=0.82 [0.67-0.998] and RR=0.75 [0.60-0.94], respectively). No adverse events were judged intervention-related. Interpretation The intervention did not reduce atopic sensitization at age 3 years. Exploratory analyses suggested possible protective effects on asthma and respiratory symptoms, particularly in children with parental asthma and in those less affected by pandemic-related disruptions. These findings justify but do not replace a definitive trial. Funding Dutch Longfonds; Bavarian State-Ministry of Health, Care and Prevention; German Center for Lung Research (DZL); FrieslandCampina.

title: Research Trends in Telogen Effluvium From 1975 to 2025: A Bibliometric Analysis
abstract: Telogen effluvium (TE) is a common cause of diffuse hair loss. Bibliometric analyses systematically map research trends to identify influential studies and reveal knowledge gaps. To characterize research trends, influential publications, and knowledge gaps in the telogen effluvium literature through bibliometric analysis of the most cited articles. Web of Science was searched from inception to May 2025 for studies involving patients with TE. Animal studies, non‐English articles, reviews, and abstracts were excluded. Bibliometric data including citation count and citations per year were extracted and manually analyzed. The 100 most cited articles were published between 1976 and 2023 with 2787 total citations (mean: 27.9 per article; total corpus h‐index of 30). Articles were classified into seven thematic categories. Associations between TE and comorbidities/exposures were most frequent ( n = 42), followed by treatment/management ( n = 25) and disease characterization ( n = 14). Quality of life/psychosocial impact was the smallest category ( n = 3). There was a large increase in citations in COVID‐19‐related publications in 2020–2021. Only six randomized controlled trials were identified. This analysis was restricted to Web of Science, potentially excluding articles indexed only in Scopus, Embase, or PubMed, among others. Also excluded were non‐English studies, citation bias favoring older articles, reliance on manual thematic categorization rather than software‐based network analysis, and the absence of formal inter‐rater agreement statistics. Psychosocial outcomes, diagnostic criteria, and the ferritin‐hair loss relationship represent the most consequential underexplored areas. Future research should prioritize validated patient‐reported outcome measures, standardized diagnostic criteria, and adequately powered trials of nutritional interventions.

title: Gamified flipped learning and the affective domain of language learning: a qualitative case study of online English classes
abstract: Gamification and flipped learning have each been linked to enhanced learner engagement, but qualitative accounts of their combined, semester-long use in online language classrooms remain scarce, particularly in Indian higher education, and the affective domain is rarely examined as a central construct in its own right rather than as a by-product of achievement studies. This exploratory qualitative case study addresses this gap by examining how undergraduate students perceived the influence of gamified flipped online English instruction on the affective domain of their language learning at a university in Chennai, India, during the COVID-19 pandemic. Methodologically, an intact Foundation English cohort ( n = 28) received pre-class materials (videos, audio recordings, and presentation slides) and played daily in-class digital games designed on the Kahoot and LearningApps platforms over one semester; 10 students volunteered for end-of-semester, semi-structured, one-on-one interviews, and transcripts were analysed in NVivo 14 using a codebook approach to thematic analysis, proceeding through initial coding, theme development, and theme review and refinement, supported by a structured codebook and co-author consensus review of the coding. Ten themes emerged under the parent construct of the affective domain: motivation and the engaging nature of the games were the most pervasive. Participants also reported gains in self-confidence, a sense of social presence, and a preference for collaborative play, and they described boredom during uninterrupted gameplay and inconsistent use of the pre-class materials, which led them to prefer in-class conceptual explanation before playing. The findings reflect context-bound perceptions rather than measures of learning outcomes; they nevertheless suggest that sequencing games after conceptual input and combining competitive and skill-oriented platforms may support positive affective states in online language classes. Thus, the study contributes qualitative evidence to a field predominantly served by quantitative designs. Implications and directions for triangulated future research are discussed.

Participants also reported gains in self-confidence, a sense of social presence, and a preference for collaborative play, and they described boredom during uninterrupted gameplay and inconsistent use of the pre-class materials, which led them to prefer in-class conceptual explanation before playing. The findings reflect context-bound perceptions rather than measures of learning outcomes; they nevertheless suggest that sequencing games after conceptual input and combining competitive and skill-oriented platforms may support positive affective states in online language classes. Thus, the study contributes qualitative evidence to a field predominantly served by quantitative designs. Implications and directions for triangulated future research are discussed.

title: The Evolution of (Post) Pandemic Labour Market Outcomes of Older Workers in Europe
abstract: The COVID‐19 pandemic caused extensive work disruptions, particularly affecting older workers, defined as those aged 50 and above. Using longitudinal data from the Survey of Health, Ageing and Retirement in Europe (SHARE), we examine the relationship between work disruptions during the first pandemic wave and later labour market outcomes. Workers experiencing disruptions had a higher probability of labour market withdrawal in 2021 and 2022. Patterns vary across welfare regimes, with labour market exit more strongly associated with retirement in Mediterranean countries and restricted non‐employment (unemployment or homemaking) in Central‐Eastern Europe, while results for Nordic countries are less conclusive.

title: Actin remodeling by human RNA virus: mechanisms and targeted intervention
abstract: The actin cytoskeleton is a central dynamic network in eukaryotic cells which preserves morphology, motility, and intracellular transport. Extensive research has confirmed the importance of actin in RNA viral infection. Actin remodeling, as a core host mechanism exploited by RNA viruses, strongly affects viral replication and transmission efficiency. This article reviews the key regulatory molecules involved in actin dynamics. Based on this foundation, we focus on recent advances in the molecular mechanisms by which six representative human RNA viruses(severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus-2, influenza A virus, respiratory syncytial virus, dengue virus, ebola virus and human immunodeficiency virus) hijack the host actin network, revealing the actin hijacking pathways that RNA viruses tend to select. Finally, we further summarize the current status of research on antiviral compounds that target the actin signaling pathway. Given that targeting host factors offers the unique advantage of broad-spectrum antiviral activity, this strategy offers promise for overcoming drug resistance caused by high viral mutation rates. However, its clinical application still faces difficulties in balancing cytotoxicity and efficacy. This article intends to provide a conceptual framework for novel antiviral intervention approaches targeting actin.

title: Standardized Annotation of Quantitative Proteomics Datasets Using SDRF-Proteomics.
abstract: Proteomics datasets require detailed and standardized metadata annotation to ensure reproducibility, reusability, and alignment with FAIR (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable) principles. This chapter presents a practical, hands-on workflow for annotating a label-free proteomics dataset using the Sample and Data Relationship Format for Proteomics (SDRF-Proteomics), a HUPO-PSI and EuBIC-MS standard that has been adopted by major proteomics data repositories. We demonstrate the process on a COVID-19 nasal-swab dataset (PXD020394), showing how to derive sample and assay metadata from the study files, encode them in SDRF with the lesSDRF web application, and validate the result. Although the worked example is label-free, the approach can be generalized to other quantification strategies.

title: Aplicación del kit de ELISA "COVID AR IgG" en muestras de suero de perros y gatos del área metropolitana de Buenos Aires
abstract: Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) has caused millions of confirmed cases in humans, while 929 cases have been reported in animals in 42 species. The aim of this study was to evaluate the pet-adapted COVID AR IgG ELISA kit, to detect the presence of seric specific antibodies against the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein in dogs and cats from the Buenos Aires Metropolitan Area (AMBA), Argentina, from July 2020 to April 2022. Significant levels of seroreactivity were found in both dogs (32%) and cats (21%), compared with those levels in a pool of 112 pre-pandemic sera (8.1%). In dogs, the OR (Odds Ratio) obtained suggests a possible association between positive results and SARS-CoV-2 exposure. However, in cats, more information is needed to support a possible association. In addition, we found insufficient evidence for an association between seroreactivity and the presence of any symptom (p-values of 0.223 and 0.781 for dogs and cats, respectively).

title: Fibroid-like Uterine Lesions and Fibroid-Associated Structural Changes in a Long-Term Murine Hepatitis Virus-1 Model
abstract: The number of patients with long COVID continues to rise as COVID-19 persists, yet research on its implications for female reproductive health remains scarce. Long COVID is linked to an increased risk of abnormal uterine bleeding, heavier menstrual flow, prolonged periods, and breakthrough bleeding. We therefore examined whether uterine changes occur in an animal model of long COVID. Female A/J mice were inoculated with murine hepatitis virus strain 1 (MHV-1), a murine coronavirus model used to investigate long COVID-like sequelae, and a subset of infected mice received the synthetic peptide SPIKENET (SPK). Mice infected with murine hepatitis virus strain 1 (MHV-1) showed chronic uterine inflammation and myometrial changes exhibiting fibroid-like features one year post-infection. We also observed changes in α-SMA, desmin, h-caldesmon, and vimentin staining, suggesting a myometrial origin for the lesions. Further, we found pathological changes that include hyperplastic foci in the outer layer of the myometrium, a uterus with intraluminal proteinaceous fluid, and a circumscribed, round-to-oval focus of benign hyperplastic myometrium with spindle nuclei and eosinophilic cytoplasm, with interspersed small, round lymphocytes and plasma cells, consistent with mild chronic inflammation. MHV-1-inoculated mice also showed an oviduct with several lymphocytes located toward the lumen, as well as a uterus with an ectatic lumen, inspissated intraluminal fibrinoid material, and mild-to-moderate subendometrial chronic inflammation (with scattered small lymphocytes). Additionally, immunofluorescence showed increased expression of conventional and unconventional uterine fibroid markers, including PLP1, versican, PR-A, PR-B, MSH2, TGF-β1 and 3, IGF-1, CA125, and HMGA2. Serum biomarker analysis showed increased IGF-1 levels but not increased levels of the other proteins identified by immunofluorescence. Furthermore, histopathology showed no uterine fibroid-like lesions in MHV-1-inoculated mice treated with the synthetic peptide SPK (known to prevent MHV-1 and SARS-CoV-2 infection in animals). Moreover, SPK prevented increases in the above-mentioned fibroid markers as measured by immunofluorescence and partially reduced IGF-1 expression in the serum. These findings suggest that uterine fibroids may develop during long COVID in humans.
