title: Respiratory pathogens detected by multiplex PCR in Malaysian public hospitals: prevalence and epidemiologic patterns from January 2023 until July 2024.
abstract: Respiratory tract infections remain an important cause of hospitalisation and diagnostic uncertainty, and multiplex polymerase chain reaction testing offers rapid detection of multiple pathogens in routine clinical practice. We aimed to describe the prevalence, demographic associations, and temporal trends of respiratory pathogens detected by the QIAstat-Dx Respiratory SARS-CoV-2 Panel in Malaysian public hospitals. This multicentre retrospective cross-sectional study included nasopharyngeal swab samples from cases with suspected acute respiratory infections tested between 1 January 2023 and 31 July 2024. Data were collected from participating sites using standardised record forms and analysed. We assessed overall positivity, pathogen frequencies, age-group and regional distributions, and monthly and quarterly trends. A total of 8,361 samples were included, of which 5,252 (62.8%) had at least one pathogen detected. Single detections were identified in 4,279 samples (51.2%), while co-detections were observed in 973 samples (11.6%). Viral pathogens predominated. Rhinovirus/enterovirus was the most frequently detected pathogen (23.8%), followed by respiratory syncytial virus A/B (13.7%) and influenza A H1N1/2009 (4.8%). Positivity was highest among children aged 1 to 4 years and infants aged 1 to 11 months, and age-related variation was more pronounced than regional variation. The leading pathogens also demonstrated distinct temporal profiles, with different peak months across the study period. In conclusion, respiratory pathogen detection in this hospital-based population was characterised by a high positivity rate, predominance of viral pathogens, marked age-related differences, and distinct temporal patterns. These findings support the value of multiplex PCR for respiratory pathogen surveillance in Malaysian public hospitals.

title: Interferon-Induced Protein 6 (IFI6): Biological Functions, Molecular Mechanisms and Pathological Roles in Human Diseases
abstract: Interferon (IFN)-induced protein 6 (IFI6) is an important member of the IFN-stimulated gene (ISG) family. It plays significant roles in anti-apoptosis, immune regulation, maintenance of mitochondrial homeostasis, antiviral defense, and tumor progression. At the molecular mechanism level, IFI6 inhibits mitochondrial membrane depolarization, cytochrome c release, and caspase activation. It also regulates the balance between B-cell lymphoma 2 (Bcl-2)/Bcl-2 interacting mediator of cell death (Bim), activates the Janus kinase (JAK)/signal transducer and activator of transcription (STAT) and phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase-protein kinase B (PI3K-AKT) pathways, and upregulates the ferroptosis-related proteins solute carrier family 7 member 11 (SLC7A11) and glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4), thereby enhancing cell survival and proliferation through multiple pathways. In terms of immune regulation, IFI6 is associated with immune cells (such as T/B cells, etc.) and the tumor microenvironment. IFI6 regulates mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (mtROS) and mitochondrial calcium homeostasis, influencing respiratory chain assembly and metabolism. In terms of viral infection, IFI6 may inhibit the replication of multiple viruses (such as hepatitis B virus (HBV), hepatitis C virus (HCV), SARS-CoV-2, etc.) by inhibiting flavivirus-induced endoplasmic reticulum (ER) invagination, interfering with retinoic acid-inducible gene I (RIG-I)-like receptor signaling pathways, and inhibiting epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) kinase activity. In addition, IFI6 is highly expressed in autoimmune diseases and malignant tumors and is associated with proliferation, metastasis, and poor prognosis. In this review, we aim to highlight IFI6 as a potential key target in disease diagnosis and treatment.

IFI6 regulates mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (mtROS) and mitochondrial calcium homeostasis, influencing respiratory chain assembly and metabolism. In terms of viral infection, IFI6 may inhibit the replication of multiple viruses (such as hepatitis B virus (HBV), hepatitis C virus (HCV), SARS-CoV-2, etc.) by inhibiting flavivirus-induced endoplasmic reticulum (ER) invagination, interfering with retinoic acid-inducible gene I (RIG-I)-like receptor signaling pathways, and inhibiting epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) kinase activity. In addition, IFI6 is highly expressed in autoimmune diseases and malignant tumors and is associated with proliferation, metastasis, and poor prognosis. In this review, we aim to highlight IFI6 as a potential key target in disease diagnosis and treatment.

title: Biotin-dependent metabolism controls germinal center fate and vaccine-induced antibody diversification
abstract: Nutrient availability shapes antibody responses, yet its role in metabolic checkpoints governing germinal center (GC) B-cell differentiation remains incompletely defined. Using heterozygous (HZ) Slc5a6 M60K mice modeling human loss-of-function mutations in the multivitamin transporter SLC5A6, we found that deficient biotin imports impaired mitochondrial metabolism and restricted preGC-to-dark zone progression after vaccination. Single-cell transcriptomics and RNA velocity revealed disrupted GC trajectories, while B-cell receptor repertoire analysis showed impaired class-switch recombination, somatic hypermutation, and vaccine-induced clonal diversity. Spatial multiplexed imaging showed reduced GL7-high GC-associated B-cell regions. Flow cytometric analyses revealed reduced frequencies of RBD-specific B cells and RBD-specific GL7 + CD95 + GC B cells in HZ mice, with higher frequencies after biotin supplementation. Pseudovirus assays demonstrated impaired neutralization of Wuhan-Hu-1 and Omicron BA.2. Dietary biotin supplementation restored GC-associated differentiation, antibody diversification, and vaccine-induced humoral responses. These findings identify biotin-dependent mitochondrial metabolism as an important checkpoint linking micronutrient availability to GC B-cell differentiation and vaccine responsiveness.

title: Viral and Inflammatory Lung Injury: Pathophysiology, Diagnostic Strategies, and Clinical Management
abstract: Acute respiratory disease may arise from viral infection, bacterial colonization, inhaled toxicants, or complex interactions between pathogens and host immunity. Although these conditions have different initiating causes, they can converge on airway epithelial injury, inflammatory-cell recruitment, altered surfactant function, impaired gas exchange, and, in severe cases, acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS). This integrative narrative review synthesizes the supplied literature on SARS-CoV-2, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), bacterial airway inflammation, lung metabolism, respiratory mechanics, inhalation injury, and biopsy findings in nonresolving ARDS. The reviewed studies indicate that respiratory pathology is heterogeneous: similar clinical syndromes may reflect different tissue-level processes, and extrapulmonary manifestations can accompany respiratory infection. Clinical assessment therefore benefits from combining symptoms and oxygenation with microbiological testing, imaging, respiratory-mechanics assessment when indicated, and selective histopathology in unresolved cases. Supportive care should be individualized to disease severity and underlying physiology, while invasive procedures and anti-inflammatory treatment require careful patient selection. Because this is a narrative synthesis of previously published studies rather than a new patient cohort, no pooled effect estimate or original clinical outcome is reported. The findings support a structured, mechanism-informed approach to diagnosis and management and highlight the need for prospective studies using standardized phenotyping.

title: Computational Workflows to Capture Molecular Flexibility in the Design of Peptide-Based Therapeutics
abstract: Peptides have emerged as a highly promising class of therapeutics, offering unique advantages such as high specificity, versatility, and low toxicity. Experimental advances in modification strategies have addressed key limitations of poor proteolytic stability and rapid clearance, facilitating the clinical translation of peptide-based therapeutics. However, computational peptide design remains challenging despite rapidly developing computational methods, including artificial intelligence tools such as AlphaFold. The intrinsic flexibility of peptides complicates reliable prediction of peptide protein structures and interactions, which is essential for structure-based drug design. To address this challenge, we developed computational workflows combining diverse strategies, including docking and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, to accurately model and design peptide-based therapeutics. We focused on the following target systems: the main protease (Mpro) and papain-like protease (PLpro) of severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), modeled with natural substrates and peptide inhibitors, and the prostate specific membrane antigen (PSMA) in complex with peptide-based radiopharmaceuticals. We developed the computational dynamic saturation mutagenesis (CDSM) protocol for automated saturation mutagenesis at each peptide position using MD simulation snapshots to capture the flexibility of peptide–protein interactions. The resulting binding free energy deviations from parent residues served as design suggestions, enabling the generation of an 8-amino acid peptide inhibitor with high binding affinity for Mpro, validated by in vitro inhibition assays (IC50 = 4.8 ± 0.5 μM). To elucidate the structure-activity relationship of PSMA radioligands, we investigated the binding modes of eight clinically relevant radioligands using a workflow that combines docking at varying hydration levels, re-scoring of docking poses, and MD simulations to generate accurate and stable ligand poses. To date, this represents the most comprehensive computational modeling study of PSMA radioligands. The computational modeling and design strategies presented in this thesis—especially the CDSM protocol, which is broadly applicable to various peptide-protein systems, as well as the workflows for elucidating PSMA-radioligand interactions—lay the groundwork for future development of peptide-based therapeutics.

title: Molecular and Physiological Regulation of ACE2: Interaction with TMPRSS2, Glycosylation-Dependent Processing, and Roles in Skin Pigmentation
abstract: Das Angiotensin-konvertierende Enzym 2 (ACE2) ist ein membrangebundenes Enzym des Renin-Angiotensin-Systems und der zelluläre Rezeptor für SARS-CoV-2. Für den Viruseintritt ist zudem die transmembrane Serinprotease TMPRSS2 erforderlich, die das Spike-Protein aktiviert und ACE2 spalten kann. Diese Dissertation untersucht die Beziehung zwischen ACE2 und TMPRSS2 in zellulären und in-vivo-Modellen. Die Ergebnisse zeigen, dass TMPRSS2 eine Trans-Autoaktivierung durchläuft und aktives TMPRSS2 mit ACE2 interagiert. Dadurch werden Verarbeitung, proteolytische Spaltung, Zelloberflächenlokalisation, intrazelluläre Retention und Freisetzung von löslichem ACE2 beeinflusst. Die N-Glykosylierung von ACE2 reguliert Reifung, Membrantransport, Oberflächenexpression, Interaktion mit TMPRSS2 und Anfälligkeit für Shedding. In TMPRSS2-Knockout-Ratten stützen die verringerte TMPRSS2-Aktivität und erhöhte ACE2-Spiegel im Gewebe eine physiologische Rolle von TMPRSS2 bei der ACE2-Freisetzung. Darüber hinaus untersucht die Arbeit ACE2 in Hautbiologie und Melanogenese. ACE2-defiziente Mäuse zeigten veränderte Fellpigmentierung, erhöhten Melaningehalt und Veränderungen melanogenese-assoziierter Genexpression, beeinflusst durch Geschlecht und Haarzyklusphase. Insgesamt zeigen die Ergebnisse TMPRSS2 als Regulator der ACE2-Verarbeitung, des Transports und des Sheddings und weisen auf eine zusätzliche Rolle von ACE2 bei der Hautpigmentierung hin.

title: Economic Burden of Post-COVID Syndrome in Germany Between 2021 and 2025: A Statutory Health Insurance Claims Data Analysis
abstract: Evidence on the economic burden of post-COVID syndrome in Germany remains limited. This study quantifies post-COVID-associated healthcare resource utilization (HCRU), sick leave, and costs. To compare HCRU, sick leave, and costs borne by the statutory health insurance (SHI) among incident pediatric and adult post-COVID patients with matched post-COVID-free controls. This retrospective cohort study analyzed an anonymized German SHI claims database provided by GWQ ServicePlus AG. The observation period spanned October 2021 to June 2025 and included all individuals with incident COVID-19 diagnosis until September 2024. Incident post-COVID was defined as the first ICD-10-GM code (U07.4!; U09.9!) recorded ≥90 days after first COVID-19 diagnosis. Post-COVID cases were exactly matched 1:2 to post-COVID-free COVID-19 controls by calendar quarter of incident COVID-19 diagnosis, acute severity, cohort entry quarter, 5-year birth interval, sex, and Elixhauser Comorbidity Index. We estimated mean differences in HCRU, sick leave, and direct SHI-borne costs per case. Rate ratios of HCRU, sick leave, and costs per person-year were estimated using Poisson (HCRU/sick leave) and linear (costs) regression. Analyses covered 365-day, 730-day, and any follow-up period. We matched 25 485 identified post-COVID cases with 49 671 controls. Matched cases and controls were comparable in age, sex, and comorbidities. Overall, during 365 days of follow-up, post-COVID patients showed higher HCRU and sick leave rates across all sectors, especially sick leave days. Mean differences per case were greatest for sick leave days (365 days: +27 days) and outpatient physician contacts (365 days: 6.9 contacts). HCRU and sick leave rates remained significantly increased over extended follow-up periods. Total SHI-borne costs per person-year were higher among post-COVID patients across all follow-up periods (all P < .001). Sector-specific costs per person-year were increased primarily in the outpatient sector and for sickness benefits (all P < .001). Mean total cost differences per case were +€1806 per case (365 days) and mean excess sickness benefits per case were +€1077. Documented post-COVID was associated with a substantial and sustained economic burden on the German healthcare system and society. Targeted strategies are needed to mitigate potential long-term impacts on HCRU and labor productivity.

title: Nanoparticles improve targeting and efficacy of endocytosis inhibitors
abstract: Endocytosis is a critical cellular process exploited by many viruses, including HIV-1 and SARS-CoV-2, for host cell entry. Inhibiting this pathway provides a promising antiviral strategy; however, existing small-molecule inhibitors often suffer from limited solubility, off-target effects, and poor bioavailability. This study reports the synthesis and evaluation of gold nanoparticles functionalized with novel endocytosis inhibitors, Les-6623 and Les-6632. The compounds were synthesized via a linear Knoevenagel condensation pathway and structurally confirmed by NMR and LC-MS spectroscopy. Molecular docking predicted more favorable interactions of Les-6623 and Les-6632 with dynamin-2 than those predicted for chlorpromazine, a classical endocytosis inhibitor. PEGylated gold nanoparticles were functionalized with the inhibitors, yielding formulations characterized by UV-Vis, fluorescence spectroscopy, ATR-FTIR, DLS, and TEM analyses. Functional assays in SH-SY5Y and BEAS-2B cells showed that AuNP_Les-6623 and AuNP_Les-6632 reduced the cellular fluorescence associated with transferrin, HIV-1 Tat, and SARS-CoV-2 Spike protein under the experimental conditions tested. Free chlorpromazine was included as a reference inhibitor. These findings support the biological activity of the investigated nanoparticle formulations under the tested conditions, while further format-matched controls are required to determine the specific contribution of nanoparticle presentation to the observed activity.

title: A Subjective Bayesian Approach to Address Unchecked Assumptions in a Causal Analysis
abstract: Causal analyses using observational data rely on identifying assumptions that cannot be verified from the observed data alone. When such unchecked assumptions fail, effect estimates may be biased and uncertainty may be understated. We propose the Adjusted Model for Unchecked Assumptions (AMUA), a subjective Bayesian framework that propagates uncertainty about the joint validity of key causal assumptions through a two-component posterior mixture. One component corresponds to the standard observational causal model in which the assumptions hold (referred to as the"assumption-hold component"); the other represents a flexibly defined model that allows the causal assumptions to fail (referred to as the"assumption-fail component"). The mixture weight $\pi$ is specified by the analyst as the prior probability assigned to the assumption-hold component. This formulation leads to a new diagnostic, $\pi_{\min}$: the smallest value of $\pi$ for which the 95\% HPD set for the average treatment effect (ATE) excludes zero. In simulations with a spatially structured unmeasured confounder, we evaluate bias, interval length, and coverage as $\pi$ varies. The results show that acknowledging assumption uncertainty can widen intervals, and improve coverage relative to analyses that treat the assumptions as certain. In a county-level application relating long-term PM$_{2.5}$ exposure to COVID-19 mortality, AMUA shows how posterior conclusions depend on prior confidence in the identifying assumptions.

One component corresponds to the standard observational causal model in which the assumptions hold (referred to as the"assumption-hold component"); the other represents a flexibly defined model that allows the causal assumptions to fail (referred to as the"assumption-fail component"). The mixture weight $\pi$ is specified by the analyst as the prior probability assigned to the assumption-hold component. This formulation leads to a new diagnostic, $\pi_{\min}$: the smallest value of $\pi$ for which the 95\% HPD set for the average treatment effect (ATE) excludes zero. In simulations with a spatially structured unmeasured confounder, we evaluate bias, interval length, and coverage as $\pi$ varies. The results show that acknowledging assumption uncertainty can widen intervals, and improve coverage relative to analyses that treat the assumptions as certain. In a county-level application relating long-term PM$_{2.5}$ exposure to COVID-19 mortality, AMUA shows how posterior conclusions depend on prior confidence in the identifying assumptions.

title: Analysis of the impact of subsidies on biological inputs for shrimp production in Mexico using instrumental variables
abstract: In Mexico, shrimp farming is characterized by an inherently volatile business model, with a “high risk, high return” profile. To date, there is no causal evidence to determine the effect of subsidies on biological inputs for shrimp production in the country. This study addresses the following research question: what is the causal effect of subsidies on biological-inputs on shrimp production in Mexico? This study estimates the causal effect of subsidies on biological inputs (specifically, postlarvaes) using the Local Average Treatment Effect (LATE) with a two-stage least squares (2SLS) design during the 2018–2019 period. The instrumental variable (IV) analysis reveals that subsidies on biological inputs, particularly shrimp larvae, had a LATE effect of 109.95 tons on farms with semi-intensive production systems, whereas on farms with intensive systems, the average effect was 82.56 tons in shrimp production during the 2020–2025 period. This is the first causal study conducted on subsidies for biological inputs in the aquaculture industry in Mexico. The results obtained contribute to the debate on the redesign of support programs, with the aim of mitigating basic financial risks and promoting the modernization of the sector, especially considering the post-COVID-19 landscape.

title: Widespread Human Exposure to Liquid Crystal Monomers: Population-Scale Urinary Biomonitoring Reveals Spatial, Demographic, and Environmental Patterns across Several Regions in China
abstract: Liquid crystal monomers (LCMs) are emerging contaminants released from electronic products and e-waste throughout their life cycle. However, population-level evidence of human internal exposure to fluorinated and nonfluorinated LCMs remains largely unknown. This study aimed to characterize human exposure to 49 LCMs in urine and examine the spatial, demographic, and environmental variability in exposure across several regions in China. We measured 49 LCMs in 597 first-morning urine samples collected from general populations across four urban and rural regions in eastern and western China using GC-MS/MS. Detection frequencies, concentration distributions, and estimated daily intake (EDI) were assessed. Nonparametric subgroup analyses were used to characterize demographic heterogeneity, and multivariable regression models were used to evaluate associations with environmental and policy-related factors. LCMs were detected in 99.7% of urine samples, with 31 compounds exceeding 80% detection frequency. The median total concentration (∑49LCMs) was 30.5 ng/mL, with fluorinated LCMs contributing 55.5% of the total burden. Urban populations showed higher concentrations and greater variability than rural populations. Urinary LCMs showed significant heterogeneity across age, body mass index, and occupational groups, whereas sex-related differences were limited. Higher urinary LCM levels were associated with temperature and humidity, while the novel coronavirus 2019 (COVID-19) policy indicators showed weak associations. Screening-level EDI estimates further identified several LCMs as priority compounds for future exposure assessment. This study provides multiregional biomonitoring evidence of widespread occurrence of LCMs in urine across several regions in China. Spatial and demographic variability suggests combined influences of environmental conditions, indoor source intensity, and population characteristics. The substantial contributions of both fluorinated and nonfluorinated compounds underscore the need for further investigation of exposure sources and compound-specific toxicokinetics.

title: Ethical aspects of triage in civil and military contexts: a qualitative research of physicians’ attitudes and knowledge regarding ethics in triage scenarios in
abstract: Triage in the medical context is a screening procedure used to determine resource distribution in situations of severe restriction of medical resources. Originally, triage was designed as a method to ascertain the treatment priority of wounded soldiers on battlefields. However, ethical discussions about clinical triage were raised during the COVID-19 pandemic. In the focus stood prioritization of care in situation of limited resources. The purpose of our investigation was comparison of experiences and ethical attitudes towards triage among military and civil physicians. To date, there is no research available on this topic. We conducted 26 semi-structured, qualitative, exploratory interviews among military and civilian physicians in Germany. All the interviews were digitally audio-recorded, transcribed and anonymized. We analyzed the transcripts via the structured qualitative content analysis method. Triage scenarios bring distinctive ethical challenges for the attending physicians. Military and civil physicians share a similar approach to solve the ethical conflicts arousing in such situations. Triage situation does not allow for an individual medical gold standard in the treatment of patients; therefore, the principles of autonomy, beneficence and nonmaleficence should be subordinated to the principle of social justice. Because of restriction of the patient's autonomy, the final decision-making authority lies with medical professionals. Pre-clinical triage conditions also restrict patient-physician relationship. The ethical justification of triage follows the imperatives of life-preservation and maximization of the number of survivors. According to interviewed physicians, in both pre-clinical and clinical triage situations, medical decisions should aim rather at maximizing the well-being of the collective – whether of wounded or of a society – than at maximizing the well-being of an individual patient. Restriction of patient autonomy regarding treatment discontinuation – ex-post triage – is unavoidable in a pandemic situation.

title: Sex-related signatures in the plasma proteome not attributable to XX and XY chromosomes and their impact on health and disease
abstract: Sex differences in human health are typically modeled as binary comparisons between males (XY) and females (XX). However, sex-linked molecular traits vary continuously and are shaped by environmental factors. Here, we introduce the Proteomic Sex Index (PSI), a continuous, plasma proteomics-based measure that quantifies the degree to which an individual's proteome aligns with their chromosomal sex, with higher PSI values indicating profiles less typical for their sex. Leveraging data from 51,310 individuals from six demographically heterogeneous cohorts, we show that PSI captures broad, biologically meaningful variation in sex-enriched traits and diseases. Individuals with proteomic profiles shifted away from their chromosomal sex exhibited trait values less characteristic of that sex. For example, males with higher PSI were shorter, had lower grip strength, and showed reduced severity of COVID-19 (OR=0.59, p=3.0x10-7). Analyses of individuals undergoing gender-affirming hormone therapy showed that, although PSI correlated with circulating sex hormones, it also captured additional variation independent of hormone levels. PSI is partially heritable and genetically influenced. Individuals with Klinefelter syndrome (XXY) had markedly elevated PSI (OR=13.7, p=1.1x10-13), and genome-wide association studies of PSI identified sex-biased cis-pQTLs with evidence of causal links to sex-specific disease risk. PSI provides a nuanced, individualized measure of sex-related biology that enables the study of within-sex molecular variation and its links to health and disease.

title: The Effect of Capital Adequacy Ratio (Car), Non-Performing Loan (NPL), and Net Interest Margin (NIM) on Return on Assets (ROA) At PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia (Persero) Tbk Period 2016-2025
abstract: This study examines the individual and joint associations of the Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR), Non-Performing Loan (NPL), and Net Interest Margin (NIM) with Return on Assets (ROA) at PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia (Persero) Tbk during 2016–2025. Using a quantitative descriptive approach, the study analyzes secondary data obtained from the bank’s annual financial statements over ten annual observations. Multiple linear regression was conducted using SPSS version 27, supported by descriptive statistics and diagnostic tests. The results indicate that CAR (t = −0.194, p = 0.853), NPL (t = 0.209, p = 0.841), and NIM (t = 1.744, p = 0.132) are not individually statistically significant predictors of ROA at the 5% significance level. The joint F-test also indicates that the three variables are not statistically significant as a group (F = 3.085, p = 0.112). The adjusted coefficient of determination is 0.410, indicating an adjusted explanatory proportion of 41% for the fitted model. The study contributes context-specific evidence on banking profitability during a period encompassing the COVID-19 pandemic and subsequent recovery, while highlighting the need to interpret the findings cautiously given the limited number of annual observations. These results suggest that further research using longer time series, additional explanatory variables, or comparative data from multiple banks may provide a more comprehensive understanding of the determinants of bank profitability.

title: The Effect of Fee-Based Income, Bank Size, Bank Capital, Non-Performing Loans, and Operational Efficiency on Bank Financial Stability
abstract: Banking crises have consistently demonstrated that the resilience of the financial system depends on the soundness of individual banks. Meanwhile, declining interest income has encouraged banks to diversify their revenue sources, particularly through fee-based income. However, empirical evidence regarding the contribution of fee-based income to bank financial stability remains inconclusive. This study examines the effect of fee-based income on bank financial stability, controlling for bank size, bank capital, non-performing loans, and operational efficiency. Unlike previous studies that measure bank size using total assets, this study adopts the bank classification based on core capital introduced in 2021 and incorporates the COVID-19 pandemic period. Using a quantitative approach, this study analyzes annual financial reports from 40 commercial banks listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during 2019–2022, resulting in 160 bank-year observations. The sample was selected using purposive sampling, and the data were analyzed using panel data regression with EViews 10. The common effect model was selected based on the reported model-selection tests. The findings indicate that fee-based income, bank capital, non-performing loans, and operational efficiency are not statistically significantly associated on bank financial stability, whereas bank size has a positive association. These findings suggest that fee-based income has not yet emerged as a significant contributor to bank financial stability, while banks with higher core capital classifications tend to exhibit greater stability. Future research should extend the observation period, incorporate digitalization, corporate governance, and macroeconomic factors, and conduct comparative analyses across bank categories.

title: Media representations of Chinese migrants in the Spanish press: A critical discourse analysis of El País and El Mundo (2020-2025)
abstract: This study examines how Chinese migrants are discursively constructed through mainstream press coverage in Spain in the wake of COVID-19. Focusing on coverage in El País (centre-left) and El Mundo (centre-right), the analysis draws on critical discourse analysis to examine 81 news articles published between 2020 and 2025. The findings show that Chinese migrants are predominantly positioned within homogeneous and stereotypical frames that mark them as peripheral outsiders to Spanish society. Despite ideological differences, both newspapers rely on similar media agendas—particularly integration, culture, and crime—through which boundaries of inclusion and exclusion are discursively produced. El Mundo , as a conservative press, focuses on constructing a universe of crimes with collective and generalized images of Chinese immigrants, based on the traditional news production routine of the Western press that represents immigration as a threat for the host society. In contrast, El País , as a liberal-minded newspaper, implicitly conveys discriminatory discourses, transmitting racism through its critics and cultural concerns. By foregrounding processes of hierarchy, normalization, and exclusion, this study contributes to debates on ethnicity, migration, and media by demonstrating how everyday journalistic practices reproduce otherness and internal differentiation within migrant communities in a Southern European context.

title: Land reform, agricultural resilience and food security under systemic shock: evidence from Africa
abstract: Land reform remains contentious in Southern Africa, where the implications of redistribution for productivity, food security and resilience depend on complementary resources and institutions. This study examines African agriculture and Zimbabwe's post-land-reform system during COVID-19 as a systemic stress test. A sequential explanatory mixed-methods design integrated a 2000–2022 panel covering 54 African countries with a thematic synthesis of 13 documents representing 11 evidence families relevant to Zimbabwe. Segmented panel models, two-way fixed-effects specifications, dynamic models, interaction tests, country-placebo analyses and robustness checks examined agricultural value added per worker, cereal yield and undernourishment. Documentary themes were integrated with panel findings through a joint display. Pandemic-period associations with productivity and cereal yield were not consistently negative. Undernourishment estimates were suggestive but sensitive to model specification, covariance estimation and pre-existing trends. Zimbabwe's estimated trajectories differed significantly from broader African patterns, but its estimates were not exceptional within country-placebo distributions. Joint tests did not support moderation by inflation or irrigation. Documentary evidence identified labor, input, financial, logistical, market and institutional disruptions, alongside adaptation supported by favorable rainfall, input programs, extension services and infrastructure. Production continuity coexisted with impaired food access, heightened vulnerability and incomplete recovery. The findings are consistent with the Land Reform–Knowledge–Resilience Framework, suggesting that productive opportunities following redistribution depend on knowledge, finance, infrastructure, markets, institutions and macroeconomic stability. Production continuity alone does not establish resilience. The integrated evidence supports interpretation of plausible mechanisms without establishing causal effects of COVID-19 or land reform.

title: Individualized Online Exercise Training Across Adulthood: A Qualitative Study of Perceptions, Barriers, and Facilitators
abstract: Despite well-established health benefits of regular physical activity, participation rates remain suboptimal among adults, particularly older adult populations. More evident during the COVID-19 pandemic, online exercise training has emerged as an interesting strategy for different groups of individuals to remain physically active. The present study explored perceptions, barriers, and facilitators of online exercise training in adults at different stages of adulthood. This qualitative study was a secondary analysis of de-identified data from semi-structured interviews previously conducted by an exercise specialist with 14 adult participants who had engaged in online exercise training for at least one year. Interviews were conducted via Zoom, transcribed verbatim, and analyzed thematically by the research team. Across the 14 interviews with adults at different stages of adulthood (aged 34-71 years), four major themes emerged: (1) benefits of online exercise training, (2) enablers of online exercise training, (3) challenges of online exercise training, and (4) client and professional profile. Participants described perceived benefits, barriers, and facilitators of online exercise training, including convenience, individualized guidance, technological challenges, and digital literacy demand. These findings provide context for understanding how adults across adulthood, including older adults, experience online exercise training but do not establish comparative effectiveness, causal effects on adherence, or sustained engagement.

title: ESG uncertainty and volatility dynamics in the most polluted sectors: a GARCH-MIDAS approach
abstract: Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) uncertainty has emerged as an important source of financial risk, particularly for pollution‐intensive industries that are highly exposed to sustainability‐related policy and regulatory changes. However, evidence on how ESG uncertainty is associated with sectoral volatility remains limited. This study examines the relationship between the U.S. ESG Uncertainty Index (U.S. ESGUI) and the volatility dynamics of the six S&P 500 sectors with the highest historical TRI‐based pollution rankings: Energy, Utilities, Consumer Discretionary, Consumer Staples, Materials, and Industrials. The study employs the GARCH–MIDAS framework, which integrates high‐frequency daily stock returns with the low‐frequency U.S. ESGUI to capture short‐term volatility dynamics and long‐term ESG‐related effects. Forecasting performance is evaluated against GARCH(1,1), EGARCH(1,1), and RV‐GARCH–MIDAS benchmark models. Diebold–Mariano (DM) tests are used to compare predictive performance, and additional crisis‐period out‐of‐sample analyses examine forecasting performance during the COVID‐19 pandemic and the Russia–Ukraine conflict. The results reveal that U.S. ESG uncertainty is significantly associated with long‐run volatility across all six sectors, while short‐run volatility remains highly persistent. Sectoral heterogeneity is evident: Energy, Utilities, Consumer Discretionary, and Materials exhibit negative long‐run associations with U.S. ESG uncertainty, whereas Consumer Staples and Industrials exhibit positive long-run associations. title: Beyond Risk-Adjusted Returns: Tail Risk and Portfolio Implications in Global REITs
abstract: This study compares the performance of major global REIT markets with REITs classified by their geographic operating market and returns measured in the corresponding local currency. The analysis evaluates risk-adjusted performance, dependence structures, downside risk, and portfolio implications using Sharpe, Sortino, Omega, VaR, CVaR, and three portfolio optimization techniques. Results show substantial variation in return distributions and downside risk across markets, while correlations generally increase during the COVID-19 pandemic and the subsequent period. Canadian and Euro-area REITs exhibit comparatively strong risk-adjusted performance, although their tail-risk profiles differ. Portfolio results further show that concentration, volatility, and tail risk do not necessarily produce identical rankings: the most concentrated tangency portfolio generates the highest Sharpe ratio while also exhibiting the most favorable historical VaR and CVaR among the optimized portfolios. The findings demonstrate that global REIT markets remain heterogeneous despite increasing integration and that portfolio evaluation benefits from jointly considering conventional performance, diversification, and tail risk.

title: Transformación digital y su incidencia en el crecimiento económico de las medianas empresas del sector comercial en Machala, durante el período 2020-2025
abstract: This research aimed to analyze, based on the perceptions of business representatives, how digital transformation is related to the economic growth of medium-sized companies in the commercial sector of Machala during the 2020–2025 period. A qualitative approach with a descriptive and interpretive scope was employed, and semi-structured interviews were conducted with representatives of fourteen companies from the sector under study. The inquiry addressed the tools implemented, the organizational areas perceived as most transformed, the main barriers to their adoption, and the economic benefits identified by the participants. The testimonies indicated that the COVID-19 pandemic accelerated the adoption of ERP and CRM systems, e-commerce, social media, electronic invoicing, and inventory control platforms. According to the interviewees, these tools were associated with perceived improvements in sales, logistics, administration, and customer service, mainly due to error reduction, time optimization, operational control, and the expansion of commercial channels. Most participants estimated that the contribution of digitalization accounted for between 30% and 40% of revenue growth. It is concluded that the participants perceived a favorable relationship between digital transformation, productivity, competitiveness, and business sustainability; however, they identified barriers related to costs, resistance to change, and the shortage of digital skills.

title: An Examination of Psychosocial Processes Related to Quality of Life in Pregnancy
abstract: Perinatal anxiety and potential protective processes are often poorly understood compared to other types of perinatal distress. The present study investigated the relationship between perinatal anxiety and quality of life or life satisfaction in a pregnant sample. Psychological flexibility and self-compassion were examined as moderators of these associations. COVID-19 and other external factors were examined on an exploratory basis. Results indicate significant correlations between perinatal anxiety and satisfaction with life, as well as psychological flexibility and perinatal anxiety; proposed interaction effects were not significant. This study may enhance understanding of these processes and contribute to the growing field of reproductive psychology.
journal: Journal of prenatal & perinatal psychology & health

title: Agamben y la pandemia: reflexiones críticas
abstract: Aquest article se centra en l'anàlisi de Giorgio Agamben sobre la crisi causada pel SARS-CoV-2 i té tres objectius. El primer és mostrar els principals conceptes que l'autor utilitza per explicar els efectes econòmics, sanitaris, socials i polítics de la pandèmia, centrant-se especialment en la dimensió eticopolítica. El segon és abordar el problema bioètic generat per la pandèmia des dels conceptes d'Agamben, és a dir, com trobar un equilibri entre la protecció de la salut pública i el respecte a les llibertats individuals. El tercer és fer crítiques a la posició d'Agamben.

title: RELAÇÃO ENTRE A SAZONALIDADE DO RIO AMAZONAS E A PRODUÇÃO DE TRATAMENTOS ODONTOLÓGICOS NO MUNICÍPIO DE PARINTINS-AM: ANÁLISE TEMPORAL DE 2018 A 2025
abstract: A dinâmica fluvial constitui um componente relevante da mobilidade e do acesso aos serviços de saúde em municípios amazônicos. Este estudo teve como objetivo analisar a relação entre a variação mensal do nível do rio Amazonas e a produção de tratamentos odontológicos registrados no Sistema Único de Saúde no município de Parintins-AM, no período de 2018 a 2025. Trata-se de um estudo ecológico, retrospectivo, descritivo e analítico, com abordagem quantitativa e análise de série temporal. Os dados hidrológicos foram obtidos na Agência Nacional de Águas e Saneamento Básico, por meio da estação fluviométrica 16350002 – Parintins, enquanto os dados assistenciais foram extraídos do Sistema de Informações Ambulatoriais do SUS, considerando o subgrupo 0307 – Tratamentos odontológicos. Foram analisadas 96 competências mensais. No período, foram registrados 55.497 tratamentos odontológicos, com média mensal de 578,1 procedimentos. A análise pela correlação de Spearman identificou associação positiva fraca entre a cota média mensal do rio e a produção odontológica no período completo (ρ = 0,218; p = 0,033). Após a exclusão de 2020, a correlação permaneceu significativa (ρ = 0,256; p = 0,019), enquanto, entre 2022 e 2025, apresentou magnitude moderada (ρ = 0,532; p < 0,001). Observou-se ainda importante redução da produção em 2020, compatível com as alterações assistenciais relacionadas à pandemia de COVID-19. Conclui-se que a sazonalidade fluvial apresenta associação com a produção de tratamentos odontológicos em Parintins, embora fatores assistenciais e contextuais também exerçam influência relevante. A incorporação de informações hidrológicas ao planejamento em saúde pode contribuir para estratégias mais adequadas às particularidades territoriais amazônicas.
journal: Revista Ibero-Americana de Humanidades, Ciências e Educação

title: Exploring inclusivity of online formative assessments in vocational training centres
abstract: Vocational training centres (VTCs) in Zimbabwe have embraced blended learning approaches beyond the COVID-19 pandemic. Consequently, formative assessments have been conducted on different e-learning platforms to gauge the students’ preparedness for final examinations and the effectiveness of the online teaching methods being applied by lecturers. Previous research has focused on identifying the e-learning platforms adopted by most universities during the pandemic and on the online learning experiences of students. However, the effectiveness of formative assessment in achieving equity among diverse students has been overlooked. The present research is informed by inclusive pedagogy to assess the inclusivity of formative assessments conducted on different e-learning platforms in the context of gender and rurality. Data was collected from students using semi-structured interviews and focus-group discussions. The results revealed that VTCs in Zimbabwe were not prepared for exclusively online formative assessments. Therefore, the advantages of online formative assessments identified in other studies seem to diminish in value, while disadvantages become more prominent. The dominant aspects that hinder online formative assessment were technical issues, lecturers’ lack of technical skills, and the format of formative assessments being incompatible with online learning. Based on these findings, research implications for universities and researchers are discussed.
journal: Journal of Vocational, Adult and Continuing Education and Training

title: Reflections on Remote Audit Practice in Accounting Firms
abstract: The audit profession has long been advancing the development of informatization and intelligent systems. As an important exploration of the digital transformation of the industry, remote auditing was comprehensively tested during the special period of the COVID-19 pandemic. Accounting firms that operate under explicit business deadlines, facing the enormous impact of the pandemic, made every effort to reduce the disruption to their engagements by using various remote technologies and means. Judged by the implementation results, remote audit technology has substituted only part of on-site auditing and is still constrained by many factors; the submission and disclosure of the 2019 audit reports were delayed to a certain extent. This has also triggered deep reflection within the industry on the application and deployment of digital information technology. On this basis, this paper starts from the audit engagements and the status of technology application of accounting firms during the pandemic, and attempts to provide more insights for the optimization of remote auditing and the digital and intelligent upgrading of the audit profession.
journal: Highlights in Business, Economics and Management

title: Forecasting the Number of Tourist Visits to Semarang City Using the Holt-Winters Multiplicative and Fourier Series Analysis (FSA) Methods
abstract: Forecasting is a crucial process in strategic planning, including in the tourism sector, which is highly influenced by seasonal fluctuations and external factors. In Semarang City, the number of tourist visits has experienced significant changes in recent years, particularly due to the COVID-19 pandemic, which caused a sharp decline in 2020 and 2021. Nevertheless, a post-pandemic upward trend in visits has begun to emerge. To support adaptive, data-driven planning, accurate forecasting methods capable of capturing both trend and seasonal patterns are essential. This study aims to compare the Holt-Winters Multiplicative method and Fourier Series Analysis (FSA) in forecasting tourist visits to Semarang City. The data used consist of monthly tourist visit records from 2017 to 2024, obtained from the Semarang City Office of Culture and Tourism. Forecast accuracy was evaluated using Mean Absolute Error (MAE) and Symmetric Mean Absolute Percentage Error (SMAPE). The results show that the Holt-Winters Multiplicative method produced a lower MAE of 44,498.31 and SMAPE of 6.76%, compared to the Fourier Series Analysis method. Therefore, the Holt-Winters Multiplicative method is considered more accurate in forecasting tourist visits. This study is expected to contribute to more effective tourism management and development strategies at the regional level.

title: Design, uptake, and adaptation of a curated global infant and young child feeding digital health education course to capacitate frontline health workers
abstract: Health workers have critical roles in delivering quality infant and young child feeding (IYCF) services, which include skilled counseling for breastfeeding and complementary feeding. However, health workers’ access to quality IYCF training has been limited. Although IYCF training opportunities are available, most are delivered in conventional learning set-ups, and accessing these trainings can be challenging for many health workers due to restrictions in schedules, inaccessibility of training locations, and inadequate training language proficiency. During the COVID-19 pandemic, the advantages of utilizing e-learning platforms for health worker training have been highlighted, including time, location, and schedule flexibility, increased access for learners, the opportunity for standardized course delivery, and completion monitoring. Recognizing a gap in accessible online guidance and support for IYCF capacity strengthening for health workers, Alive & Thrive and its partners curated available training materials from authoritative health organizations into a practical, competency-based, and self-paced e-learning course. Using the Analysis, Design, Development, Implementation, and Evaluation (ADDIE) model for course development, and with support from a digital solutions service provider and a technical steering committee composed of international experts, available training materials were translated into an e-learning format to create a self-paced course for IYCF. The final product is packaged as the “IYCF E-learning Course: Investing in Child Nutrition” and is available in Arabic, English, and French. A country adaptation of the IYCF e-learning course was also made in Jordan in 2023, through which the course was translated into Arabic. From its launch in June 2019 to January 2021, about 2,000 enrollees from 106 countries accessed the Arabic, English, and French versions of the course package. Positive feedback from users was received on the inclusive nature of the course content and imagery, as well as the breadth of resources available. Meanwhile, the adapted version for Jordan recorded 1,123 enrollees from 33 countries as of June 2024. The course is currently hosted on the UNICEF Agora platform. The development and experience monitoring the uptake of the IYCF E-learning Course has demonstrated the utility of an extensive e-learning course package that can be further adapted to fit specific country-level or local contexts.

title: Upper secondary education policy adjustment, educational disengagement and juvenile justice involvement: an interrupted time-series analysis in Shandong province, China, 2014–2025
abstract: Educational disengagement (ED) in upper-secondary education is theoretically associated with adolescent social integration and delinquency risks. However, whether upper-secondary education policy reforms can reshape ED patterns and whether aggregate educational disengagement is statistically associated with juvenile justice involvement remain insufficiently examined at the macro level. Using annual provincial data from Shandong Province, China, from 2014 to 2025, this study develops a framework linking education policy reform, ED, and juvenile justice involvement. An interrupted time-series (ITS) design was employed to evaluate the immediate and trend effects of the 2020 upper-secondary education policy reform on ED rates, followed by exploratory regression analyses examining the association between ED and juvenile justice involvement. The results show that the reform was significantly associated with an immediate 2.4 percentage-point reduction in ED rates ( β = −2.397, p ≈ 0.050), but no significant long-term declining trend was observed. Further analyses found no statistically significant association between ED and juvenile justice involvement ( p > 0.10), although descriptive temporal patterns suggest a possible time lag. Given the single-province design, the limited number of annual observations, and the overlap of the 2020 reform period with other contemporaneous changes, including the COVID-19 pandemic, the observed reduction in ED cannot be uniquely attributed to the reform.

title: Regime-Dependent Predictability of Cryptocurrency Distress: Nonlinear Evidence from Cross-Exchange Dynamics
abstract: The study of regime-dependent predictability of cryptocurrency market distress is examined in this paper using the dynamics of cross-exchange spread signals as an innovative early-warning tool. The research offers a three-stage econometric framework comprising: a Markov regime-switching VAR to infer endogenous bull, transition, and bear regimes in the BTC, ETH, BNB, and SOL markets; a Panel Smooth Transition Regression (PSTR) model for the regime-dependent spread-distress predictive relationship; and quantile regression providing the complete profile of the distress distribution. The full sample spans January 2020–December 2025 (2191 daily observations); the January 2020–December 2022 sub-period (1095 observations) is used for baseline in-sample estimation, while January 2023–December 2025 is reserved for out-of-sample validation. The results show that cross-exchange spread dynamics contribute to the occurrence of distress regardless of the market state and confirm that bear markets predict distress better than bull markets (with AUROC values changing from 0.848 to 0.963, respectively). In addition, the results of the PSTR function suggest that the predictive role of the spread increases in stressful periods (from 0.152 to 0.588), as supported by LM tests yielding results with p-values less than 0.001. The suggested model outperforms seven competing models, including MS-VAR, GARCH-M, linear logit, LSTM, and XGBoost, on all evaluation measures (AUROC, Brier score, Diebold–Mariano) across every regime. The results remain stable across different exchange-pair configurations and COVID-19-related sub-samples, and when varying the threshold definition.
journal: Journal of Risk and Financial Management

title: Prostitution Enforcement: Evaluating the Impact of Texas H.B. 1540 Using Interrupted Time Series Analysis
abstract: 1540 made a first offense for purchasing sex a state jail felony. We examine Houston Police Department prostitution enforcement using monthly interrupted time-series models of 7,701 arrests from September 2015 through June 2023. The models treat COVID-19 and H.B. 1540 as separate interruptions, assess total, felony, and misdemeanor arrests, adjust for police arrest activity, and compare severity outcomes with simple assault as a nonequivalent control. A secondary analysis links arrests to incident reports and examines buyer- and seller-classified arrests in 6,997 incidents containing one qualifying prostitution arrest. 1540 was followed by an immediate felony increase and misdemeanor decline. No significant post-law level or slope changes emerged for buyer- or seller-classified arrests, and the buyer–seller contrast was nonsignificant. The evidence therefore supports a change in recorded charge severity more strongly than increased buyer-focused enforcement. Actor classifications are incident-inferred, and the follow-up cannot establish verified roles or longer-term effects.

title: O trabalho da gestão escolar no contexto da pandemia
abstract: O debate acerca do trabalho docente e da gestão escolar durante a pandemia é uma temática relevante para a reflexão dos desafios desse novo cenário da educação escolar causado pelo Covid-19. Este trabalho tem por objetivo compreender, a partir do Estado do Conhecimento, as discussões levantadas sobre as implicações da pandemia no trabalho dos gestores escolares para a reorganização das atividades escolares. Esta pesquisa é de natureza qualitativa, configura-se como uma revisão de literatura, organizada de forma descritiva e analítica. Para o desenvolvimento das análises, foi realizada uma busca em repositório selecionado para investigação: Biblioteca Virtual Brasileira de Teses e Dissertações – BDTD. O estudo é de grande pertinência para a reflexão acerca da efetivação das políticas educacionais nas condições de trabalho dos gestores e professores, oportunizando, portanto, elementos para a melhoria da qualidade do ensino em nosso país.

title: Efficiency in Rural Employment Schemes and Unequal Access: A Decadal Analysis of MGNREGA in Rajasthan (2015–2025)
abstract: This study looks at how the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act has been put into practice in 33 districts of Rajasthan, India, from 2015 to 2025. We used various methods, including descriptive statistics, correlation analysis and K-means clustering, to gain insights into how different areas of Rajasthan are performing in terms of employment generation and household coverage. The findings from our analysis show that approximately 7 per cent of district-year observations are exhibiting strong performance, while over half are currently facing significant challenges. There are several important factors that have been playing an important role in uncovering these outcomes, including the density of rural populations, the capabilities of local administrations, the ongoing effects of the COVID-19 pandemic and the unique geographic features of each region. Through the use of clustering techniques, we have been able to assess the performance of each district and highlight areas where there may be opportunities for improvement in the implementation process. Additionally, our analysis suggests consistent regional patterns that may reflect underlying challenges in rural governance and resource allocation, warranting further attention and consideration. Based on our findings, we suggest a tiered policy approach that focuses on providing targeted support where it is needed most, learning from successful models and making overall improvements to the system. We believe these insights can help strengthen rural employment schemes in India and lead to more inclusive and effective policy interventions.
journal: Journal of Land and Rural Studies

title: Diskursive Resonanzen zwischen Säkularen und Religiösen – Pathologisierung, Vergeschlechtlichung, Kolonialisierung
abstract: Der Kontext des Beitrags ist die kritische Forschung zur Säkularität, in der die Binarität von Säkularität und Religiosität infrage und die postsäkulare Betrachtung der Gleichzeitigkeit und Ko-Konstitution in den Vordergrund gestellt werden. Dabei geht es auch darum, dass bei antifeministischen und antigenderistischen Perspektiven nicht Religiosität das Problem darstellt, sondern der Heterosexismus (auch in der weiteren Gesellschaft). In diesem Kontext befasst sich der Beitrag mit der Präsenz säkularistischer Diskurse in qualitativ-empirischer Forschung. Der Fokus liegt dabei darauf, wie diese von drei (feministischen) Teilnehmerinnen eines Projekts zu Erfahrungen während Covid-19 in ihre Erzählung eingewoben werden. Durch Anlehnung an diffraktives Lesen werden hier exemplarisch drei Diskursstränge herausgearbeitet: die Psychopathologisierung nichtnormativer religiöser Erfahrungen, die vermeintliche Rückwärtsgewandtheit alles Religiösen in Bezug auf Geschlecht und Sexualität sowie die kolonialistisch entwickelte Konstruktion eines rückwärtsgewandten Islam. Die Diskurse werden als strukturgebend und wirksam für Erzählpassagen erkannt und stellen somit eine ähnliche Herausforderung für den Umgang mit Machtbeziehungen in qualitativer Forschung dar, wie es sich bereits in anderen Bereichen, wie etwa der Sexualitätsforschung, gezeigt hat.

title: Determinants of Profitability in Indonesian Commercial Banks: Financial Ratios and Macroeconomic Fluctuations
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic significantly affected the profitability and operational performance of Indonesian commercial banks during changing macroeconomic conditions. This study examines the effects of financial ratios and macroeconomic fluctuations on the profitability of KBMI 3 and KBMI 4 commercial banks (excluding Islamic banks) across the pre-pandemic (2018–2019), pandemic (2020–2021), and post-pandemic (2022–2023) periods. A quantitative approach was employed using balanced panel data from 15 banks, analyzed through panel data regression, Data Envelopment Analysis (DEA), and Difference-in-Differences (DiD). The results indicate that BOPO has a significant negative effect on Return on Assets (b = −0.077, p < 0.001), whereas Net Interest Margin (b = 0.164, p < 0.001) and exchange rate fluctuations (b = 0.0008, p = 0.013) have significant positive effects. The regression model achieved an R2 of 0.857 (Adjusted R2 = 0.840), and DEA results indicate an average technical efficiency of 85.5%. DiD analysis further reveals that KBMI 4 banks experienced a larger decline in profitability during the pandemic than KBMI 3 banks. These findings highlight the importance of improving operational efficiency and resilience to enhance banking performance during periods of economic uncertainty
journal: International Journal of Accounting & Finance in Asia Pasific

title: ANÁLISE MULTINÍVEL DA SÍFILIS ADQUIRIDA NO BRASIL: UM ESTUDO HIPOTÉTICO-DEDUTIVO DO MUNICÍPIO DE CASCAVEL EM NÍVEL NACIONAL
abstract: A sífilis adquirida é uma infecção sexualmente transmissível com importante impacto na saúde pública, especialmente por seu potencial de agravamento em estágios avançados e pelas possibilidades de prevenção e tratamento eficazes. Este estudo teve como objetivo analisar dados epidemiológicos relacionados à sífilis adquirida no município de Cascavel (Paraná), comparando-os com os registros da Macrorregional Oeste do Paraná e do Brasil entre os anos de 2019 e 2023. A análise buscou identificar padrões de variação na incidência da doença nas diferentes escalas geográficas e avaliar as possíveis interferências que a pandemia da COVID-19 apresentou sobre os dados da sífilis adquirida nos períodos relatados. Observou-se que os casos de sífilis adquirida apresentaram uma queda entre os anos de 2019 e 2020, aumentando progressivamente e ultrapassando os níveis pré-pandêmicos nos anos de 2021 a 2023. Atribui-se a esse padrão epidemiológico a diminuição do funcionamento do sistema de notificações com consequente subdiagnóstico, a redução real dos casos e os diagnósticos errôneos durante a pandemia entre os anos de 2019 e 2020, o que pode ter levado a um acúmulo de casos nos anos subsequentes.
journal: Revista Ibero-Americana de Humanidades, Ciências e Educação

title: Design and Technical Evaluation of a Standards-Based System That Delivers Enclave-Derived Case-Finding Models to Patients and Clinicians
abstract: BackgroundResearch data enclaves such as the All of Us Research Program do not allow participant-level data, or models fitted to them, to leave, which makes it hard to deliver case-finding models, which flag patients with possibly uncoded conditions for clinician review, to patients and clinicians. ObjectivesWe describe and technically evaluate a system that fits models outside an enclave from released summary counts and delivers them through standard health information technology interfaces. MethodsWe exported dissemination-compliant summary counts from the All of Us Researcher Workbench and, outside the enclave, fitted versioned models for Long COVID, chronic fatigue, fibromyalgia, endometriosis, Lyme disease, lupus, migraine, depression, and anxiety. A model contract (a model file and a written specification), a Python reference implementation, and synthetic Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources (FHIR) test patients define the expected outputs. One JavaScript scorer runs in a patient demonstration, a SMART on FHIR clinician application, and a CDS Hooks service. An atlas displays aggregate results. We evaluated the system on synthetic records with automated tests, cross-implementation output comparison, launches through the public SMART sandbox, and a counterexample review of the scoring and display rules. ResultsThe deployed Long COVID model had an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.67 in a random validation split. The eight self-report models reached 0.61 to 0.82 in identifying self-reporters without a code. The JavaScript scorer reproduced all 162 reference outputs exactly, and all 437 automated tests passed. A counterexample review found 5 classes of failure, including scoring ineligible patients and treating unavailable data as absent, all fixed and added as tests. ConclusionsModels fitted from released summary counts can be delivered through FHIR, SMART on FHIR, and CDS Hooks with reproducible scoring on synthetic records. Real-record interoperability, usability, and prospective clinical performance remain to be evaluated.

A model contract (a model file and a written specification), a Python reference implementation, and synthetic Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources (FHIR) test patients define the expected outputs. One JavaScript scorer runs in a patient demonstration, a SMART on FHIR clinician application, and a CDS Hooks service. An atlas displays aggregate results. We evaluated the system on synthetic records with automated tests, cross-implementation output comparison, launches through the public SMART sandbox, and a counterexample review of the scoring and display rules. ResultsThe deployed Long COVID model had an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.67 in a random validation split. The eight self-report models reached 0.61 to 0.82 in identifying self-reporters without a code. The JavaScript scorer reproduced all 162 reference outputs exactly, and all 437 automated tests passed. A counterexample review found 5 classes of failure, including scoring ineligible patients and treating unavailable data as absent, all fixed and added as tests. ConclusionsModels fitted from released summary counts can be delivered through FHIR, SMART on FHIR, and CDS Hooks with reproducible scoring on synthetic records. Real-record interoperability, usability, and prospective clinical performance remain to be evaluated.
